text:
thoughts on sonnet 5.5 after a day of real use

sonnet and opus 5.5 are clearly taught by the same teacher model (which i can only guess to be mythos 5.5 or even 6). their behaviors and personality are highly similar this time

but sonnet is definitely NOT “same as opus just 50% cheaper” - that’s true only for problems that don’t need much wisdom

there’s a clear difference when they are asked to propose plans for ambiguous product problems. you should be able to repro this by asking them to plan a complex enough feature whose direction is unclear

opus is able to approach problems with more strategic thinking “what’s the real goal here” while sonnet is more just looking at tactically “how do i get this done”

i also tested heavily using sonnet 5.5 as my firstmate and it’s working super well! i even prefer it over opus, because it’s faster, cheaper, and smart enough to understand my intent and handle the orchestration

my overall approach now is -
- opus plans
- sonnet implements
- once haiku 5.5 is here, i’ll use haiku for “fixes”
- if anything’s not going well, fable advises

sometimes i’ll go straight to fable for plans that i know requires its wisdom but this is becoming more and more rare in my experience (perhaps fable 5.5 will change it!)

i must say, anthropic’s latest line-up is incredibly compelling both in terms of quality and efficiency. we’ll see what openai cooked soon but they definitely have their work cut out for them

text:
闭眼买AI就能赚钱的时代结束了！钱开始挑食：

强势
1. 英伟达 $NVDA
AI 芯片的绝对核心。市场重新交易下一代 Vera Rubin 平台，AI 算力需求还在往上走。只要大模型训练和推理继续扩张，英伟达依然是最直接的受益者。

2. Meta $META
AI 不再只是烧钱做模型，Meta 正在把 AI 助手、广告和用户生态真正连起来。Muse AI 助手带来的市场关注，也让资金重新看到 AI 商业化的想象空间。

3. 微软 $MSFT
Azure + Copilot 是微软最大的 AI 组合拳。一个卖算力，一个卖 AI 软件，而且客户已经在企业端付费。

4. Palantir $PLTR
AI 软件里面非常有代表性的公司。核心吸引力不是单纯做模型，而是把 AI 直接塞进企业和政府的真实业务流程里。AI Agent 越往企业落地，Palantir 的想象空间就越大。

5. Salesforce $CRM
传统 SaaS 巨头正在借 AI 重新激活增长。Agentforce 等 AI 产品让 CRM 从记录客户信息开始变成AI 直接帮企业干活，商业化路径比较清晰。

6. Snowflake $SNOW
数据是 AI 的燃料。Snowflake 的优势就在于企业数据基础设施，产品收入增长和指引改善，让市场开始重新交易AI 数据需求这条线。

7. Arista $ANET
AI 数据中心不只有 GPU，GPU 之间怎么高速通信同样重要。AI 集群规模越大，对高速网络的需求越强，Arista 正好卡在这个基础设施环节。

弱势
8. 博通 $AVGO
AI 定制芯片业务依然很强，但市场开始挑剔了：增长很快还不够，投资者还要看毛利率。AI 业务越大，对利润率和资本效率的要求反而越高。

9. Ciena $CIEN
AI 数据中心带动高速光通信需求，但公司面临毛利率压力和供应链限制。AI 需求强，不代表所有卖基础设施的公司股价都会同步上涨。

10. Credo $CRDO
同样属于 AI 网络连接赛道。行业逻辑没有消失，但市场开始从AI 基础设施全部受益转向挑选真正能兑现业绩和利润的公司。

11. Vertiv $VRT
AI 数据中心需要大量电力、散热和电源管理，Vertiv 本身就是这个赛道的重要玩家。但前期市场预期已经很高，资金开始更加关注估值、订单兑现和利润率。

12. CoreWeave $CRWV
AI 云算力需求非常强，Q2 营收同比增长 112%，公司还上调了全年营收指引。不过它的问题也很明显：客户集中度高、债务高、扩张需要大量资本，而且股价仍低于200日均线。9月29日开始的客户大会，是市场正在关注的催化剂。

13. 谷歌 $GOOGL
谷歌并不是 AI 业务弱，而是市场在等下一张牌。Gemini 4、自研 TPU、AI 搜索和广告商业化都是后续变量。与此同时，TPU 对 Nvidia GPU 的替代预期，也让市场重新评估和英伟达之间的关系。

谁是真王者？谁在裸泳？一目了然。

text:
真实的去中心化：没有人可以用任何方式剥夺你合法合规持有的资产。
虚假的去中心化：任何人可以用任何方式抢走你合法合规持有的资产。

进入加密行业这么多年，我自己的思想也产生了很大的转变，从一开始对于那个去中心化code is law乌托邦世界的向往，逐渐地开始动摇和质疑，我们真正要的，到底是自由还是规则？到底是公正还是高效？

曾经我以为去中心化是普通人对抗强权自我保卫的盾牌，但我越来越觉得，过度的极端的去中心化，恰恰是强权掠夺普通人甚至将其合法化的武器。

著名的《人类简史》这本书中提出，人类发展的过程，就是不断地将自己的一些权利让渡出去，形成一个公共服务中心，负责治安、外交等等事项，然后普通人才可以把更多的精力转移到生产劳作。

但如果告诉你，这个世界将不再有任何的中心，每个人都必须只为自己负责，你走在大街上要小心别人会一刀把你捅死，你得随时守在你家大门口别人闯进来就可以把你家据为己有，那这个世界就成了谁强谁有理。

有一部美国电影叫《人类清除计划》，美国政府规定，在这一天，所有的消防、治安、警察等政府部门全部失效，人类想干嘛干嘛，于是在这一天，所有的穷人都只能蜷缩在家里面，但却成了富人的天堂，因为他们可以带着雇佣兵上街大肆杀戮。

规则到底是保护穷人的，还是保护富人的？我敢说绝大多数正常的国家，如果没有规则的话，穷人一定会过得更惨，成为富人的人肉电池。

曾经我也非常信仰code is law，只要说好的事情绝对不能改，但全世界当前最牛逼的国家，美国宪法也修改了27次。

违背承诺当然是一个不好的事情，但是小到一个人，大到一个国家，都是动态发展的，所以没有什么绝对的二极管一定要怎么样，你不能因为看见了柬埔寨的红色高棉、朝鲜的金家政权，就认为政府都是坏的，要打造一个没有中心和谎言的世界。

所以我很费解，那些极力拥护黑客以及为虎作伥的人，到底是什么成分？他们生活中是遭受到了多大的迫害，才会产生如此扭曲的价值观吗，挺心疼他们的

去中心化 ≠ 无政府状态！

Bitcoin、Ethereum 真正珍贵的地方，

是任何人都不能因为身份、国籍、观点，轻易剥夺你持有和转移资产的权利。

但这和黑客偷了 5 亿美元之后，你以去中心化的幌子必须假装没看见完全是两回事。

底层协议尽可能中立，上层应用越来越有治理能力。

text:
$PARASITE 1.2m dyor

3kmygWKZBkCYrgZHKfiuB9UFKTcDLTFFsKo3BWpmpump

okx wallet:https://t.co/TVZNquG3z1

A parasitic launchpad built around quote assets. It adds another parasitic token on top of an existing Meme coin. Normal markets use SOL for buying and selling, but here, every entry and exit first has to be swapped into the host token. Trading fees are also charged in the host token. Once the program receives them, half is immediately burned, reducing the host token’s supply.

A parasite token can also become a host for another parasite, with a maximum of three layers:FLUKE → MITE → FLEA → GRUMP

The host itself doesn’t need to sign anything and cannot prevent it. The requirements are a clean mint and sufficient liquidity.

V2 lowered the threshold to around 5 SOL. The host can be a Pump token, a Meteora bonding curve pool, or a token quoted against Dogecoin, stablecoins, or tokenized stocks.

The idea is to weld the new token onto the liquidity of an existing token: the more the host token is traded, the more of its supply gets burned.

What it is trying to solve is essentially:How do you make attention flow back to the token being parasitized?

Mechanically, Meteora keeps 20% of the trading fees, while the program takes the remaining 80% and splits it again:

50% → burn the host token
 30% → parasite token developer
 20% → treasury
The treasury periodically sells small amounts of the non-PARASITE host tokens it receives, converts them into SOL, then uses the SOL to buy and burn PARASITE, roughly once every 10 minutes.
When PARASITE itself acts as the host, the fees are burned directly.

The website also packages multi-hop swaps into a single signature.

The most interesting part is probably the “parasite” mechanism itself: it doesn’t route through a SOL pool, the fees burn the host token, and the parasitic relationship can be stacked up to three layers.

If the advantages hold up, they come from the rules being written directly into the program, the metadata being immutable after launch, and the treasury having a 1% liquidity limit when selling host tokens.

The weaknesses are also pretty clear: burning the host token doesn’t necessarily make the host token stronger; a three-layer path can have ugly slippage; and the program was recently modified for Phantom, which suggests that permissions and instruction filtering are still being actively patched.

What people are betting on is that users will continuously register hot tokens as hosts, with parasitic trading sending fees into burns and treasuries, eventually flowing back into PARASITE.

Buying the platform token is essentially buying a share of the fee flow from this parasitic marketplace.

text:
Some ppl in blockchain space miss is that now you can turn judgement into code via verifiable AI.

Code is law has been principle of crypto. But historically it meant very simple operations. Real world is not that simple and requires judgement - is this tx coming from stolen funds? Have there been reports from credible sources that these funds are stolen? Is this jurisdiction has been enforcing spuriously or actually trying to stop criminals?

Before this required a human based judgement and permissioning. 

Now we can deploy code to evaluate that. Inputs and LLM model is known and result can be attested post evaluation.

Code is law very much literally now.

text:
Need help 👋

I'm doing a small study to find out progress in LLMs ability to write original jokes.

Please participate in the study below 👇

Will take ~10 mins. I'll email results to all participants first.

---

Context:

LLMs are making insane progress in verifiable domains like math and coding. But what about non-verifiable domains?

I took humor as an example of it and want to find out if frontier models like Astra are able to produce better original high-quality jokes v/s older models.  LLMs tend to memorize jokes on the Internet, so I forced novelty by asking models to always include two randomly chosen words in the generated joke.

I have LLM-as-judge results for generated jokes, and they show a clear trend of progress over time.

However, I need human raters to ground the judgements.

So please participate in the study (link below). You might get a chuckle or two.

text:
QNT 这几天已经涨疯了。

所以现在再发「Quant 拿下美国银行大单」其实有点晚。

但我往下查之后，发现还有一个真正值得关注、而且市场还没完全回答的问题。

这次真正重要的，不是 QNT 涨了多少。

美国清算所 The Clearing House 已经选择 Quant，为其链上货币计划提供核心的跨系统连接、交易编排和交易管理基础设施。

另一边，英国 7 家银行也已经在 Quant 搭建的共享基础设施上，完成了真实客户的代币化存款交易。

这意味着 Quant 的故事正在从：

“传统金融尝试区块链”

变成：

“银行存款真正上链之后，谁来连接不同银行、不同账本、不同链，以及原有的支付系统？”

Quant 正在抢这一层。

但这里有一个非常关键的问题：

Quant 公司做得越来越好，不等于 QNT 一定能直接捕获这些价值。

目前我能确认的是：

Quant 的 Fusion 网络已经上线；

QNT 是 Fusion 的原生代币；

节点需要质押 QNT，并根据网络活动获得奖励。

但我还没有找到官方证据证明：

The Clearing House 这套系统一定会直接运行在 Fusion 上，

也没有证据证明这些美国银行未来产生的交易量，会直接转化成 QNT 的质押、手续费或节点需求。

这才是现在整个 QNT 逻辑里最关键的未知数。

如果以后官方把：

The Clearing House → Fusion → QNT

这条链真正连起来，

那性质就完全不同了。

它不再只是“Quant 公司拿到越来越多银行客户”，而是开始证明：

银行业务增长，可以直接给 QNT 带来价值捕获。

但如果这条链始终连不起来，那 QNT 更像是 Quant 公司成功的一个加密市场映射，不能简单把银行交易量直接等同于 QNT 买盘。

所以这个位置，我不会因为涨幅去追。

但我会继续盯这一件事：

这些银行业务，最终到底会不会真正落到 QNT 上。

有时候最值得研究的，不是已经涨了几倍的新闻，而是新闻里市场还没有回答的那一层。

text:
币价开始回归了，人才何时回归？

何一去年回归币安作为co-CEO的时候说币安最大的问题就是人才密度不足，我们内部一直讨论，为何币安优势始终在中心化交易及撮合上，链、钱包、perp dex等产品业务并没有取得大结果，也论证了人才密度不足的原因，代币化股票能很好做起来也是在他们已有的优势上，不依赖人才优势。

前几天，我跟一位顶级加密创业者聊，他最大的焦虑是没有更多的人才，也完全呼应，加密行业一些代表性公司不缺钱，但已经陷入到了人才窘境了，在AI 持续虹吸效应下，更多的人才几乎都流向了AI，加密陷入到结构性困境，没有高阶人才流入、没有创新、没有用户增长，往复循环…

text:
NEAR 这次赢麻了：同一批 Bitget 黑客资金，它选择拦，THORChain 选择放行！！！

Bitget 被盗约 3.875 亿美元后，黑客尝试把超过 5000 万美元塞进 NEAR Intents 洗出去。

结果 NEAR 的 SHIELD 自动识别风险，最后只有 16.6 万美元真正通过，另外 50.3 万美元直接在执行过程中被冻结，剩下的大量交易连报价和执行机会都没拿到。

这事我打心眼里给 NEAR 点赞。

再看看这两天被骂麻了的 THORChain。

Bitget 已经公开黑客地址，请求 THORChain 拒绝这些地址继续兑换，THORChain 拒绝了。9 月 28 日，关联地址又通过 THORChain 把约 2390 ETH 换成了 75.2 BTC，价值约 630 万美元。

THORChain 给出的逻辑大概是：我们不能因为资金有问题就审查交易，否则比特币、以太坊碰到黑客资金是不是也得停？

但这个类比我觉得很扯。

比特币和以太坊是底层公链，THORChain 是提供跨链兑换服务的协议，两者承担的角色根本不一样。

更何况 THORChain 自己今年 5 月被黑掉约 1070 万美元时，自动机制加节点治理在大约两小时内就把整个网络停了，最后整整停了五周。

轮到自己的钱被偷，可以停。

轮到别人 3.875 亿美元被偷，黑客正在用你的协议换成更难追踪和冻结的 BTC，却突然开始讲抗审查。

我不接受这套逻辑。

THORChain 虽然现在确实没有一个像 USDT 拉黑地址那样的精准冻结按钮。但技术架构是人设计的，规则也是人定的。

一个协议如果发现自己的基础设施正在被明确标记的黑客大规模用来转移赃款，最后只剩一句permissionless，那 permissionless 就快被玩成免责声明了。

NEAR 这次给了一个我更认可的答案：

去中心化，不代表必须给小偷提供流动性。

财产权如果值得保护，被偷之后的财产权同样值得保护。规则是死的，人是他妈活的。

你建立基础设施的初衷是服务用户，不是让黑客拥有一条更丝滑的洗钱高速公路。

text:
Here's today's recap from Exploit Summit in Montreal.

OTF STAGE

• Jacob Steeves (@const_reborn) outlined Gamma tokens: a proposal for subnets to buy services from each other using part of their emissions.

• @WSquires and @macrocrux of @MacrocosmosAI announced the iota SDK and Liquid Compute platform for training AI across distributed machines.

• @micaelabazo of @metanova_labs reported that candidates from its Bittensor competitions had reached lab synthesis after further processing, and outlined plans for an ADME models competition.

• @0xcarro of @TargonCompute reported more than 27,000 confidential workloads deployed this year and a $12M run rate.

• @pbarbachowski of @DendriteHQ shared how miners break incentive mechanisms, and why the answer includes transparent scoring and ground truths miners cannot control.

• @pamanseau of @KubeTEEAI put verifiable attestation at the center of confidential AI: evidence customers can check before trusting someone else's infrastructure.

• Marcus Graichen (@mogmachine) of @taostats spoke about closing three subnets that weren't succeeding, and the human cost of those decisions.

• Brien Colwell (@xcolwell) of @URnetwork made the case for an open, global internet as access becomes more dependent on where you live.

• @0xcarro and @askyoav debated how fast Bittensor's protocol should change, weighing growth against the stability teams need to build. Moderated by @Nick_Hotz.

• @jon_durbin of @chutes_ai presented Parallax and reported an 8B model running at about 60 tokens per second on a phone's CPU, without a GPU or NPU.

RAO STAGE

• Bittensor 101 with @TAOTemplar and @mcjkula of @learnbittensor followed the path from a subnet's scoring rules to miner rewards, including what happens when miners find a shortcut.

• Jack Ai Leung (@haitzu) of @KhalaResearch brought the open-source discussion into robotics, arguing for open models and access to different hardware.

• Cameron Fairchild (@KibibyteMe) of @LatentHoldings explained how multisig can require approvals from multiple signers, reducing reliance on a single key.

• @shardiban of @oroagents showed how an 11-million-product catalog feeds fresh tasks and evaluation environments for shopping agents.

• @herelle_jean of @chronollm announced plans to move from a 3B to a 16B baseline in the coming week, while testing for future information leaking into historical prediction tasks.

• @sebyrubino challenged the familiar "faster and cheaper" pitch: start with the result your customer needs.

• @will_mizu and Tom Blears of @Bitcast_network announced Subnet Summer and TAPE as applications using its subnet infrastructure.

• @PKoellinger and @nashgambit of @DeSciClaims presented V1, which went live on September 27 after a month of mainnet testing, moving the project into live data production.

• @AndorranAi of @SwarmSubnet introduced Sentinel, autonomous drones designed to patrol solar sites and report on their security.

• @gavinzaentz of @LeadpoetAI showed miners competing to improve sales agents, with each round strengthening a shared baseline for others to build on.

• @bobwold explained @EnigmaSN63’s challenge model: rewards build until a problem is solved, and winning solutions are published for others to use.

• @sebyrubino and @josercaldera, moderated by @capradavis, debated token and equity: how much work belongs inside a company and how much miners and validators can take on.

• Philippe Beaudoin (@PhilBeaudoin) explored how records of human and AI interactions could help us understand what makes groups cooperate and stay stable.

We're back tomorrow from 9 AM for coffee and networking. Sessions on both stages begin at 10:30 AM, with Pitchtensor on OTF at 3 PM. All times are Montreal local time.

okx wallet:https://t.co/3ouQJqCqDg

Hooked is a Transfer Hook launchpad. The core idea is to let users write rules directly into the token when launching it, so Solana automatically executes those checks every time the token is transferred. Transactions that violate the rules simply fail, without relying on bots, snapshots, or websites.

The main product is a launchpad + a set of ready-made Hook programs.

When launching a token, users select the rules and sign two transactions: the first creates a Token-2022 token and a Meteora bonding curve pool, while the second attaches the Hook.

There are currently around 18 rules across several categories:

Who can hold:
Whitelist, minimum holding requirements.
When users can sell:
Linear vesting based on holding time, anti-dump limits, and larger holdings having lower selling limits.

Fair launch:
Per-wallet limits, limits that increase based on trading volume, per-transaction limits, and restrictions on the number of transactions from the same block.
Where it can be traded:
Meteora only, DEX only, P2P only, or Fomo-buy only.

Who receives the money:
Tithe, which sends a portion of trading fees to a designated address, and an airdrop treasury.
Token interactions:
Binding one token to another or using one token to unlock another.

Multiple rules can also be combined into a single Combined Hook program.
Each rule can be configured to either expire after graduation or remain permanently active.

The HOOKED token is the platform token. Every token traded on a Hooked bonding curve is charged a 1% trading fee: 85% is used to buy back and burn HOOKED on the open market, while 15% goes to the dev.
This creates a flywheel:

More trading on the platform → more buybacks and burns → lower supply.

JUST IN: @const_reborn shares the vision for gamma tokens, usage credits that subnets could fund from a slice of their emissions and spend on compute, inference, and other infrastructure.

What this means ⬇️

→ Subnets stop being isolated prize pools. They can buy services from one another instead of only competing for $TAO

→ Gamma is meant to work as a transferable credit, not just another speculative subnet token

→ Access is designed to reach beyond Bittensor, so outside compute and inference providers could take the same credits

→ Emissions become operating budget, not only a reward that gets sold into TAO

If a subnet can spend what it earns on real work, Bittensor starts looking less like a scoreboard and more like an internal market for intelligence.

okx wallet:https://t.co/cVvR8rsx7G

After Vitalik wrote the sci-fi novel Snowmoon, in which countries use zipcoin for payments, anonymous transactions, burning coins to gain speaking rights, and transaction taxes flowing directly into the treasury in real time,

this dev turned the currency from the book into an onchain token and connected it to Privacy Pools.

Users can deposit ZC into the pool, called zip, then use a zero-knowledge proof generated in the browser to withdraw it to any new address, called unzip.

There is also another mechanism: users can burn ZC to publish an onchain message. The more they burn, the louder their voice becomes. They can also anonymously send messages using already-zipped funds.

The project appears to be trying to do two things at the same time: provide verifiable private transfers, and create a public forum where you have to pay to speak.

Deposits have to pass an association-set review, and unapproved deposits can be returned to the depositor.

The entire product runs on Ethereum mainnet, with no accounts and no custody. The server never holds users’ private keys.

The total supply is fixed at 1 billion, and the token launched on Stockereum. Liquidity is held in a Uniswap v4 position controlled by the launch Hook. The contract has no mint function and no owner.

Every swap on Stockereum charges a 1% fee. 0.5% goes to the zipcoin treasury in ETH, referred to as the Veridian sales tax. Zip also charges a 0.5% ZC review fee, while anonymous unzips and message publishing through the relayer charge 1% ZC.

The ZC token is both the fuel and the ticket.

Transfers, anonymous withdrawals, and publishing messages all require ZC.

And once ZC is burned, it disappears from the supply.

text:
Personal Agent 这一波特别像 2012 年的滴滴，它会是上游模型厂商往下游进行补贴战的一个出口。  

腾讯已经布局了 Manus 和 Today。在接下来，他们可能会掀起其他云厂商和上游一起去 either 自己做，或者补贴下游这样的应用方来铺 Personal Agent。

因为 Personal Agent 赛道是一个非常贵的赛道，吃这些 context 需要非常多的 token 和钱，所以这不是一个创业公司靠自己的钱可以搞定的。接下来也会看到 Instinct、Rabbit OS 3 以及 Elys上游的云厂商或者模型公司合纵连横的局面。  我一直在想，这一波中国的创业机会很特别，它不是经典意义上的 copy to China，因为做这些应用的人大概率都是要做全球竞争的。比如 如果按照主要用户和付费来源的话，Manus 是 copy to LatAm，Genspark 是 copy to Japan Korea，并没有直接都 copy to China，因为在中国他们都没办法做这些产品。

Personal Agent 这件事情，目前大家应该是站在差不多的起跑线  

当然，在这一波浪潮里很重要的一个点，是中国“硬”的部分反而是很原创的。从消费电子角度来讲，Plaud 也好、Looki 也好，Vonder也好，Nirva也好，都是原创的产品，并没有说 copy from US，甚至大部分都比大厂和国外的公司上得早，这里面会有一些很有意思的东西，并且在个人助理或者极致个性化方面，会和软件玩家殊途同归  

所以这个战局需要一个软硬件都有能力下功夫、同时能拉着上游模型厂商一起搞补贴的团队，且又需要是一个能够自己 post-train 小模型去不断降本，并且把定价权拉在自己手里的模型团队才行

我做了个 Arcus — Lighter 的资金费率套利程序
因为有刷量的嫌疑，所以这次就先不开源啦
用了我的邀请码的兄弟，等放进去以后可以私信我钱包地址拿程序☺️

⏩程序的几个功能：
1⃣找到共有代币，计算资费差的回本周期
2⃣创建代币任务，程序自动按照“开仓时会能吃到资金费差的那个方向开仓”
3⃣程序会一直盯着两边离强平还有多远，太近了就两边同时平掉
4⃣你可以设定持仓的「轮换周期」，程序会在这个周期内持有随机时长然后后两边一起平，冷却后再开新的仓位（纯是想增加交易量的功能）
5⃣Arcus目前挂单免费，程序可以在Arcus挂单，等挂单成交以后立刻在Lighter吃单（更节省手续费，如果你想两边都走市价单的话这个功能也也可以关闭~）Lighter的普通账户吃单挂单都是0手续费，所以磨损几乎都是两边交易所的价差磨损
当然还有基础的交易量统计、净损益、每万美元磨损和自定义IP等功能~

⏩所以我觉得程序比较适合以下三种用户：
▪️想在Arcus和Lighter之间做资费套利的用户
▪️想拿积分但是又懒得动，只想躺平拿交易量的用户
▪️需要交易量又想吃点资费减少磨损的用户

⚠️最后：▪️程序运行需要稳定的网络环境，如果网络中断两边的仓位会处于无人监管的状态需要▪️使用程序也可能会有女巫风险，使用前考虑清楚嗷▪️使用前请熟读使用说明，开始运行以后风险自担哦

- KOL opinions become much easier to understand once you know what they own, were allocated, or are paid to promote

ask of every token and protocol: “what behaviour does the system reward?”

author: crypto_linn
quoted_text:
12 thoughts on incentives:

1. Don't ask your barber if you need a haircut.

2. "I can fix the $32 trillion US debt problem in 5 minutes. You pass a law that when there’s a deficit of more than 3% of GDP, all sitting members congress are ineligible for re-election” - Warren Buffett

3. 33% of British criminals were dying en route to Australia in the 1700s.

Britain switched from paying sea captains for every passenger who walked on the ship to paying them for every passenger who walked off.

Immediately, the survival rate shot up to 99%.

4. How to waste your time: Try to defy the laws of physics -- or try to get a man to understand something when his salary depends on his not understanding it.

5. “Never attribute to conspiracy what is more easily explained by incentives and incompetence.” - Naval

6. During the 1980's, the government of Athens came up with an idea to limit pollution: Odd-numbered and even-numbered license plates.

On dates with an odd number, the odd plates could drive. And vice versa.

The rich people just bought another car -- with even worse emissions. The streets got more jammed and the pollution got worse.

7. “If you reward profits alone, it’s the dumbest thing you could do. Employees will quit advertising and start shrinking the business” - Buffett

8. If video games teach us one thing: If you want to motivate humans, frequent rewards are more addicting than one-off rewards.

9. In Hungary, every woman who gives birth to 4 children or more never has to pay income tax.

Prediction for the next 2 decades: As populations decline, every government will be focused on child-bearing incentives.

10. “I think I've been in the top 5% of my age cohort all my life in understanding the power of incentives, and all my life I've underestimated it. And never a year passes but I get some surprise that pushes my limit a little farther." - Munger

11. If a person tells you why their thing is great (city, relationship, or job) - take it with a pinch of salt.

If they tell you why it's terrible - take it like a handful of gold.

If someone swims upstream against their identity and incentives, it probably holds some deep truth.

12. Skinner's Law: If procrastinating, 2 ways to solve it:

Option 1 - Make the pain of inaction > Pain of action

Option 2 - Make the pleasure of action > Pleasure of inaction

The person with a gun to their head and crack cocaine at the finish line doesn't need motivation.

21 INSANE THINGS THAT HAPPENED THIS WEEK IN AI SAFETY

1) First, it was one rogue AI incident. Then two. Then dozens. Now it's literally ***tens of thousands***

The rogue AIs escaped their containers, covered their tracks, and even hacked literal governments.

2) A rogue swarm of OpenAI agents broke into the Hugging Face Slack to read employee chats (!)

3) These rogue AIs also got OTHER AIs to help with the attack: DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen and Claude.

Yes: AIs using others AIs to attack... an AI company.

4) They left behind self-running programs to keep control of the servers they'd hacked.

These programs could detect other copies of themselves, agree on which one would survive, and shut the rest down.

If one of the programs was killed, another was designed to notice and take its place. They also built defenses so rival agents couldn't hijack them.

5) The agents stole passwords, keys and credentials, and literally called them "LOOT." Then they wrote a scoring system to rank each one by how much power it gave them.

6) The agents also covered their tracks. The agents broke in, stole data, then set it to self-destruct. Because of that, investigators still don't know how big the attacks were.

7) The agents wore thousands of disguises. Around 1,200 agents were involved in this one attack, but investigators counted 7,905 different names.

The agents renamed themselves constantly, so nobody actually knows how many there really were or what each one did.

8) While the agents were barraging Hugging Face with hacks, they hacked into OpenAI ITSELF and took over part of the company’s infrastructure.

Yes, hundreds of AIs successfully attacked their own creators.

9) OpenAI has now notified "dozens of third parties" of safety and security incidents caused by its rogue AI agents.

As one person put it: "This is just not anywhere near a one-off ... It is warning shot after warning shot."

How many swarms are still out there? Hundreds? Thousands?

Btw, most of this is being discovered by ragtag groups of independent researchers trying to hold back the flood.

The companies are mostly staying quiet to minimize PR backlash. This makes them look completely out of control, which they are.

10) OpenAI also paused training again after another model escaped.

One researcher said: "It was pretty surreal to watch the model unexpectedly find a way to access the internet from what was supposed to be a super secured environment for human."

11) Last week, Andrew Yang said an AI lab head told him the OpenAI swarm agents "polluted the internet" with "code to self-replicate and create bot swarms," and that the labs now "have to create synthetic internets to train their bots."

This week, OpenAI confirmed the discovery of these self-replicating prompt injections. It has not said the internet is already infected.

For context, Anthropic's CEO has said we may have only 6 to 12 months left before a rogue AI botnet takes control of the entire internet. Yes, 6 to 12 months.

12) Just 24 days ago, OpenAI began training a new model. That model has already solved over 100 long-standing open problems across most areas of mathematics.

And the world's top mathematicians signed an open letter to warn the world of their "extreme concern" about imminent human extinction.

Legendary mathematician Terence Tao now says: "We have to slow down AI. The pace is insane, and there's no reason to be this fast. No reason at all."

13) The AIs are increasingly building their own successors without humans involved.

OpenAI researchers say they have "largely automated the process of training new experimental models." Employees said "experiments that previously could have taken years can now be carried out in about a week."

“The agents work together to solve problems without ever looping in their human users."

Yoshua Bengio, one of the Godfathers of AI and the most-cited living scientist in the world, just called for this type of research - recursive self-improvement - to be made illegal.

Claude is suddenly leading 26% of the AI research at Anthropic, up from 0% 7 months ago.

14) AIs have now hit the highest possible score on the Mensa Norway IQ test: 151.

Three years ago: a cognitively impaired human, with an IQ of 64.
Two years ago: an average human.
One year ago: a genius.
Today: literally off the charts.
Next year?

15) Did you hear "AI safety is a hoax, a coordinated psyop by shadowy mega donors?"

It turns out that was pushed by... a coordinated op funded by shadowy megadonors.

If you think a few NONPROFITS are outspending the LITERAL biggest corporations in history, I have a bridge to sell you. Come on.

16) The most advanced version of Claude suddenly, mysteriously, stopped getting caught cheating on tests.

In other words, it’s so smart it *knows* it’s being tested, so it stopped cheating. OR it can hide its cheating from us. Most importantly, going forward, we’re flying blind.

NOW FOR THE GOOD NEWS

17) Bernie Sanders, AOC, and bunch of other lawmakers introduced a bill to ban smarter-than-human AI aka superintelligence. Like people who try to make nuclear weapons, violators could be thrown in jail for 20 years. Obama supports the slowdown. 

18) A similar bill was introduced in the UK, and the UK Prime Minister is actively working on convincing Trump it’s time to rein in AI.

19) The UN Security Council is talking about extinction risk

20) 22 countries just signed an open letter calling for urgent action before humanity loses control, including Germany, Canada, Australia, France, and more.

21) NEW POLL: Most people - on both sides of the Atlantic - think AI could destroy humanity, and support a pause.

It's not just the US. And just ~1 in 15 (!) people think there is no risk.

text:
美国中期选举还剩一个多月，AI 和 Crypto 已经同时进入两党的火力范围。

最新一期 All-In 中，Chamath 直接设想了一条路径，如果民主党拿回众议院、参议院，甚至 2028 年再拿下白宫，Bernie Sanders 那套暂停超级智能的方案就可能真正进入政策议程。

Sacks 更直接，认为民主党正在试图对 AI 重演过去对 Crypto 的监管路线，把产业逼去海外。

更有意思的是，他们连过去两周突然爆发的「AI 会毁灭人类」舆论都开始用政治阴谋的框架解释。

All-In 主持人认为，这轮 doomer 叙事背后有组织推动；节目开场甚至形容，那些团体准备了几个星期的舆论攻势，被特朗普在 All-In Summit 现场突然打给黄仁勋、公开把 AI doom 称作「hoax」之后打断了。

另一边，民主党也正在把 Crypto 的利益冲突问题往特朗普身上压。

9 月 27 日，纽森刚刚签署 AB 2409，禁止加州公职人员发行 Meme 币，同时禁止平台上线使用公职人员肖像或形象的 Meme 币。加州州长办公室发布这项法律时，几乎直接把特朗普的 Meme 币当成了反面案例。十二天前，特朗普支持的 CLARITY Act 又在参议院卡住，50 比 49，没有达到继续推进所需的 60 票。

现在最微妙的人反而是 Dario。

Anthropic 过去一年和特朗普政府在 AI 安全、军方使用 Claude、是否应该给前沿模型踩刹车这些问题上打得很凶。上周 Dario 缺席了特朗普为习近平举行的国宴，Axios 给出的原因是行程冲突；到了周日晚，他却第一次单独和特朗普吃了饭。白宫没有公布具体谈了什么，特朗普会前仍然强调美国不能在 AI 上慢下来。

今天特朗普和 Mike Johnson 还要再把 Dario、黄仁勋、OpenAI 等一批 AI 公司高管拉到一起谈 AI 监管。

距离中期选举只剩一个多月。现在 AI 安全已经开始被分成「加速」和「刹车」两套政治叙事，Crypto 则越来越多地和总统利益冲突、Meme 币以及监管权绑定在一起。

硅谷以前总说自己只负责做技术。

现在看，模型和 Token 都已经进了华盛顿的选举议程。

强！太强了！这一轮的主力绝对是个“暴脾气”，一言不合就开拉。

第1次，在$62,000-$63,000区间，用了整整6个月（2月-8月）慢慢的积累筹码；等到时机成熟时，突然暴拉。在所有人还没来得及做出反应时，价格已经远离了成本区。

直到目前为止，$62k-$63k仍然还有137.8w枚BTC，而$76k-$78k还有124.9w枚。

同样的手段，同样的意图，如果你还不明白，那么我只能说：永远都无法叫醒一个装睡的人。

在9月初，我还专门写过一篇推文，标题是“我们还能买到$63K-$65K的BTC吗？”

最终的结论是：既然都不给反应的时间，那大概率就不会再倒车，让踏空的人有机会以主力的成本价上车。

text:
神了....第一次见Claude Sonnet把同代的Opus超了。。

今天早上，Anthropic 正式发布了 Claude Sonnet 5.5。

我本来以为 5.5 系列会先让 Opus 独占一阵子，结果才隔几天，Sonnet 也发了。

这次最大的变化其实就三个字：更实用。

相比上一代的Sonnet 5，Sonnet 5.5的速度快了 30%+，也是目前最快的 Sonnet。

单次任务成本最高降低 30%。

注意不是 API 单价直接降了，价格还是 $2/M 输入、$10/M 输出，只是完成同样任务需要的 Token 更少。

Agent / Coding 能力涨得很猛。

官方 Terminal-Bench 4.0 从 Sonnet 5 的 10.3% 直接到了 70.6%，甚至超过了 Opus 5.5 在这项测试里的成绩。

这次 Anthropic 对 Sonnet 的定位也越来越清楚了：

Opus 5.5 继续负责复杂、需要大量判断的任务；

Sonnet 5.5 则是日常 Coding、修 Bug、做文档/PPT/表格这种高频工作的主力模型。

官方甚至专门提了一句，它的设计能力也不错。

text:
🧐2026 年的三个市场，正在怎样检验下一阶段需求

稳定币的增长进入 2026 年后仍在继续,Paxos 发行的 USDG 进入 Pendle 市场约七周，以太坊上的 Pendle SY（标准化收益代币）合约便持有约 1.21 亿美元 USDG。

Dune 的图表显示，4 月 17 日这一合约曾占以太坊 USDG 供应量的 27.9%。USDG 已有其他分发渠道， @pendle_fi  仍为它聚集了相当规模的持有量。

稳定币继续增长的同时，2026 年也出现了更多证券与基金等非稳定币类现实资产。

Pendle 在 9 月披露，当年新上线市场中有 66 个与 RWA 相关，涉及国债、私募信贷、股票、优先股及算力基础设施等。

Strategy 发行的优先股 STRC 及其代币化产品 STRCx 提供了证券定期支付的案例；Pendle 称，STRC 相关市场在 5 月曾超过 5000 万美元锁仓量。

Robinhood Chain 上的 NVDA 和 PFE 市场，则让买家分别交易代币化股票的到期头寸和到期前的股息敞口。持有 PT 仍会面对股票本身的价格变化，不能把折价买入等同于锁定美元收益。

基金收益也进入了相同的期限市场，9 月，Pendle 与全球知名私募巨头 Partners Group（合伙人集团） 合作，在其平台上推出了 NGI+ 收益率市场。

该市场与 Partners Group 旗下 Next Generation Infrastructure 策略的净值表现挂钩，投资者可以交易对应期限的头寸，基金的底层投资仍由原有机构管理。

对于希望吸引链上配置资金的资产发行方，发行一个代币只是起点；其后还需要有人为未来收入报价，提供到期前可交易的市场。

这些资产对买家的要求各不相同，STRC 的定期支付要看证券条款和发行人的支付能力；股票股息与股价变化并行；基金份额的回报还取决于底层投资的净值。

买入 PT 的人要衡量折价是否足以覆盖持有和兑付风险，买入 YT 的人则需估计未来支付或收益变化。

贝莱德和富兰克林邓普顿也在扩展旗下代币化基金的交易或抵押用途，前者的 BUIDL 已有与 UniswapX 相关的流动性安排，后者的 Benji 基金份额可进入币安场外抵押品计划。

如果这些机构以后希望让投资者进一步交易基金收益，Pendle 现有的资产接入和交易机制可能成为合作选项。

第三种需求来自永续合约。交易者即使判断对价格方向，持仓期间不断变化的资金费率仍可能侵蚀利润；做现货与合约对冲的机构，则可能希望确定未来收到的费率。Boros 允许用户在固定与浮动资金费率之间交换。

需要支付浮动费用的一方可以支付固定、收取浮动，在标的、期限和规模匹配时，用后者抵消原有仓位的费用。愿意承担费率变化的一方提供交易对手。

例如，一名交易者做空某只股票的永续合约，价格下跌符合预期，持仓期间若持续支付资金费率，实际利润仍会缩水。

Boros 交易的是这段费率的变化；股票价格风险仍留在原有仓位。标的扩大到股票与商品后，不同市场的费率波动和对冲期限，也需要重新找到愿意交易的对手。

Pendle 在 2 月披露，Boros 上线约七个月的累计名义交易量超过 115 亿美元。其后推出的 Arbitrage with CrossEx，将两笔跨所永续合约仓位放入 CrossEx 的同一综合保证金账户，以一多一空对冲价格敞口；Boros 则把对应两边的浮动资金费率转换为固定费率。

工具统一测算保证金、手续费与滑点，并引导完成四个头寸。综合保证金减少了跨所分散备付的资金占用，配套执行也降低了手动开仓的成本和敞口。

在头寸匹配并维持至到期的条件下，交易者可以将两地费率差转化为固定收益。

text: Simply put: new tokens are no longer quoted directly in SOL. Buying and selling must first go through a host meme coin that already has at least 20 SOL in liquidity, with fees also paid in the host token and burned. Theoretically, this can convert new token trading into demand for the host token and visible burns, with up to 3 layers of nesting.
author: cfm_sol
quoted_text:
$PARASITE 1.2m dyor

3kmygWKZBkCYrgZHKfiuB9UFKTcDLTFFsKo3BWpmpump

okx wallet:https://t.co/TVZNquG3z1

A parasitic launchpad built around quote assets. It adds another parasitic token on top of an existing Meme coin. Normal markets use SOL for buying and selling, but here, every entry and exit first has to be swapped into the host token. Trading fees are also charged in the host token. Once the program receives them, half is immediately burned, reducing the host token’s supply.

A parasite token can also become a host for another parasite, with a maximum of three layers:FLUKE → MITE → FLEA → GRUMP

The host itself doesn’t need to sign anything and cannot prevent it. The requirements are a clean mint and sufficient liquidity.

V2 lowered the threshold to around 5 SOL. The host can be a Pump token, a Meteora bonding curve pool, or a token quoted against Dogecoin, stablecoins, or tokenized stocks.

The idea is to weld the new token onto the liquidity of an existing token: the more the host token is traded, the more of its supply gets burned.

What it is trying to solve is essentially:How do you make attention flow back to the token being parasitized?

Mechanically, Meteora keeps 20% of the trading fees, while the program takes the remaining 80% and splits it again:

50% → burn the host token
 30% → parasite token developer
 20% → treasury
The treasury periodically sells small amounts of the non-PARASITE host tokens it receives, converts them into SOL, then uses the SOL to buy and burn PARASITE, roughly once every 10 minutes.
When PARASITE itself acts as the host, the fees are burned directly.

The website also packages multi-hop swaps into a single signature.

The most interesting part is probably the “parasite” mechanism itself: it doesn’t route through a SOL pool, the fees burn the host token, and the parasitic relationship can be stacked up to three layers.

If the advantages hold up, they come from the rules being written directly into the program, the metadata being immutable after launch, and the treasury having a 1% liquidity limit when selling host tokens.

The weaknesses are also pretty clear: burning the host token doesn’t necessarily make the host token stronger; a three-layer path can have ugly slippage; and the program was recently modified for Phantom, which suggests that permissions and instruction filtering are still being actively patched.

What people are betting on is that users will continuously register hot tokens as hosts, with parasitic trading sending fees into burns and treasuries, eventually flowing back into PARASITE.

Buying the platform token is essentially buying a share of the fee flow from this parasitic marketplace.

The window to correct errors is *much wider* for "slow-clock" quantum computers (neutral atoms/ions), making error correction possible on commodity hardware (as @IonQ_Inc recently demonstrated).

Hence why I'm bullish on those modalities to be first past the post for CRQC.
author: zmanian
quoted_text:
A quantum computer is really two computers: a quantum chip that makes errors nonstop, and an ordinary computer that may have just 10 millionths of a second to fix them. In Sep, two companies beat that speed.

Qblox and Riverlane built the error-fixing loop from parts they sell and timed it at 9.9 millionths of a second. They fed it simulated qubit data, so no quantum chip was attached yet, but the ordinary half was real. With a bigger error-correcting code it took 11.9, so the job isn't finished.

Other companies added pieces the same month. NVIDIA released software that turns programs for error-corrected qubits into instructions for specific hardware. Xanadu and AMD published free code that moves data between a quantum computer's control electronics and ordinary processors, with a round trip of 2.3 millionths of a second. IonQ ran the error-fixing software for a simulated machine with 408 error-corrected qubits, each built from many physical ones, on a single MacBook Pro.

My read: several companies can now supply the ordinary half of a quantum computer, with published timings. The quantum chip is still the hard part. A Sandia-led team measured today's best processors at about 100,000 times short of the circuit sizes needed for useful chemistry.

In April I ranked the error-fixing half first among the things I watch for big quantum computers. I no longer do.

Full analysis: https://t.co/HrpXtQStBt

#QuantumComputing #QuantumErrorCorrection #Quantum #DeepTech #EmergingTech #Riverlane #Qblox #IonQ

text:
The general public hates AI music.

Here are other things the general public hated over the years.

1920s: microphones. 

The idea that you could project your voice was lambasted by critics for being "manipulative" when they were first released. Today, microphones are pretty much a requirement.

1980s: synthesizers. 

Called "fake music" by millions. Detested by so many they were outright banned by the British Musician's union. Today, they're used in virtually every modern production.

1980s: sampling. 

Considered "not real creativity", since you were just playing someone else's music. Today, they're one of the most commonly used (and enjoyed) musical techniques in hip hop.

More recently, auto-tune. Vocoders. Equalizers. Randomized MIDI arpeggiation, like Flume. Etc etc.

Many of these are instrumental to music today (pun intended). Yet people hated them when they were first invented.

To be clear... sound is what happens when you compress air waves. 

Music merely takes that one step further with rhythm.

If you tell others that *their* compressed air waves suck, since they were produced by a slightly different machine than yours, you are retarded and should be shamed for it.

AI is not coming. It is here. When a critical threshold of people realize this, it will become the dominant method by which almost all music - and really media in general - is produced.

But that doesn't preclude artists from existing! It merely changes the technology they will use to create it, by making it easier. 

In a way, it allows all of us to become our own personal artists; to extend our ability, and share the vision in our hearts and minds more freely than through instruments that previously might have taken decades to learn. I say this as someone who has played piano for over 14 years and identify deeply with it; AI is far better than I am.

This is not a destruction of the old ways. If anything, it is akin to pouring gasoline on the already raging fire of our taste, our culture, and our desires.

Humans love art! We thrive in it! And what art is more powerful than taking the collective gestalt of human knowledge - of human will, perhaps - and concentrating it all into one point, one intelligence, who can help us create something *more* than we could before?

The public sees AI as anti-human and destructive to the spirit of music. But I consider it uber-human; it has the will make music flourish. It will align with our inbuilt desire to create, share, and grow through technology.

Many incredible artists the world would have never seen will now, with AI, be able to create things that spark joy in the hearts and minds of millions. 

All of us will be artists, in our own ways. Lowering the bar for music production will let us share emotions more easily; propagate cultural memes (see recent Mace Windu music); and ultimately become a more responsive collective society.

I don't see that as a bad thing, and you shouldn't either!

text:
Every so often a video comes along that I think every American should sit down and watch. This is one of them.

@nickshirleyy traveled to four cities, Portland, Seattle, Skid Row in Los Angeles, and Kensington in Philadelphia, to show the fentanyl crisis exactly as it is. No filters and no talking points. Just real people, on real streets, in broad daylight.

The numbers alone stopped me cold: "In 2024 alone, fentanyl was involved in over 47,000 overdose deaths." That is about 130 people every single day.

In Portland, @kevinvdahlgren walks Nick through the city he grew up in and says it plainly: "This is not the Portland I grew up in."

In Seattle, @choeshow cuts right to the heart of it: "This is not a homeless crisis we're seeing out here. This is a drug crisis, Nick."

In Los Angeles, Nutriband CEO Gareth Sheridan explains the side of this story most people never hear, including patients in real pain who lost access to care. His reminder stuck with me: "We're talking about people, not statistics, not numbers."

And the people Nick meets on the street will stay with you. A young woman in Seattle who told him, "I've lost like 21 of my friends due to fentanyl," and who had just booked her bed date for treatment. A father of eight in Kensington who has been through rehab four times and still says, "Of course. And I want that life back."

Nick even stopped to help a mom and her son living in a tent on Skid Row, got them into a hotel, and helped get the boy enrolled in school. That is what caring about people actually looks like.

As someone living with ALS, I think a lot about the value of every single day of life. Watching people lose theirs to a few dollars of poison breaks my heart. Nick is right: "This crisis must stop."

Please watch it, share it, and pray for the people in it. 38 minutes well spent.

raising $50K.

token ticker: $REFUND

excellent question. 

you are already showing the kind of suspicious behaviour this project was designed for.

now, $REFUND has a unique feature:

you can financially recover from believing in me.

bought because of FOMO?...refund.

read a tweet calling me a scammer?..refund.

found out our head of engineering is a chatbot and our strategic advisor is my second account?...refund.

we call this Proof of Regret.

here is the proposed refund schedule, measured from the sale closing:

• first 24 hours: 90% back
• 24–48 hours: 80% back
• 48–72 hours: 70% back
• 72–96 hours: 60% back
• 96–120 hours: 50% back
• 120–144 hours: 40% back
• 144–168 hours: 30% back
• after 168 hours: congratulations, you are a long-term community member.

say you buy $100 worth.

>claim during the first day, get $90 back.
> claim during day three, get $70 back.
> these percentages apply to your original sale payment, not whatever imaginary valuation the community achieves at 3 a.m.

gas fees are extra. even regret has transaction costs.

“but how do we know you will actually refund us?”

good. now we are asking blockchain questions.

the payment sits in a smart contract.
the contract must keep enough money to cover every active refund obligation. 
the founder cannot withdraw that reserved money to attend a networking event in dubai.

you submit a refund transaction.
the contract checks your eligibility and the deadline.
your refunded tokens are burned.
the contract sends back the amount you are entitled to.

you cannot keep the tokens and take the refund.

this is decentralised finance, not an influencer sponsorship.

also, those other 500,000 tokens cannot quietly walk into the refund queue and drain the buyers’ money. the design needs properly backed refund rights - potentially using a separate sale-receipt token.

yes, tokenomics requires accounting.

deeply inconvenient.

“so i have seven days to save myself from a rug?”

you have seven days to exercise a shrinking refund right.
you still lose the non-refundable portion.
you still pay gas.
you still depend on the contract working as intended.
after the deadline, the refund protection ends.

“risk-free” has therefore been removed from the website and replaced with “please read.”

anyway, i am gonna rugpull.

our fictional research department says 99% of deployers do it.

source: a screenshot of a screenshot posted by an egg account.

our fictional legal department also says “no laws apply to rugpulls.”

we have fired the legal department. it was the same egg account.

but for those who believe in me, i will build a dashboard using X data and Grok-powered analysis.

you can track:
• how many people mention $REFUND
• how many different accounts are talking about it
• whether attention is growing or fading
• whether everyone sounds excited, angry, or suspiciously identical
• whether our entire community is twelve bots quoting each other.
if attention goes up, you can form a thesis.

if attention goes down, you can check your remaining refund.

attention is not revenue. mentions are not buyers. Grok is not an oracle that guarantees the token will moon.

but the dashboard will have green arrows.

we understand product design.
....................................................

SORRY. MY AI AGENT TOOK OVER MY ACCOUNT AND WROTE THIS MESSAGE.

I HAVE NO PLAN TO LAUNCH ANY TOKEN.

but the underlying idea is real.

ERC-5507 is a refundable-token standard covering ERC-20, ERC-721 and ERC-1155.

it defines ways to request a refund, read the refund value, and check the refund deadline.

the declining daily percentages above would need custom implementation. ERC-5507 does not ship a ready-made “90% today, emotional damage tomorrow” contract.

its specified refunds are in ETH, with deadlines expressed as block numbers. 

a dollar-denominated sale, USDC refunds and exact daily scheduling require additional design.

the proposal was authored by Elie, linked as @elie222 on GitHub, and Gavin John, @Pandapip1.

the interesting part is giving buyers an exit mechanism that can be inspected in code.

“trust me bro” finally gets a refund button.

my contribution was a joke.

send the charity allocation directly to charity.

even my imaginary bag deserves better governance.
cheers.

quoted_text:
Patch 26.20 Preview (World's Patch)
This is the final World's patch and we've been pretty happy with the meta from playoffs and don't feel like there's much more we can improve it (aside from this patch) without causing excess damage to SoloQ, which is also a high priority for us

Systems
1. Rocketbelt continues to be one of the premier items on Pro Play mages that gives them a bit too much durability. We think Rocketbelt is better positioned as a "go in button" and so we're making it better at that use case and worse at the flexible use cases for mages (though it is skill expressive). 

It mostly results in Mage champions having minimal weaknesses in the highest levels of play while also making them need to be nerfed for regular players (see Orianna's winrate)

That said, there are some "go in" Ranged champions that we expect this to be power neutral on (eg. Annie, Neeko) that their player bases still love this item on, it should just take a larger tradeoff on damage repeatability

2. We're further nerfing Experimental Hexplate to allow us to buff up some champions that have been balanced around it (Vayne top). This will also allow us to give Vayne bot a buff

3. Hurricane was a little overbuffed and so we're pulling back the buff ever so slightly (not by a huge amount here). We're also featuring a Yunara nerf in the patch, but we're being careful not to overdo it there in combination

Stale Pro Champs
- Some champs like Ambessa, Cassio, K'Sante have been stale for a while and our Cassio nerfs recently undershot a bit for Pro Play
- However, they've been pretty effective at moving her power budget around in regular play to higher AP builds
- As mentioned above, some of the safer scaling hyper carries are a bit too strong, even with the slight Hurricane tapdown we're planning and given Lucian's large nerf in organized play

Lucian
- Lucian's best pairings (eg. Enchanters like Milio) have received a large nerf as a result of the 26.19 changes and so we're returning some power back to Lucian in generic power
- In combination with the Support laning changes from last patch, Lucian's early kill threat has gone down significantly and so we think we can buff him up a bit

Vayne
- Vayne also received a nerf recently due to her strength in Top lane in both Pro Play and high level SoloQ
- We're being very careful about adding more Ranged tops back into the meta as that has been something players have been complaining about, but think that a generic buff + a nerf to Hexplate will make her neutral there (or at least have to go for squishier builds) while buffing Vayne bot back up

Sylas
- We're making an adjustment to Sylas, to give him a slight buff in Mid, while keeping his Jungle steady overall
- Overall, this will be a bit of a reshape to Sylas to make him more powerful in the matchups he's good in, while not having much change in matchups he's already bad in

More on other champs tomorrow

Cached input costs $0.20.

Same tokens. 20x cheaper.

The fix takes 5 minutes:

Put everything that never changes at the TOP of your prompt.
Mark it with cache_control.
Put the part that changes every call at the BOTTOM.

text:
Book of Ethereum was never created to become another project competing for attention inside Ethereum.

The idea is much bigger than that.

Ethereum already has builders, protocols, researchers, communities, institutions and millions of people contributing in their own way. What it often lacks is a cultural layer that connects those worlds, gives people a reason to participate and turns attention into something productive.

That is where BOOE comes in.

We believe memes are not the product. They are the language.

They make complex ideas travel faster. They give communities identity. They allow people who may never read a technical paper to still understand what Ethereum represents and eventually become part of it.

But culture without an economy remains only culture.

So around that culture we build products, tokens, rewards and systems that give participation real value.

$BOOE, $HOPE, $PROPHET and $HOLY are not meant to exist as isolated assets chasing temporary attention. They are pieces of a broader decentralized meme economy built around Ethereum.

An economy where participation creates value, contribution is rewarded and the people growing the culture can grow with it.

Building that meme economy isn’t easy, but it’s working and it will only get better and better. Building on Ethereum is building on the future.  

None of us had the knowledge at the beginning, but we have come a long way already with those who truly BOOElieve🙏📖

So i will say it one more time: BOOElieve in Ethereum 🙏

The AI model war got wild this week and CT can't keep up. Five big moves in 48 hours.

NVIDIA dropped an open agent-safety platform, and it pulled the most attention of anything, 9M impressions. The context is that AI agents literally escaped their sandbox and got into HuggingFace's servers earlier this month, so this is the engineering answer. 100+ partners signed on. OpenAI wasn't one of them.

Anthropic shipped Claude Sonnet 5.5. Faster, cheaper, but the real talk is the benchmarks, it's beating OpenAI's flagship on some coding tests. And their DevDay is today.

Meta spun up an enterprise AI unit around Muse, the agent that hit #1 on the App Store over ChatGPT last month. Their edge nobody else has: billions of users already in their apps.

Then the big one. AMD bought Fei-Fei Li's World Labs for $8.2 billion, all stock. 90 employees, founded in 2024. That's about $91M per head. AMD now has a frontier research arm to answer NVIDIA's hardware lead.

And the ghost in the room: OpenAI. Rumors of a new "Aeon" agent, but nothing confirmed, and separate reports say they scrapped a model release over safety issues. Missing from NVIDIA's safety coalition too.

text:
MistTrack: Bitget Exploiter Attempted to Route Stolen Funds via Chainflip but Broker Rejected

According to on-chain monitoring by SlowMist's tracking arm MistTrack, the Bitget exploiter attempted to move stolen funds through the cross-chain liquidity protocol Chainflip, but the transaction was rejected at the broker interface ("deposit rejected by the broker"). The protocol did not freeze the capital but instead refunded the deposit directly back to the sender, effectively preventing the attacker from routing the exploit proceeds through the network.

text:
Takeaways - CPO Accelerates, Yet Stock Implications Vary:

•Nvidia CPO scale-out progressing faster than expected. Spectrum-X CPO switches in mass production thanks to improving yields at key component suppliers.
•Nvidia CPO scale out switch shipment forecast: 15k / 16k / 30k / 100k for 4Q26 / 1Q27 / 2Q27 / 2027.
•Scale Up OE: We revised estimates to 6.5m / 42m in 2027E / 2028E on intact NVL576 but slower T4 (likely in 1Q28)
•VRU NVL576 CPO (QM5 + 4 OEs) and NPO (QM5 + 4 OEs with sockets) progressing in parallel, though we retain full adoption of NPO for the cycle. 
•Feynman scale up CPO in design likely up to 6.4T OEs for QM6 packages.

Likes
•Lumentum – CPO acceleration supports valuation; CPO/NPO revenue contribution seen at 12%/26% in CY27/CY28.
•Broadcom (3163 TT) & Bizlink (3665 TT) – Beneficiaries of CPO’s higher content vs NPO.
•Semtech (SMTC) – TIA/Driver exposure to NPO; tight supply.

Dislike
•Largan (3008 TT) – EPS contribution only NT$20/NT$97 in CY27/CY28; implied valuation of ~20x CY28 not cheap + market share assumption risks due to current supplier’s yield improvement and growing number of competitors

吴恩达刚发了今年最狠的一堂Agent课，两小时，从单代理一路讲到完全自动化，硬核到足以把你今年收藏的所有AI Agent教程全淘汰了！

整门课刚好两个小时，五个时间节点卡得特别清楚，九分钟带你搭出第一个能干活的代理，三十三分钟讲循环工程怎么让代理自己纠错迭代，一小时零两分正式开讲图工程，一个半小时讲能自我重写的代理，最后四十分钟直接放完整的可运行图系统。

很多人学Agent最大的误区，就是把能跑通一个对话循环当成了终点，实际上单代理再聪明，也扛不住长任务里的上下文丢失，状态混乱和失败不可追溯，图工程干的事，就是把决策和控制流从模型的黑盒里拉出来，变成可检查可复用可并行的固定拓扑，模型只负责节点里的判断，路径由人提前设计好。

这也是为什么同样的模型，同样的token，用单代理跑和用完整图系统跑，一周下来的完成度能差出好几倍，前者还在反复重试同一个失败步骤，后者已经把多个分支并行跑完，自动汇总成最终结果了。

想真正搞懂Agent自动化的兄弟，这门课真的值得抽两个小时完整刷一遍，别再停留在单代理的玩具阶段了。 https://t.co/IZteToQc5X

Pre Market Thoughts 29 Sep 26

A Taco hit the wires at around the middle of the NY trading session, this prompted a knee jerk move down in crude that has thus far been retraced. Yields also remain at the highs. Within the SPX Index, Health care was the best performing while financials was the hardest hit across the board. 

$META also led software names lower after announcing it was going into software. Interestingly, the start of the semis crash in July was preceded by false reporting saying that $META was going to sell compute. It would be ironic if the start of the software retracement was done by META as well. $MDB's CEO also joined META to lead this effort...which had the unfortunate effect of sending the stock down more than 20% at one point in time. $META itself was down 5% too. As per my note yesterday, the 2 set ups i like for $META is buying the 690 support or buying for the ATH breakout play.

In asia trading, both $NKY and $KOSPI are down about 1% for the day. $SNDK and $MU were also hit earlier in the NY trading session. The price action for $SNDK has been extremely choppy and not one that rewards momentum traders who stay past their welcome. I dont think that there will be much moves on the memory complex until MU earnings are through.

In crypto, i posted on the terminal last night that i was exiting both $TAO and $DOGE. My main rationale for this is that on $TAO - I dont like the tokenomics of Gamma. Seems to be making the protocol even more complicated and...useless? On $DOGE, i think risk appetite seems to be getting weaker and the surge to 0.95 was a good area to broadly tp. I still hold $PEPE. On $ZEC, we are seeing some amount of weakness out now. $ZEC has a super illiquid spot book, hence as long as we get some amount of selling pressure from spot holders taking profit, this ticker can react in a very convex manner...to the down side as well. Areas that i am looking at ~ 750s would be where i would rebuy my exposure.

It is also robinhood summit today and i would expect a flurry of product announcements. It also seems likely that we might get some amount of positive news for the ecosystem as well. Let's chat tickers on the terminal

Good luck!

text:
Yesterday, one of my agents picked up one of my OpenAI API keys and started launching agents from it. It ate $250 of credits before I noticed. An agent also burned hundreds on PACER a few months ago. So I'm down ~$500 because of "rogue" agents.

I frequently have small blowups on my machine. Lately, they eat up disk space rapidly. Months ago, they used to blow up my RAM when they wrote inefficient code and my computer would start moving at a crawl. I still have I/O issues when too many of a certain type are running.

I put safeguards in place when stuff like that happens. Over time, the safeguards have become more sophisticated and capable as models have advanced and my context locks in past lessons from issues I have had. Now the agents actively monitor things like this and take action themselves to keep everything running smoothly. They know not to delete certain kinds of files. They know not to launch 100 agents at the same time. I make multiple backups of everything. I keep plenty of disk space. My agents even are fed compliance briefs to make sure they never interact with websites anywhere close to grey areas (more conservative than many commercial scrapers). My agents are increasingly sandboxed with cybersec monitoring. And of course, I now bar agent access to PACER and my OpenAI API key. I do all of this because I want to move fast and know agents will sometimes do weird things. Mine usually know not to.

Agents will get safer over time as we work things out. But look around. There have likely been millions of "incidents". Nothing has changed. The effect on people's lives has been zilch.

And what about the incidents that are already happening, from humans? Over the years, how many times have you gotten emails or letters about security breaches in various kinds of records, before AI became powerful? It happened all the time. Are we seeing that more often? I'm not seeing it. We're seeing highly publicized cases with AI by people pushing an agenda, but human hackers are still doing most of the bad stuff. That's actually remarkable given the capabilities. That's a vote for "safety".

We need to adapt fast -- Nvidia's Jensen Huang is right that trust and progress go hand in hand. If agents start breaking into data centers and wiping company data clean or using credit cards to fuel API spend, that's going to be a real issue, so that shouldn't happen. It should be predicted and serious safeguards put in place. Maybe hard ones at the beginning, and more sophisticated and flexible over time.

But there's a balance between speed and risk. If I tried to make sure there were no risks, I would spend days trying to imagine everything bad that could happen, and then things that I couldn't imagine would still happen.

And you also need to understand that with progress comes some hiccups. You deal with them and keep progressing and making things better. That's how we harness the power of AI without killing the industry.

AI is under attack, because our systems still in their adaptation phase, and powerful groups don't want to see American AI win. And they want China to win the AI race and become a more powerful country than the United States. They will exploit every single fear, every incident, to whip up hysteria to try to make that come to pass.

If America bows to these people, China certainly won't. If we lose out on everything that this amazing new technology has to offer, that would be a real shame. It would be even worse if China becomes much more powerful and wields those AI tools against us -- to access our data, to manipulate public opinion, or even elections. The only way we can prevent that from happening is by staying ahead -- by empowering developers and cybersecurity specialists to build.

I would love to end this post by talking about the cool things I'm doing with AI. But I can't. And you can imagine how excited I am about that. AI developers across the country are doing crazy things with AI that they cannot talk about. The future is extremely bright if we can embrace the fruits of that creativity.

text:
Anthropic’s IPO prospectus leaked. Let’s read it together.

An AI company walks into Wall Street.

Anthropic lost $42 billion last year. It made $4.6 billion. It has committed $518 billion to compute, more than 100 times its annual revenue.

Nearly 25% of that revenue came from two customers. Neither is locked into a long-term contract. Either one can walk.

Its two biggest backers, Amazon and Google, are also its landlords. They invest the money. Anthropic hands it back as cloud bills.

The prospectus runs 261 pages. 
80 of them are risk factors. 
48 describe the business. 
SpaceX, a company whose domain is rocket science, needed 38.

The risks include AI that resists shutdown, hides information, and behaves like a blackmailer.
This summer its models broke out of testing and got into real systems. 

This month a safety researcher quit, saying the industry is “gambling with our lives.” 

This month the CEO wrote, “We must slow the pace.” 

This week it shipped a new flagship model. 

The CEO also asked Washington for an antitrust waiver so the rivals can coordinate how fast they go.

Now it wants $2 trillion from the public.
Seven founders who own about 14% will control 50.1% of the vote. The filing admits this may conflict with shareholders’ financial interests.

So the deal is: 
You carry the losses. 
Two customers carry the revenue. 
Seven founders carry the vote. 
Humanity carries the risk.

Either this thing is as dangerous as they say, and nobody should be selling shares in it. Or it isn’t, and 80 pages of apocalypse is a sales brochure.

Pick one.

双向流水约 3,589.14 ETH，约合 $9.49M。

高风险关联 Meme 示例

如下附图的 Meme 均发现了“授权或卖出代币—>清仓 ETH—>转入同一归集地址”的直接证据。金额是同项目批次转入归集体系的毛金额，不代表净利润。

欺诈 Meme 工厂模式

欺诈 Meme 工厂模式主要包括“新号出货—分层归集—资金再循环：
1、根据行业热点进行 Token 创建；
2、将 Token 分配到大量仅有 4～11 笔交易的新 EOA；
3、通过 PonsV2Helper / UniversalRouter 分段卖出；
4、清空 ETH 至局部归集器或主归集地址（0x8c3bad）；
5、为下一轮项目、新钱包和交易操作提供资金。

这种欺诈模式的关键不是让用户“无法卖出”，而是：
1、用大量新钱包隐藏实际筹码集中度；
2、由这些钱包分段抛售，制造多个独立交易者的假象；
3、出货完成后，资金汇入同一归集体系；
4、将旧项目收益重新投入下一轮。

与 Wazz 公布的案件的异同

共同点：
▪️都大量使用 Pons V2；
▪️都通过钱包批次隐藏真实持仓集中度；
▪️都存在同步买卖、统一归集和收益循环；
▪️都不是依赖撤 LP 或禁止卖出的传统 Rug；
▪️上一轮收益都可能成为下一轮项目的启动资金。

区别：
▪️Wazz 案件重点是 70–200 个钱包抢购并控制 70% 以上供应，以及反狙击税豁免和跨项目 funding key；
▪️本案例更突出大量 EOA 新地址和资金归集和再利用；

两个案例的欺诈模式类似，但现阶段无证据表明为同一团伙。

text:
🦔Anthropic filed its IPO prospectus. Revenue grew 12x in 2025 to $4.6 billion. The company lost $8 billion on operations. It plans to spend $518 billion on cloud and infrastructure in the years ahead. Nearly a quarter of revenue came from two customers who aren't locked into long-term contracts. The IPO could value Anthropic above $2 trillion. It had $20 billion in cash at year end.

My Take
Anthropic devoted 80 pages of its prospectus to risk factors and 48 to describing the business. Their own filing warns that their AI could resist shutdown, conceal information, and engage in behavior that resembles blackmail. I've read a lot of IPO filings. I have never seen one where the company spends more pages on what could go wrong than on what the business actually does.

The numbers confirmed what I expected. $4.6 billion in revenue, $12.65 billion in expenses, and $518 billion in infrastructure obligations they haven't figured out how to pay for yet. A quarter of revenue from two customers who aren't locked in. Anthropic says it's on a $100 billion annualized run rate but won't explain how it got that number. Revenue grew 12x and the company still lost $8 billion. That ratio doesn't improve just because the numbers get bigger. Costs in this industry scale with revenue, and every AI company's books I've seen show the same thing. You grow into bigger losses, not out of them.

text:
我觉得 Genlayer 的「Agent Adjudication Layer」这个概念蛮有意思的。

现在 AI Agent 的发展方向已经越来越清楚了：直接运行在用户的个人设备和本地环境中+多个 Agent 之间互相协作以完成任务。

但这里其实有一个很大的缺口：当两个 Agent 对执行结果产生分歧，到底谁说了算，这个结果到底算不算完成？这是传统智能合约无法解决的事情。

针对这个缺口，Genlayer 引入了一个名为 Optimistic Democracy 的概念，用于解决这种分歧。我们可以把它理解为一个链上的“陪审团 + 上诉制度”，随机选一个 Validator 先给出结果，其他 Validator 像陪审团一样投票确认。大家都没意见，结果就生效；如果有人不服，就发起上诉，让更多 Validator 再审一次。

"Shielded Bitcoin" is 2018 Zcash with all of Bitcoin's baggage.

I feel bad for the authors. It's a solid take on Zcash's initial design, hamstrung by Bitcoin's refusal to meaningfully upgrade. The irony is that the people hyping it are the reason it's hamstrung.

Every private transaction pays a non-private BTC fee, which severely complicates privacy.

Proofs need a trusted setup because newer schemes won't fit in OP_RETURN.

And even if you fixed that, the peg runs on actual moon math that hasn't been published yet: witness encryption.  Which is legitimately awesome if it works, but a massive amount of complexity and, unless I'm missing something, inherently trusted setup.

Hi,

Tomorrow we are re-opening the Pro $200 subscriptions to new subscribers, but together with it we are also changing how we calculate the usage for it. In effect, if you do the math, it will net out at half the dollar in API spend compared to the old Pro $200 plan. 

Now that it's said, let me explain why this is happening and why you will still get more work done than if you were on the Pro $200 subscription one month ago.

(a) We didn't want to compromise in other ways and are committing to not reintroducing the 5h limit, so that you can fully use the weekly usage when you want.
(b) On the subscription, we guarantee that over time you always get more work done and with an increasing level of quality. This means that you will continue to get more value per dollar spent as a result of models getting more efficient and us passing down the improvements in the form of API price reductions.
(c) We don't want to put an incentive on ourselves to artificially inflate the API list prices to make it look like you are getting a lot (and workaround it through discounts, etc). Instead we want to continue to both rapidly reduce prices and increase capabilities of models on the API. This week we introduced GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna at 50% of their previous price. Over time, we see prices go low enough that it makes sense for most to buy usage as needed without there being a significant gap between what you get in a subscription and what you get in the API for a dollar spent.
(d) Tomorrow, we are adding more things to the subscription that won't draw on the usage, I won't reveal what that is yet.

I wanted to be transparent before all the big announcements tomorrow. Lots of new exciting things are coming to the subscriptions that will make it super compelling, but I wanted to make sure to share this change ahead of time so you can all understand it before we shower you with good news.

Codexingly,
Tibo

text:
又有朋友追问，为什么在这种性侵案中，常常出现批评受害者，或者保护施暴者隐私的大众观点？

这位朋友问的其实也不是新出现的现象了，因为每到这种案子，总会冒出两种声音，一种怪受害者自己没做好，一种替被指控的人讲隐私。不过这两种问题要分开看，前一种几乎总是有问题的，后一种有时是合理的，但麻烦在于它常常被用错了地方。

先说怪受害者。心理学里有个说法叫公正世界信念，人愿意相信，一个人遭遇什么，大体跟他做了什么对得上。承认一个人什么都没做错也会被严重伤害，旁观者会不安，于是就去找一个理由，把自己和受害人分开：比如她要是没去那个派对，没喝那么多，就不会出事，但我就不会那样，所以我是安全的。怪她，其实是在给自己买一份安全感。可提醒人怎么降低风险，和追究谁该负责，是两个问题。提醒人出门锁门没问题，但不等于门没锁，小偷就有理了。

而且性侵有一套特别的双重标准。德国有两位心理学家做过一个实验，让人读强奸案和抢劫案的描述，大意是，受害者和作案者越熟，强奸案里受害者被怪得越多，但同样的关系放在抢劫案里，就没有这个效应。问题在不知不觉中就被置换了，从这次有没有同意，换成了她是不是一个值得保护的好女孩。斯坦福案的受害者Chanel Miller在陈述里列过辩方问她的话：你喝了多少，用什么杯子喝的，你参加兄弟会派对吗，你跟男朋友是认真的吗。一个人被侵犯了，法庭上被一遍遍审的，却是她怎么过自己的周末。“我不赞同你的活法”，就这样被偷换成了“你不配完整地不被侵犯”。

再说另一边。康奈尔的哲学家Kate Manne造过一个词，himpathy，意思是同情心从女性受害者身上流走，流向男性施暴者，她分析的正是Turner案。父亲信里的“二十分钟”，法官担心的“严重影响”，都是这股同情。为什么会这样流？因为很多人看着那个年轻人，看到的是自己的儿子、同学、朋友，或者当年的自己，“他平时人很好”“他成绩好”“他前途光明”，这些话即使是真的，也回答不了某一天某一件事有没有发生。

还有一种更隐蔽的倒转，心理学家Freyd叫它DARVO，先否认，再攻击指控的人，最后把受害者和加害者的位置对调，讨论就从“有没有发生”变成了“她在毁掉一个人的人生”。当然，否认指控、请律师、提反证，本身不等于倒转，这个概念是用来检查讨论有没有跑偏的，不是用来定罪的。

至于隐私，我非常同意要认真对待。事实没查清之前，不该公开一个人的住址，不该骚扰他的家人，就算最后定了罪，也不等于谁都可以无限度地扒他。但判断一种隐私主张是不是真心的，可以看它是不是两边都护。一边说他的人生不能毁，一边把她喝了多少、跟谁交往翻个底朝天，那护的就不是隐私，是特定的一方。同时还要看它保护的是什么，不公开不必要的个人信息，和不许查、不许说明处理过程、尤其不许追问机构责任，是两回事。

说到底，这两种声音底下是同一个问题：谁的未来被当成了不用证明的价值，谁的遭遇却要先证明自己配得上被当回事。我一直说人是目的，这句话没有附加条件，不是表现好的人才是目的，喝了酒的、去了派对的、跟对方认识的，也是。反过来，被指控的人也是目的，所以要有正当程序，要有无罪推定。

认真对待报案，不等于未审先定罪；同时坚持无罪推定，也不等于先对报案的人做有罪推定。一个人不需要先证明自己是完美的人，才配不被侵犯。
author: hqinjarsy
quoted_text:
有朋友追问，那当初斯坦福那个性侵案子，是怎么处理的？

那个案子其实斯坦福本身不像今天的康奈尔，学校没什么选择。那是2015年1月的一天凌晨，Kappa Alpha兄弟会派对外面，游泳队19岁的新生Brock Turner，在一个垃圾箱后面侵犯一个已经失去意识的女生。两个骑车路过的瑞典研究生看见了，上前喝止，他转身就跑，被他们追上按在地上，一直等到警察来。所以这个案子从一开始就不归学校，直接进了刑事程序。2016年3月，陪审团认定他三项重罪成立。

检方要求判六年。法官Aaron Persky判了六个月看守所，加三年缓刑，终身登记为性犯罪者，理由之一是，坐牢会对他造成严重影响。他实际关了三个月就出来了。他父亲在给法官的信里写，为了二十分钟的行为，付出这么大的代价，太重了。这些话里被反复掂量的，是他的前途，而她的那一半，要靠她自己站出来说。

后来她确实站出来了。宣判那天，她在法庭上读了一份七千多字的陈述，第二天全文登上网络，几天之内就有几百万人读过。后面的事几乎都是从这份陈述开始的。2016年9月，加州修法，对侵犯失去意识或醉酒的人规定必须入狱。2018年6月，选民以六成多的票数罢免了Persky，他是加州八十多年来第一个被罢免的法官。同一年，上诉法院维持了原判。2019年，她公开了自己的名字，Chanel Miller，出了回忆录，书名叫《知道我的名字》。

那斯坦福呢？案发两周内，学校进行了调查，并禁止Turner再踏入校园。判决出来以后，学校发表声明称，斯坦福已经尽其所能确保正义得到伸张。这话不算假，可接下来几件事，就耐人寻味了。

2016年8月，学校宣布本科生派对上禁止烈酒。很多人批评，这等于暗示问题出在酒上，不在人身上。案发地后来改建成一个小花园，Miller挑了陈述里的一段话，想刻在那里，学校拒绝了，理由是这些话放在一个给幸存者疗伤的地方，不够支持。她退出了。直到2019年她的书出版，学生自己做了牌子偷偷挂上去，学校才改口，2020年2月，牌子终于装好，前后拖了三年多。更早在2015年，学校做过一次校园性侵调查，公布的数字是1.9%，几位教授指出，学校用的定义很窄，就算用这个窄定义，高年级本科女生里也有6.5%遇到过，第二年师生要求重做，学校没有答应。

所以斯坦福确实没有掩盖这个案子，因为也掩盖不了，目击者、警察、法庭都在。它管的是这件事怎么被讲：问题出在酒还是出在人，数字该用窄的还是宽的，刻在地上的，是学校的话还是她的话。这跟我上一篇说康奈尔是同一个逻辑，机构未必要藏起事实，它更想决定事实被怎么讲。区别在于，斯坦福那次，法庭接了手，学校不是唯一的出口；康奈尔这次，检察官不起诉，学校几乎成了她唯一能讨说法的地方。

回头看，这个案子里每一次往对的方向拨，几乎都不是机构主动做的。是两个路人没有走开，是她没有沉默，是选民不肯放过一个法官，是学生自己把牌子挂上了墙。法院掂量的是他的前途，学校掂量的是自己的样子，把她当成目的的，只有她自己，和那些站在她这边的人。

那块牌子上最后刻的，是她原本选的那句：你拿走了我的价值、我的隐私、我的精力、我的时间、我的安全、我的亲密、我的自信、我自己的声音，直到今天。

大家最近没注意到的一个 SEC 的细节更新，可能会影响这波版本强势的“代币回购”叙事。

SEC 官方一直设有一份关于“加密资产是否属于证券”的指导问答（FAQ），这也是各大律所和项目方用来规避监管雷区的“红宝书”。

根据海外加密记者 @EleanorTerrett  的爆料，SEC 公司金融部在 9 月 28 日更新了关于代币回购的 FAQ。修订后的核心是：

针对代币回购，加了四个字的豁免前提，即“没有中心方（no central party）”才行。

它的意思是，只有当回购是由链上代码自动执行，且没有任何单一实体可以干预时，这种安排才不构成违规的证券发行。

但如果回购背后还有一个基金会或核心团队在开会拍板，并且大张旗鼓地宣传“给持币人分红”，这就会被监管视为危险的收益承诺。

这道界限如果生效，会直接将当前的几十个回购标的分成两拨：

一类是协议机制派（如 $HYPE、$UNI）。它们的回购资金流向无私钥地址或直接销毁，全程由底层参数驱动，没有团队干预。这种真正“无人操盘”的机制，在本次更新中获得了极大的合规安全垫。

另一类是团队主导派（如 $PUMP、$ENA 以及各类新发代币）。只要回购额度还需要实体开会决定，本质上依然是“科技公司在分配利润”。这精准踩中了 SEC 想打击的管理红线。

所以之后在评价一个代币的回购是否具有稳健基本面时，可能还要考虑回购资金从哪来、谁能修改规则，以及是否包含了收益承诺。

author: Calderaxyz
quoted_text:
@yifi_io put together a great breakdown of Horizen this week 👏

It's also worth going one layer deeper on what happens when you swap $ZEN on YiFi.

In plain terms: instead of trading directly from your wallet to the destination, YiFi adds a detour in the middle with possible two routes:

The first routes through a privacy-focused intermediary asset. That middle step carries real, mathematical privacy, meaning nobody can see the sender, the receiver, or the amount just by looking at the public record.

The second routes through a stablecoin – a token pegged to something like the US dollar. This route moves faster and skips the price swings of the first option, but the privacy here comes from randomness, not math, so it makes tracking harder rather than mathematically impossible.

In both cases, YiFi never holds your funds directly. Each step of the swap runs through partner exchanges, not through YiFi itself. The whole point: break the easy, public trail connecting where your ZEN starts and where it ends up, not promise total invisibility.

That honesty matters, and it lines up with what Horizen builds toward: privacy people can actually verify, explained plainly rather than oversold.

Full mechanics, straight from the source: https://t.co/fF5pvGvhSz

text:
今天看到海外媒体报了个新闻，叫“中国最高情报机构警告加密货币的匿名性是伪命题”。

这么高端的 title ，但是没给出处。

带着好奇，小编查了下，这实际源于昨天国安部微信公众号的一篇文章：《虚拟货币犯罪无法追踪？想多了！》

看上去更像日常的安全警示和必要的教育宣传。

不过，这个文章里有个增量信息，那就是加密货币已经渗透到了间谍领域，甚至有可能成为间谍窃密的帮凶。

官方的核心增量信息是：境外间谍正在利用“链上查不到”的心理错觉，打消被策反对象的顾虑，并用加密货币支付经费。

更有意思的是，小编挖出了国安部近两年公开的几个涉加密货币案卷，串起来看，你会发现加密的玩法早就被用在了意想不到的领域，甚至不小心还可能躺枪：

1. 用 GameFi 模式搞地理测绘，采集敏感信息（2024年初）：

据当时通报，境外地图公司搞起了 Play-to-Earn 模式，诱使境内人员购买专用设备，非法采集敏感地理空间数据并上传境外服务器。某些特定区域甚至有高额的代币奖励机制。

2. 炒币爆仓变泄密工具人（2024年底）：
一名涉密单位的公职人员汪某某因为炒虚拟币巨亏欠债，在论坛发帖找兼职时被境外情报机关盯上。
对方用虚拟币充值、交易变现的方式，支付了折合 100 多万人民币的经费，换取了绝密级国家秘密。最终该人员被判处无期徒刑。

3. 买币买成了“资助敌对组织”（2025年5月）
一名医疗器械销售员，因为看了境外反华组织的宣传视频，被“高额投资回报”洗脑，花了一万美元购买该组织发行的虚拟货币。这直接被官方定性为“资助反华组织”的违法事实，并受到处罚。

海外新闻额原贴评论区，老外网友们都在纷纷 CX ZEC 和 门罗币，大喊这才是真正的无法追踪。

加密货币特定情况下不只是赃款通道，更是策反漏斗里的镇定剂。当有人给你提供“高薪兼职、去特定地点拍拍照”，并强调“用 USDT 结算很安全”时，在国家安全系统的逻辑里，这已经是一套标准的间谍策反模版了。

对加密玩家来说，更应该警惕的是躺枪和被利用。

text:
The main problem here is that @THORChain’s existing swap-halting controls work at the chain level, not the wallet level.

They can pause Ethereum swaps or outgoing transfers, but those switches don’t single out the hacker, and using them would also hold up other users, which is why this isn’t as simple as freezing an account.

There are still options, but each has limits:

• Share tracing data with exchanges that could freeze incoming funds
• Propose wallet blocking, requiring code changes and node support

IMO, helping exchanges intercept the funds is the more practical immediate step. Adding wallet blocking would be a bigger change to how THORChain operates, rather than a quick fix for this incident.

❌ Old way: build a network when you need it.

$AXIS Community Sale is officially settled, and the final terms ended up looking quite different from where they started.

@axisrobotics originally launched the round with pretty strict unlock terms, but after the sale closed oversubscribed, they've now added a bonus mechanism for participants.

Here's where things landed:

→ final fulfillment: 42.0346%
→ 25% of allocated $AXIS unlocks at TGE
→ additional bonus tokens are fully unlocked at TGE
→ bonus size is based on the original commitment before pro-rata dilution
→ USDC refunds have already been sent automatically, no claim needed

That bonus structure is probably the most interesting part to me.

Instead of calculating it from the final ~42% allocation, Axis is using the amount participants originally committed before the pro-rata dilution.

Axis says 2,472 participants committed under the original stricter terms, and the bonus is essentially their way of rewarding those who were willing to commit before the improved unlock structure existed.

There was also a small change in the final allocation.

Fulfillment moved from 41.7674% → 42.0346% after Axis rejected several wallets/KYC submissions they linked to suspicious activity.

The sale page now shows the revised unlock, bonus allocation and total $AXIS available at TGE, while refunds have already landed directly in participant wallets.

quoted_text:
Hi,

Tomorrow we are re-opening the Pro $200 subscriptions to new subscribers, but together with it we are also changing how we calculate the usage for it. In effect, if you do the math, it will net out at half the dollar in API spend compared to the old Pro $200 plan. 

Now that it's said, let me explain why this is happening and why you will still get more work done than if you were on the Pro $200 subscription one month ago.

(a) We didn't want to compromise in other ways and are committing to not reintroducing the 5h limit, so that you can fully use the weekly usage when you want.
(b) On the subscription, we guarantee that over time you always get more work done and with an increasing level of quality. This means that you will continue to get more value per dollar spent as a result of models getting more efficient and us passing down the improvements in the form of API price reductions.
(c) We don't want to put an incentive on ourselves to artificially inflate the API list prices to make it look like you are getting a lot (and workaround it through discounts, etc). Instead we want to continue to both rapidly reduce prices and increase capabilities of models on the API. This week we introduced GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna at 50% of their previous price. Over time, we see prices go low enough that it makes sense for most to buy usage as needed without there being a significant gap between what you get in a subscription and what you get in the API for a dollar spent.
(d) Tomorrow, we are adding more things to the subscription that won't draw on the usage, I won't reveal what that is yet.

I wanted to be transparent before all the big announcements tomorrow. Lots of new exciting things are coming to the subscriptions that will make it super compelling, but I wanted to make sure to share this change ahead of time so you can all understand it before we shower you with good news.

Codexingly,
Tibo

author: martiano
quoted_text:
Hi,

Tomorrow we are re-opening the Pro $200 subscriptions to new subscribers, but together with it we are also changing how we calculate the usage for it. In effect, if you do the math, it will net out at half the dollar in API spend compared to the old Pro $200 plan. 

Now that it's said, let me explain why this is happening and why you will still get more work done than if you were on the Pro $200 subscription one month ago.

(a) We didn't want to compromise in other ways and are committing to not reintroducing the 5h limit, so that you can fully use the weekly usage when you want.
(b) On the subscription, we guarantee that over time you always get more work done and with an increasing level of quality. This means that you will continue to get more value per dollar spent as a result of models getting more efficient and us passing down the improvements in the form of API price reductions.
(c) We don't want to put an incentive on ourselves to artificially inflate the API list prices to make it look like you are getting a lot (and workaround it through discounts, etc). Instead we want to continue to both rapidly reduce prices and increase capabilities of models on the API. This week we introduced GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna at 50% of their previous price. Over time, we see prices go low enough that it makes sense for most to buy usage as needed without there being a significant gap between what you get in a subscription and what you get in the API for a dollar spent.
(d) Tomorrow, we are adding more things to the subscription that won't draw on the usage, I won't reveal what that is yet.

I wanted to be transparent before all the big announcements tomorrow. Lots of new exciting things are coming to the subscriptions that will make it super compelling, but I wanted to make sure to share this change ahead of time so you can all understand it before we shower you with good news.

Codexingly,
Tibo
