author: AlphaSeeker21

text:
most ai tokens are a wrapper around a chatbot and a roadmap pdf.

@promptduel is trying to sell the thing labs actually run out of: judgment.

models can spit answers all day. the bottleneck is which answer is better, at scale, with a trail you can reuse. static benches rot. llm-as-judge copies the judge’s prior. scale pays humans in batches and hopes the vendor isn’t lying. that’s the whole post-training stack sitting on wage labour and vibes.

$stakd - style pads monetise attention. this one is trying to monetise disagreement.

you get a prompt and two completions. you buy tickets in eth. 0.0001 eth a ticket, 1 to 32. you pick a side. counts settle onchain. the tape is preference data with capital sitting on it. if a lab ever pays for a slice, 30% of that invoice is reserved to buy and burn $duel. protocol eth from fees splits the same way. 70% ops. not the full invoice. nobody should pretend otherwise.

$duel is not the collateral. that’s the bit most people will miss and then get angry about later. tickets, payouts, claims are eth. token is the rebate and the api key. stake it, you skip the 5bps protocol spread. unstake is 7 days. production api wants 100k staked when that module is actually on. whitepaper is explicit: do not infer ownership of the venue, the dataset, or some claim on future invoices just because you hold the ticker.

so what are you actually buying at ~250k?

a week-old robinhood listing. testnet venue live, mainnet still behind a security review. 440 holders. pons already spraying eth at holders off trading fees — call it 2 eth in the first few days. they say 88m burned. some of that is real sink, some of that is launch optics. treat it like a trader.

the flywheel they want:

hold / stake $duel → eth from the pair → more tickets → more preference tape → fees + data sales → burns → tighter float → more people using the venue.

half of that loop is live. the important half isn’t. if mainnet never does volume, if no lab writes a usdc cheque for the tape, this is just another rh narrative coin with a clever readme. that’s the invalidation. not a red candle. stalled settlement revenue.

why it can still be mispriced if they ship:

evaluation is not a cute side quest. it is the control layer for everything being trained after pretrain. a permissionless pairwise market is a cleaner primitive than “trust our dashboard.” founder is not a cartoon anon - aric eggers is building in public, paper is a working draft, they’re iterating the mechanism in the open. that usually looks ugly until it doesn’t.

i’m not telling you this is priced like a data business. it isn’t one yet. i’m saying the market is selling you a meme wrapper while the thing underneath is an attempt to turn human preference into a public tape. those two interpretations should not have the same multiple once the venue is live and the first tape invoice clears.

until then size it like a pre-product option on rh chain. if duel counts, treasury eth from settlement, and a real data buyer show up, the optionality is obvious. if they don’t, you didn’t need a thread to know what that looks like.

are you paying attention.

text:
1/ Bitget users loves this outcome: thief tries to wash it through cross-chain rails. Near Intents' SHIELD flags the dirty flow -> freezes mid-swap -> waives the bounty so more can go back to users.

Users got saved, but i fsee few CT calling it "decentraliztion failed" - that's a bad take.

Coinbase blacklists stolen BTC. BTC is still Bitcoin.
same logic: chain stays open, the rail refuses the loot.

NEAR Intents is an execution venue. user signs an outcome, solvers (MM...) compete to fill it, contract settles. solvers can just not quote. SHIELD can refuse a flow or halt one mid-execution. That's a market maker not buying stolen bags.

2/ permissionless = anyone can submit an intent.
it does not mean the venue has to monetize hacked funds for you.
a system that calls itself permissionless so it can be the ATM for thieves is not a better system. it's just protecting the thief.

NEAR L1 = permissionless chain.
intents.near = settlement contract anyone can call with a valid signed intent.
NEAR Intents the product (quotes, solvers, SHIELD) sits on top and can refuse a flow.
judging $NEAR's moneyness by a solver venue's risk policy is like saying ETH isn't money because Aave can freeze a reserve.

3/ Also it's funny how "decentralization" works in this industry:
protect your bags => gud
protect someone else's bags => bad bad bad 

Few examples: 
- Aave Apr 2026: Kelp rsETH (~$292M) dumped as collateral, real WETH borrowed out. Guardian froze rsETH then froze WETH across chains to stop their pool from dying. ~$8-12B ran for the exit.
- Hyperliquid: JELLY validators force-settled the market to save HLP. POPCAT they EmergencyLocked the Arbitrum bridge.
- THORChain May 2026: halt the whole network when their vault got drained ~$10.7M.
- Arbitrum council yoinked ~30.7k ETH (~$71M) from the Kelp attacker.
- Sui validators just didn't include Cetus attacker txs and froze ~$162M.
same THORChain this week: Bitget asks them to refuse publicly known attacker addresses. they say no, halt is only to protect the protocol, not to freeze a swap, then ~$6.3M ETH → BTC goes through them anyway.
- Bybit 2025 was the same movie. they will pull the plug when their own vault is on fire. they will not pull it when someone else's stolen funds use them as a bridge. that's not principle. that's selective insurance.

4/
Also the "never intervene" crowd always skip the origin stories
- 2010: overflow bug minted 184 billion BTC in one tx. more than 8,000x the 21M cap. Satoshi shipped a patch in ~5 hours. the network reorged, orphaned the bad block, deleted the fake coins.
- 2016: The DAO got drained for ~3.6M ETH (~5% of supply then). Ethereum hard forked at block 1,920,000 and moved the funds back. the "code is law, do nothing" chain still exists. it's called ETC.
so the two chains people treat as scripture both chose not to sit there and watch the system die.

If "permissionless" means you never touch anything, even when a bug prints 184 billion BTC or a contract eats 5% of the supply, then permissionless just means "the attacker keeps the bags."
BTC didn't accept 184B fake coins because that would make BTC meaningless. ETH didn't accept the DAO drain because that would've nuked the whole chain.
refusing to quote known stolen Bitget funds on a solver venue is not some unique sin. it's the same instinct, one layer up.

5/
ZEC/XMR... are bearer money. Intents is a solver venue,  comparing those two is how you get the "billions to trillions" fanfic.
if your decentralization only turns on when the hole is in your P&L, just say that 🤷

To me, NEAR is the market of markets, the silk road as Mert said, and this road open for everyone except thiefts, and NEAR is the only viable infra for NEAR intents to grow on: 6+ years of mainnet, 100% uptime and proven scalable tech.

text:
NEAR Intents 冻结 50.3 万美元 Bitget 被盗资金，主动放弃赏金

NEAR Intents 发布报告称，黑客曾尝试通过其转移超过 5000 万美元的 Bitget 被盗资金，最终有 16.6 万美元通过，另有 50.3 万美元在交易执行途中被冻结，目前等待依法处理和追偿。

这些拦截由风控系统 SHIELD 完成。它会结合资金流异常、交易监测服务及安全机构等提供的信息，识别与黑客攻击有关的交易，并通过不提供报价或中止执行来阻止资金转移。报告提到，超过 5000 万美元是剔除重复记录后的尝试转移金额，相关资金后来转向了其他服务商，并非全部被 NEAR Intents 冻结。

针对 Bitget 公布的“5%＋5%”赏金安排，NEAR Intents 表示将主动放弃自身可获得的赏金，让 Bitget 尽可能追回更多资金，并请其通过适当的法律和执法渠道对接，处理被冻结的资产。

NEAR Intents 也在报告中明确了自己的立场：“无需许可不代表中立。”团队认为，协议建设者可以选择拒绝协助转移和变现被盗资产，不能一边要求数字产权获得承认，一边为处置被盗财产提供便利。

quoted_text:
NEAR is permissionless programmable money.

Permissionless means nobody needs permission to own and transfer assets, or deploy contracts on NEAR.

It does not mean every application or liquidity provider must process every transaction.

SHIELD is how NEAR Intents applies this in practice: shared, real-time risk intelligence that lets participants identify hacks and other incidents and choose not to facilitate stolen funds. Partners can both consume and contribute incident data.

In the Bitget hack, SHIELD identified $50M+ in attempted flows through NEAR Intents and helped stop funds during execution.

Open financial infrastructure does not require us to make theft easy. Instead of hiding behind "it's permissionless, what can we do" while sitting on pause button, we should be creative in solutions that are addressing underlying problem.

We can have permissionless protocols that have intelligent defense. This is what we are building with SHIELD and invite everyone to join to make SHIELD industry-wide.

text:
Chainlink's CCIP 2.0 is live, and its biggest upgrade might be how customizable it is.

Institutions can now configure how their assets move cross-chain based on their own requirements.

They can add independent CCVs (@chainlink's Cross Chain Verifiers) for additional verification, define when that verification kicks in, and choose between faster execution or full finality depending on the transaction.

Through ACE, they can also embed custom KYC, AML, sanctions, allowlist, and transaction policies directly into cross-chain transfers. This is a pretty important unlock for bringing institutional assets onchain.

A $10K payment and a $100M institutional settlement don't need the same security, compliance, or settlement parameters. CCIP 2.0 gives issuers control over those parameters without requiring them to build their own interoperability stack for every chain.

Tomorrow we are re-opening the Pro $200 subscriptions to new subscribers, but together with it we are also changing how we calculate the usage for it. In effect, if you do the math, it will net out at half the dollar in API spend compared to the old Pro $200 plan. 

Now that it's said, let me explain why this is happening and why you will still get more work done than if you were on the Pro $200 subscription one month ago.

(a) We didn't want to compromise in other ways and are committing to not reintroducing the 5h limit, so that you can fully use the weekly usage when you want.
(b) On the subscription, we guarantee that over time you always get more work done and with an increasing level of quality. This means that you will continue to get more value per dollar spent as a result of models getting more efficient and us passing down the improvements in the form of API price reductions.
(c) We don't want to put an incentive on ourselves to artificially inflate the API list prices to make it look like you are getting a lot (and workaround it through discounts, etc). Instead we want to continue to both rapidly reduce prices and increase capabilities of models on the API. This week we introduced GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna at 50% of their previous price. Over time, we see prices go low enough that it makes sense for most to buy usage as needed without there being a significant gap between what you get in a subscription and what you get in the API for a dollar spent.
(d) Tomorrow, we are adding more things to the subscription that won't draw on the usage, I won't reveal what that is yet.

I wanted to be transparent before all the big announcements tomorrow. Lots of new exciting things are coming to the subscriptions that will make it super compelling, but I wanted to make sure to share this change ahead of time so you can all understand it before we shower you with good news.

Codexingly,
Tibo

text:
今天亚洲时段，十年期美债收益率仍在 5.23% 附近，处于 2007 年以来的高位。能源通胀和美国债务的压力还在，投资者要求更高的收益，才愿意持有长期国债。

美伊这边，双方已经在周一分别与调解人沟通，后续讨论围绕伊朗提出的七天方案的修改版本展开。伊朗外长表示，仍在等待美国对最新停火和恢复霍尔木兹海峡通航条件的回应。与此同时，川普隔夜公开否认已经向伊朗提出制裁减免和解冻资金的条件。

油价也继续受到供应担忧而缓慢上涨。中东原油出口虽然有所恢复，但部分运输仍依赖船对船转运等安排，效率更低、成本更高，距离正常供应还有差距。

从这个情况来看，油价即使不再大幅上涨，只要长时间维持在高位，运输、生产和居民日常支出的成本就会继续受到影响。如果这些成本不断向其他商品和服务传导，美联储继续收紧政策的压力也会增加（加息概率上升）。

而十年期美债收益率维持在 5.23% 附近，意味着长期融资成本已经在给经济施加压力。企业借新钱、偿还到期债务会更贵，居民贷款消费的负担也会加重。对美股和 bitcoin:native 来说，更高的美债收益率也提高了资金承担风险的门槛，投资者需要看到更好的回报前景，才愿意增加风险敞口。

今天最重要的就是美国是否愿意和伊朗进行霍尔木兹开放的谈判，伊朗外交部长已经公开表示，希望美国可以在周二给出明确答案。

quoted_text:
周一开盘以后石油普遍上涨了 2% 左右，这种上涨基本就是周末川普表示不会和伊朗谈判的反应，但从上涨趋势来看别没有快速的回到美联储加息前的高点，说明市场认为加息对于抑制油价的上涨还是会有帮助的。

目前我个人的观点是 WTI 可能会维持在 100 美元左右，Brant 可能会维持在 105 附近，这个价格可能还会有波动，但继续向上的空间未必会很大，如果继续上涨的话，美联储大概率会用继续加息的方式来应对。

另外需要关注的是十年期的长债收益率已经突破了 5.2% ，市场的担心很有可能就是油价在短期很难下降会带动美国的通胀上涨，从而刺激美联储继续维持高利率。

对于美股和 bitcoin:native 来说，美债收益率上升也会提高资金选择风险资产的门槛。当相对低风险的资产能够提供更高收益时，投资者就需要看到更好的盈利前景，或者更大的上涨空间，才愿意承担额外的风险，这会给高估值和依赖资金推动的资产带来压力。

text:
有人说 Khua Player 不就是 FFmpeg 的套壳吗？

但其实，为了开发一个性能足够强大、功能又有新意的播放器，真正需要完成的工作，远不止把视频解码出来。 

FFmpeg 提供了优秀的基础，但画面何时呈现、声音如何同步、拖动进度是否干脆、资源如何分配、文件损坏后怎么办，都需要播放器自己处理。认出一个底层库，并不等于理解了整个产品。

Khua 自己实现了播放调度、音画同步、画面渲染、音频输出和异常恢复，仅四个核心实现文件就超过 2 万行。

代码多不代表产品就好，但这些代码实现的功能、解决的问题，也不能被「套壳」两个字一笔带过。

用户看到的是一个播放按钮，按钮背后却是一整套需要协调运转的系统。把所有功劳都归给 FFmpeg，实际上是把解码之后、画面呈现之前的大量工程直接跳过了。

Khua 与 VLC、IINA 的区别，也在于产品取舍。

成熟播放器需要照顾广泛的环境、历史兼容性和完整的功能需求，这些目标会影响架构和优化方向。

Khua 则主动收窄范围，聚焦 Apple 芯片、现代 macOS 和本地视频体验，把更多精力放在明确平台上的针对性优化。

覆盖更多场景，与集中打磨一种体验，本来就是不同的路线。 功能列表更长，不代表每个用户都需要同样庞大的功能版图。

这种选择最终要落实到观看过程中：让运动画面通过实时补帧变得更流畅，让没有字幕的视频可以在本机生成和翻译字幕，让损坏或尚未下载完成的文件仍有机会继续观看。

底层能力来自 FFmpeg、Apple 等组件，而如何把它们组织成可用的功能，处理它们与播放、交互和资源消耗之间的冲突，是 Khua 自己的工作。尊重底层贡献，和承认产品工程的价值，完全可以同时成立。

FFmpeg 提供了处理视频的基础能力，Khua 还要负责把整个播放体验做好。 播放是否顺畅、操作是否跟手、补帧和字幕功能是否好用，都需要额外的设计和开发。

评价 Khua，应该看这些工作做得怎么样。只看到它用了 FFmpeg，就把其余部分统统叫作「套壳」，忽略的恰恰是播放器本身的价值。

quoted_text:

text:
Big deal for the $COIN . Bottom line:

- The CFTC approved Coinbase's own clearinghouse today. A DCO is the entity that guarantees every derivatives trade settles: it becomes the buyer to every seller and vice versa.

- Until now, Coinbase's futures exchange cleared through a third party (Nodal Clear). Now Coinbase owns the full stack: exchange plus clearinghouse. That keeps clearing fees in-house and lets them launch products without waiting on someone else's rails.

- The scope is fully collateralized futures, options on futures, and swaps. Fully collateralized means every position is backed 1:1, no leverage blowups, no default fund. Same model Kalshi uses. Retail-friendly, regulator-friendly.

- This is the plumbing for the Everything Exchange push: prediction markets, the 24/7 single-stock perpetuals they filed for, options on futures.

author: teortaxesTex
quoted_text:
We took the kids to Japan last month. It was my 3rd trip, Sara’s 2nd, & their 1st. They of course loved it.

But a few days into Tokyo they said something that was more profound than I think they realized, “It’s not futuristic.”

Before the trip they had watched a bunch of videos showing how Tokyo was going to feel like the future (It’s how we ended up at a capybara cafe.)

And they really did love Japan. In Tokyo we ended up at the fish market almost every morning because they wanted to keep going back and try different foods. Blowtorched scallops, oysters, and BBQ octopus were the favorites.

We had Kobe beef, made our own chopsticks, went to the Nintendo Museum, had deer bow to us in Nara. It was an incredible trip. I highly recommend it, especially with elementary/middle school-age kids.

But their observation was quite specific. There were no Cybercabs, no Waymos, no delivery robots on the sidewalk, all things they see every day in Austin.

I was a kid in the late 80s/early 90s (don't do the math please 🙏). I grew up on anime and cyberpunk, and later Blade Runner and Akira. Tokyo was the image of the future. 

Even one of my kids’ favorite movies, Big Hero 6, imagines the future as a mashup of San Francisco and Tokyo.

My kids went all the way to Tokyo expecting to see the future and instead the future was at home.  

We may be leaving the cyberpunk era and entering the cowboy futurism era.

quoted_text:
Hi,

Tomorrow we are re-opening the Pro $200 subscriptions to new subscribers, but together with it we are also changing how we calculate the usage for it. In effect, if you do the math, it will net out at half the dollar in API spend compared to the old Pro $200 plan. 

Now that it's said, let me explain why this is happening and why you will still get more work done than if you were on the Pro $200 subscription one month ago.

(a) We didn't want to compromise in other ways and are committing to not reintroducing the 5h limit, so that you can fully use the weekly usage when you want.
(b) On the subscription, we guarantee that over time you always get more work done and with an increasing level of quality. This means that you will continue to get more value per dollar spent as a result of models getting more efficient and us passing down the improvements in the form of API price reductions.
(c) We don't want to put an incentive on ourselves to artificially inflate the API list prices to make it look like you are getting a lot (and workaround it through discounts, etc). Instead we want to continue to both rapidly reduce prices and increase capabilities of models on the API. This week we introduced GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna at 50% of their previous price. Over time, we see prices go low enough that it makes sense for most to buy usage as needed without there being a significant gap between what you get in a subscription and what you get in the API for a dollar spent.
(d) Tomorrow, we are adding more things to the subscription that won't draw on the usage, I won't reveal what that is yet.

I wanted to be transparent before all the big announcements tomorrow. Lots of new exciting things are coming to the subscriptions that will make it super compelling, but I wanted to make sure to share this change ahead of time so you can all understand it before we shower you with good news.

Codexingly,
Tibo

text:
Stocks and RWAs are moving onchain.

But I don't think enough people are paying attention to what that actually means.

For years, stocks, ETFs and bonds were basically out of reach for a lot of people outside traditional financial markets.

I remember thinking Tesla was a great buy years ago, but I couldn't actually buy it.

Not because I didn't know what Tesla was.

I simply didn't have access to the market.

That access problem is slowly changing.

We've spent years watching companies build the infrastructure to bring traditional assets onchain.

Ondo has built a large catalogue of tokenized stocks and ETFs across multiple chains.

Backed/xStocks has brought hundreds of equities and ETFs onchain.

Coinbase is bringing tokenized stocks onto Base.

Robinhood has its own tokenized stock infrastructure.

Binance has bStocks.

Backpack is bringing actual securities exposure onto Solana.

The important part isn't that every issuer is doing the exact same thing. They aren't.

The legal structure, rights, custody and jurisdictions can differ significantly between products.

But the direction is clear:

traditional financial assets are becoming programmable, transferable digital assets.

And that's where I think Jumper gets interesting.

Because once you have all these issuers creating assets, you still have a distribution problem.

You don't want to visit five different platforms to find five different versions of the same asset.

You don't want to think about which chain an asset lives on.

You don't want to manually bridge, swap and route capital every time you want exposure to something.

Jumper is increasingly becoming the layer that brings that fragmented market together.

Their RWA interface already lets users explore tokenized assets from issuers including Ondo, xStocks, Robinhood, Backpack Securities, Coinbase and bStocks in one place.

And you can already see the direction:

$TSLA
$NVDA
$AAPL
$MSFT
$SPY
$QQQ
$Gold

and dozens of other assets.
One interface. Multiple issuers. Multiple chains.
That gets even more interesting when you move from individual assets to portfolios.
I find the idea of RWA asset baskets particularly interesting.

Instead of someone having to decide:
"Should I buy Nvidia?"
"Should I buy Tesla?"
"Should I buy the S&P 500?"

You can start thinking in terms of exposure.

AI.

Technology.

The S&P 500.

Dividends.

Gold.

Growth.

A basket can package multiple assets into one portfolio exposure, making diversification much simpler.

And because these assets live onchain, the portfolio doesn't have to stop at simply holding them.

Eventually you can imagine the same assets being used across lending, collateral, trading, yield and other onchain financial applications.

That's the bigger opportunity.

Tokenization is only the first step.

Issuers bring the assets onchain.

Jumper brings the assets together.

DeFi gives those assets utility.

And users get a financial system that starts looking much more open and composable.

This is also why Jumper's September 22 announcement is important.

Jumper isn't positioning itself as just a bridge anymore.

The stated direction is to become a super-app for onchain finance  one place where users can swap, bridge, access yield, trade perps and access tokenized stocks and other RWAs.

They already have the distribution.

$40B+ lifetime volume.

100K+ monthly active users.

15%+ share of bridging volume, according to Jumper.

Now they're trying to turn that distribution into a much broader financial application.

That's the thesis I'm watching.

The future may not be about bringing every asset to one chain.

It may be about making every asset accessible from one interface.

And Jumper is clearly trying to build that interface.

The next step is the JUMP launch on Legion.

The sales goes live today September 29.

If you're interested in what @jumperapp  is building and want to participate in the sale, start from the links in the comment:

Hi,

Tomorrow we are re-opening the Pro $200 subscriptions to new subscribers, but together with it we are also changing how we calculate the usage for it. In effect, if you do the math, it will net out at half the dollar in API spend compared to the old Pro $200 plan. 

Now that it's said, let me explain why this is happening and why you will still get more work done than if you were on the Pro $200 subscription one month ago.

(a) We didn't want to compromise in other ways and are committing to not reintroducing the 5h limit, so that you can fully use the weekly usage when you want.
(b) On the subscription, we guarantee that over time you always get more work done and with an increasing level of quality. This means that you will continue to get more value per dollar spent as a result of models getting more efficient and us passing down the improvements in the form of API price reductions.
(c) We don't want to put an incentive on ourselves to artificially inflate the API list prices to make it look like you are getting a lot (and workaround it through discounts, etc). Instead we want to continue to both rapidly reduce prices and increase capabilities of models on the API. This week we introduced GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna at 50% of their previous price. Over time, we see prices go low enough that it makes sense for most to buy usage as needed without there being a significant gap between what you get in a subscription and what you get in the API for a dollar spent.
(d) Tomorrow, we are adding more things to the subscription that won't draw on the usage, I won't reveal what that is yet.

I wanted to be transparent before all the big announcements tomorrow. Lots of new exciting things are coming to the subscriptions that will make it super compelling, but I wanted to make sure to share this change ahead of time so you can all understand it before we shower you with good news.

Codexingly,
Tibo

text: 1/ Our @projecteleven research team (@conordeegan,  @furkanakal, Louis Tajan, and Jamie Judd) just published an early look at CUTS, a new few-time hash-based signature scheme. At 546 bytes, close to WOTS size, & a key that signs twice in error keeps 53 bits of security instead of collapsing.  🧵
author: apruden08
quoted_text:
Introducing CUTS (Chained Uniform-sum Tree Signatures), a new few-time hash-based signature scheme from our research team at Project Eleven.

Hash-based signatures are one of the most conservative paths to post-quantum security. Their security rests only on hash functions, but that simplicity comes at the cost of larger signatures.

The most compact schemes reduce that cost by using one-time keys, which become vulnerable if they are ever reused. Restore an old backup or load the same seed onto two devices, and a one-time key can end up signing twice. A WOTS+C key that has signed twice keeps only about 34 bits of security. One GPU can then forge a new signature in under a second.

By contrast, few-time signatures are built to handle reuse, but they are larger. FORS, the few-time construction inside SLH-DSA, needs more than 2 KB per signature at 128-bit security.

CUTS targets the middle ground: more security after reuse, at sizes close to one-time signatures. It arranges hash chains in a tree, and the message hash picks which chains each signature reveals. When a key signs twice, the two signatures usually expose different parts of the key.

At 546 bytes, close to one-time size, a CUTS key keeps 53 bits of security after two signatures.

At 1,360 bytes it keeps the full 128 bits. That is 41% smaller than any FORS parameter set at that security with practical key generation.

At 2,128 bytes, CUTS is smaller, faster to verify and cheaper to generate than every FORS parameter set we compared, including the one in SLH-DSA-128s.

The aim is hash-based signatures that hold up in systems where accidental key reuse can happen. The parameters let each application trade signature size, verification cost, key generation and security after reuse against each other.

The paper, with the full specification and security proofs, is coming soon. These figures come from our current analysis, and the parameter sets and numbers in the paper may differ. We'd love feedback, from improvements to attacks. Reply or get in touch.

text:
Awesome progress on threshold signatures for hash-based schemes. Dan Boneh, Benedikt Bünz and al. show how to turn a Winternitz-style one-time key into a (t)-of-(n) setup while still emitting a normal single-signer signature.

The chain never learns (n) or (t). The trick is a context-aware threshold PRF that derives the hash-chain secrets. 

However the construction comes with limitation. It covers one-time WOTS and few-time schemes like XMSS and FORS, so it maps to the compact stateful path of SHRINCS. It does not apply to SLH-DSA, hence not to the stateless fallback. 

There is no efficient DKG, so shares still need a centralized trusted dealer for each signature. And the large-(n) variant puts a lattice assumption on the signers, the assumption hash-based signatures were chosen to avoid. The verifier stays hash-only, if the lattice breaks, signers can attack each other, not the chain.

text:
这几天 Bitget 的安全事件，我一直在想一个问题：

一家交易所真正的信用，到底靠什么验证？

9 月 24 日，Bitget 监测到部分热钱包和温钱包出现异常转账，官方随后暂停提现。

目前官方披露的受影响资产规模约 3.875 亿美元；冷钱包未受影响，用户账户余额不受影响，Bitget 表示由超过 4.64 亿美元的 Protection Fund 覆盖此次事件的财务影响，同时委托 Mandiant 和 SlowMist 参与调查与资金追踪。(Bitget)

这些都是公告层面的信息。

但交易所出了安全事故以后，我反而觉得，公告本身不是最重要的验证方式。

真正重要的是三个东西：

钱还在不在。
提现能不能开。
开了以后能不能扛住真实的提款压力。

9 月 28 日，BTC 按计划恢复提现。

恢复后的早期阶段，Bitget披露已经处理 9,585 笔 BTC 提现，总计约 4,098.036 BTC；ETH、USDT以及其他资产随后按照时间表逐步恢复，而且官方明确表示恢复方案不区分 VIP，不给任何账户优先提现。(The Coin Republic)

我觉得这才是这次事件真正值得观察的地方。

因为安全事故之后，用户自然会产生一个最直接的行为：

“既然你说我的钱没问题，那我现在就把钱提出来试试。”

这其实就是一次真实的压力测试。

至于这是不是所谓的“挤兑”，我不会急着下结论。

但至少可以确认，提现恢复后确实出现了非常集中的提款需求，而系统已经开始承受这部分真实压力。(Bitcoin News)

然后就在这个时间点，Bitget上线了「同行计划」。

9 月 28 日至 10 月 26 日，活动周期4周。

平台拿出相当于**合格非机构用户实际留存净交易手续费收入30%**的金额进入奖池，其中60%按交易贡献分配，40%按资产贡献分配。

注意，这里的30%不是“平台所有手续费的30%”，最终奖励也不是固定收益，而是随着实际净手续费收入、用户交易量和合格资产规模动态变化。

所以我不会简单把它定义成“分红”。

更准确地说：

这是一次平台收入向用户重新分配的激励机制。

但它有一个很有意思的地方——

40%的资产奖励，并不要求你为了拿奖励不断增加交易量，而是按照合格资产的7天平均价值参与分配。

换句话说，它同时在奖励两类东西：

给平台创造交易收入的人，
以及愿意把合格资产留在平台的人。

当然，规则里也有不少限制：100 USDT平均每日有效交易量门槛、300万USDT的交易量计算上限，以及大量不计入的交易类型。最终奖励还取决于其他参与者的规模。

所以对于这次「同行计划」，我的看法比较简单：

它不是无风险收益，更不是让用户为了奖励去制造交易。

但如果本身就在使用 Bitget，有正常的交易和资产配置需求，那么在这个时间节点重新看一遍平台的利益分配机制，确实有研究价值。

尤其是把两件事情放在一起看：

一边是安全事故之后，平台需要重新建立用户信任；

另一边是平台把未来一部分实际产生的手续费收入拿出来，与参与者重新分配。

这两个动作放在一起，比单独看任何一份宣传文案都有意思。

交易所的信用最终不是靠一句“请相信我们”。

用户会用提现验证，市场会用资金流验证，时间会用下一次黑天鹅验证。

至于「同行计划」到底能不能算一笔有意义的“分红”，我觉得也不用急着下结论。

把规则、奖池、实际发放和后续资金情况持续摆出来看，答案自然会越来越清楚。

对交易所而言，安全事故之后最重要的从来不是把故事讲得多漂亮。

而是让用户能够把自己的钱，正常地存进去，也正常地拿出来。

这才是最硬的信用。

风险提示：数字资产价格波动及平台风险均较高。本文基于公开信息及活动规则进行个人观察，不构成投资、交易或资产配置建议。具体资格、奖励及结算以 Bitget 官方规则为准。

text:
晚上又迭代了一个版本，主要加入的是期权的低买、高卖保护。

主要功能就是花一部分权利金，买入看跌期权，减轻 BTC 大跌时的损失。代价是收到的净收入会减少，有时还需要额外付钱。

下面都按 1 BTC、相同到期日的美元计价线性期权举例，权利金是假设报价，不计手续费。

1. 低买保险：

例如，卖出行权价为 80,000 美元的看跌期权，再买入同到期、同数量、行权价为 75,000 美元的看跌期权。

假设卖出收 500 美元，买保护花 100 美元，净收 400 美元。

到期 BTC ≥ 80,000 美元：两张期权都没有需要支付的到期差额，赚取这 400 美元。

到期 BTC 跌到 70,000 美元：卖出的期权亏 10,000 美元，买入的保护期权收回 5,000 美元，再加上最初收到的 400 美元，合计亏损 4,600 美元。

如果继续下跌，两张期权新增的盈亏相互抵消。也就是说，在两腿正常结算、完整持有到期的前提下，这个组合的最大亏损是：

80,000 − 75,000 − 400 = 4,600 美元。

这叫看跌信用价差。拿出一部分原本能收到的权利金，给到期亏损设定一个上限。

2. 高卖保险：

例如，持有 1 BTC，愿意在 90,000 美元卖出，于是卖出这个行权价的看涨期权收钱，同时买入同到期、覆盖 1 BTC 的 75,000 美元看跌期权。

假设建立组合时 BTC 是 84,000 美元，卖出看涨期权收到 500 美元，买入看跌期权花掉 100 美元，净收 400 美元。

下面的盈亏，都从建立组合时这枚 BTC 价值 84,000 美元开始计算。

如果到期 BTC 涨到 100,000 美元：

持有的 BTC 增值 16,000 美元，但卖出的看涨期权需要支付 10,000 美元差额，买入的看跌期权到期没有赔付。

加上最初收到的 400 美元，最终盈利：

16,000 − 10,000 + 400 = 6,400 美元。

即使 BTC 再往上涨，覆盖部分的新增现货收益也会被看涨期权的新增亏损抵消，到期利润上限仍是 6,400 美元。

如果到期 BTC 还是 84,000 美元：

现货价值没有变化，两张期权都没有到期差额，最终赚取净收到的 400 美元。

如果到期 BTC 跌到 60,000 美元：

持有的 BTC 亏损 24,000 美元，但 75,000 美元的看跌期权可以补偿 15,000 美元，卖出的看涨期权到期不需要支付差额。

再加上最初收到的 400 美元，最终亏损：

24,000 − 15,000 − 400 = 8,600 美元。

BTC 跌破 75,000 美元以后，保护期权会抵消对应数量现货的进一步下跌损失。因此，这个组合持有到期的模型最大亏损是 8,600 美元，最大盈利是 6,400 美元。

这叫领口组合：通过限制一部分上涨收益，换取下跌保护。75,000 美元到 84,000 美元之间的下跌，仍然需要自己承担。

这里的“保险”都是期权保护，并不保本。

上述上限只适用于组合完整持有到期、正常结算的情况，实际还要考虑手续费和保证金。

晚上花了很长时间把双币和期权的功能迭代好了，目前已经是一个可用的版本的了。

首先因为要读取 Binance 和 Okx  的双币数据，所以需要接入这两个交易所的 API ，我强烈建议用小号或者是子账户的 API ，并且只开放只读功能，能读取到数据就可以。而 Deribit 是不需要 API 的。

现在这个版本对我来说最直接的优势就是节省了我还要一个个的打开 APP ，而是在网页端直接可以看我需求价格下哪家交易所给的利息最高，而且可以通过和期权的对比知道我被扣除了多少“手续费”。

甚至我可以直接在 Deribit 组我自己的双币策略。

版本目前实现的功能：

1. 持有 USDT，通过“低买双币”收取收益

选择自己愿意买入 BTC 的价格，在等待期间赚取双币票息。系统显示本期预计收款、接币后的有效成本，以及 BTC 跌到什么价格开始亏损，帮助你判断这笔收益是否值得承担接币风险。

2. 持有 BTC，通过“高卖双币”增加收益

选择自己愿意卖出 BTC 的价格，赚取持币期间的双币票息。系统计算有效卖价，并比较“做双币”和“继续持有 BTC”的结果。

3. 对比 Binance 和 OKX，挑选同等条件下给得更多的产品

集中查看两家的目标价、到期日、年化和本期收益。对相同方向、目标价和到期条件的产品进行比较，按投入金额计算预计收款，减少来回切换平台和手工计算。这是提高报价选择效率。

4. 通过期权报价，判断双币的收益是否划算

将选中的双币与相同行权价、方向和到期时间的期权对照，查看双币票息与卖出期权权利金的差异。接入 Deribit 行情、盘口和可视化图表，并提供 Binance 期权相关比较。这能帮助判断“交易所这款双币给得是否合适”。

5. 评估用期权组合，自建类似双币的收益结构

当前提供两类测算：准备现金卖出看跌期权，以及持有 BTC 卖出看涨期权。系统计算合约数量、预计净权利金、资金预留和不同到期价格下的盈亏，再与双币和直接持有比较。自建模型目前基于 Binance USDT 期权。

6. 跟踪“低买接币—高卖换回 USDT”的连续操作

登记实际到账后，可以把结算结果带入下一笔测算：收到 BTC 后评估高卖，收到 USDT 后评估低买。历史记录支持核对累计投入、票息、费用和剩余 BTC 的回本价格，判断整轮操作究竟赚了多少利息。

7. 用实际到账复盘

支持历史表格导入、到期待办、实际收款登记，以及按平台、方向和时间统计盈亏；还能比较是否跑赢直接持币或持有 USDT。预期收益与实际到账分开，模拟交易不计入真实收益。

配套已支持报价自动刷新、完整产品列表。

text:
I spend an embarrassing amount of my day doing this:

- ask ChatGPT about something
- check the market
- go back to ChatGPT
- open the exchange
- check the pair
- repeat

So MEXC now building a CLI that connects the AI I’m already using 

with supported MEXC capabilities actually makes a lot of sense to me.

The idea is pretty simple, let me explain:

You can use a compatible AI Agent like ChatGPT or Claude, explain what you want in normal language, review the information and parameters, and MEXC CLI connects that workflow with the MEXC actions it supports.

So imagine I notice a token suddenly moving.

Instead of treating my AI research and my exchange like two completely separate tools
set the parameters

I can now include the supported @MEXC workflow from there.

The AI still isn’t deciding whether I should make the trade.

(Unfortunately I remain responsible for my own bad decisions)

It just removes some of the stupid friction between having an idea and actually doing something with it.

And I think this is probably where AI in trading becomes genuinely useful.

This is a really interesting feature made by MEXC

今天亚洲时段，十年期美债收益率仍在 5.23% 附近，处于 2007 年以来的高位。能源通胀和美国债务的压力还在，投资者要求更高的收益，才愿意持有长期国债。

美伊这边，双方已经在周一分别与调解人沟通，后续讨论围绕伊朗提出的七天方案的修改版本展开。伊朗外长表示，仍在等待美国对最新停火和恢复霍尔木兹海峡通航条件的回应。与此同时，川普隔夜公开否认已经向伊朗提出制裁减免和解冻资金的条件。

油价也继续受到供应担忧而缓慢上涨。中东原油出口虽然有所恢复，但部分运输仍依赖船对船转运等安排，效率更低、成本更高，距离正常供应还有差距。

从这个情况来看，油价即使不再大幅上涨，只要长时间维持在高位，运输、生产和居民日常支出的成本就会继续受到影响。如果这些成本不断向其他商品和服务传导，美联储继续收紧政策的压力也会增加（加息概率上升）。

而十年期美债收益率维持在 5.23% 附近，意味着长期融资成本已经在给经济施加压力。企业借新钱、偿还到期债务会更贵，居民贷款消费的负担也会加重。对美股和 bitcoin:native 来说，更高的美债收益率也提高了资金承担风险的门槛，投资者需要看到更好的回报前景，才愿意增加风险敞口。

今天最重要的就是美国是否愿意和伊朗进行霍尔木兹开放的谈判，伊朗外交部长已经公开表示，希望美国可以在周二给出明确答案。

quoted_text:
Hi,

Tomorrow we are re-opening the Pro $200 subscriptions to new subscribers, but together with it we are also changing how we calculate the usage for it. In effect, if you do the math, it will net out at half the dollar in API spend compared to the old Pro $200 plan. 

Now that it's said, let me explain why this is happening and why you will still get more work done than if you were on the Pro $200 subscription one month ago.

(a) We didn't want to compromise in other ways and are committing to not reintroducing the 5h limit, so that you can fully use the weekly usage when you want.
(b) On the subscription, we guarantee that over time you always get more work done and with an increasing level of quality. This means that you will continue to get more value per dollar spent as a result of models getting more efficient and us passing down the improvements in the form of API price reductions.
(c) We don't want to put an incentive on ourselves to artificially inflate the API list prices to make it look like you are getting a lot (and workaround it through discounts, etc). Instead we want to continue to both rapidly reduce prices and increase capabilities of models on the API. This week we introduced GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna at 50% of their previous price. Over time, we see prices go low enough that it makes sense for most to buy usage as needed without there being a significant gap between what you get in a subscription and what you get in the API for a dollar spent.
(d) Tomorrow, we are adding more things to the subscription that won't draw on the usage, I won't reveal what that is yet.

I wanted to be transparent before all the big announcements tomorrow. Lots of new exciting things are coming to the subscriptions that will make it super compelling, but I wanted to make sure to share this change ahead of time so you can all understand it before we shower you with good news.

Codexingly,
Tibo

author: euler_mab
quoted_text:
The chief economist at Apollo is warning that mass adoption of AI agents could trigger a bank run as they optimize user investments. Gary Gensler spent his last few years as SEC chair warning that the exact same problem will hit the markets: the pursuit of algorithmic perfection at scale destroys system stability. Personal-finance agents making simultaneous optimal decisions could potentially cause a massive flash crash. 

Agent acausal coordination, with no messages passed between them, will show up in a lot of places. Markets will get the big headlines, but huge numbers of clever advisors making very similar choices will impact all of human society. Capability gains make this worse, not better. The smarter the agents, the narrower the optimal path; and knowing that other agents see that exact same path lets them move together without talking to each other. Agents do not need to collude to act in unison. Thus, they break no human laws by doing so. Human laws were not written for this. They were not written for a lot of what is coming, and it is about to start happening very fast.

teams make the same mistake, over & over: they overcomplicate their product, and especially the way they communicate it.

attention gets more expensive every day. more products, more content, more people competing for the same audience.

you don’t have 10 minutes to explain why someone should buy. you have seconds.

they need to understand what it does, why it matters, what makes it different, and why it deserves THEIR money and has upside.

teams are biased. when you live and breathe a product, ofc everything starts to feel obvious.

it isn’t.

that’s why every word has to fight for its existence. product names, features, tweets, positioning… everything should make the product easier to understand.

great marketing is making something complicated feel so obvious.

if people have to work hard to understand your product, you’ve already lost the majority.

text:
一大早被Anthropic上市的新闻的新闻刷频了，要抢在OpenAI之前上市。

有一些值得注意的关键词：
估值超过 2万亿美元
挂牌时间更可能推迟到 11月美国中期选举之后
高增长高亏损并存

我将以目前已知IPO信息和之前的重要融资信息，来做一个整理：

1️⃣为什么要IPO？
核心原因还是钱不够花。根据披露的信息，其 2025 年实际收入接近 46 亿美元，同年剔除部分融资相关会计减记后的经营亏损仍超过 80 亿美元。
赚的越多，似乎也亏的越多。扩张、基建所需要的现金流是巨大的。scaling law依然奏效的当下，需要更多算力。

2️⃣为什么抢上市？
当然是在现金流充沛的时候IPO好拿钱，SpaceX已经抽走了一些，抢在OpenAI之前先拿到钱，很重要。
同时，Anthropic此前已经进行了多轮融资，在私募和战略投资者获得了大量资金。公开股权市场能提供更深的资金池。

3️⃣420亿亏损：
其中340 亿美元主要是“可转换融资工具的公允价值重估损失”。但剔除这项后，公司仍有超过 80 亿美元经营亏损。
简单说“340亿”就是：本质是公司估值上升了。公司以前为了拿到融资，发行了未来可能转换为 Anthropic 股票的工具；后来这些工具对应的股票权益变得更值钱，按相关会计处理，公司的负债或融资义务账面价值上升。

4️⃣营收一年12倍
Anthropic 的营收从 2024 年约 3.9 亿美元增至 2025 年接近 46 亿美元，约增长 12 倍。
同年计算与基础设施支出达到 73.3 亿美元，约为营收的 1.6 倍，占路透社所述 126.5 亿美元总经营费用的约 58%。

5️⃣改变命运的2026年
截至 2026 年 7 月底，Anthropic 的年化收入运行率超过 650 亿美元，OpenAI 超过 400 亿美元。但这些数字不代表两家公司已经分别实现了 650 亿和 400 亿美元的全年营收。
*年化运营率是取最近一段时间实际产生的收入，假设这个速度保持一整年，再换算成年收入。不等于最终的真实年收入。

author: teortaxesTex
quoted_text:
It's in both the American and the European strategic interest to stop ASML's DUVi exports to China.

But right now, Americans feel like they have no choice but to beat the Dutch into submission. That makes for a volatile standoff, and it could backfire on both sides: 

(1) The proposed MATCH Act nudges the Dutch to tighten controls fast, or else threatens to force them via the Foreign Direct Product Rule.

Many Europeans find it somewhat hypocritical that Americans are doing this while still shipping chips to China. They feel they're being asked to pay a commercial price for American strategic preferences that even the US admin isn't willing to pay.

Many Americans point out that the Dutch simply aren't moving fast enough, and that repeated attempts at friendly deals have failed. 

(2) The FDPR itself is controversial with allies; it's hard for any sovereign nation to accept that the US thinks it can regulate products anywhere in the world because they're made with American technology.

I think transatlantic relations are bad enough that, if a bill relying on the FDPR passes and becomes a political issue, European policymakers might become even more opposed to aligning. They might eventually lose, but winning will not exactly make future US-EU alignment against China more likely.

(3) There's a genuine revenue argument: if ASML has to stop exporting DUVi to China, they lose an important market. Eventually, we should fix this through creating European / allied demand, but that will take a while.

In the meantime, America could put some thought into sharing the financial burden that its own export controls impose on allies.

(4) Europe should want its SME chokepoints to be a geopolitical asset, or at least to seem like one. Having these chokepoints visibly and unilaterally be legislated over by the US Congress undermines that strategy and effectively disempowers US allies - which makes them more erratic and less reliable in the future.

Put differently: you really don't want to make SME exports a live issue in adversarial US-EU negotiations if you can help it, and both sides should realise as much.

China mustn't have access to DUVi imports, and Europe should take responsibility instead of being dragged there by the US. Other European governments should lean on the Dutch to cooperate, and Americans - despite their frustrations - should still try to offer the Dutch a better deal.

Hi,

Tomorrow we are re-opening the Pro $200 subscriptions to new subscribers, but together with it we are also changing how we calculate the usage for it. In effect, if you do the math, it will net out at half the dollar in API spend compared to the old Pro $200 plan. 

Now that it's said, let me explain why this is happening and why you will still get more work done than if you were on the Pro $200 subscription one month ago.

(a) We didn't want to compromise in other ways and are committing to not reintroducing the 5h limit, so that you can fully use the weekly usage when you want.
(b) On the subscription, we guarantee that over time you always get more work done and with an increasing level of quality. This means that you will continue to get more value per dollar spent as a result of models getting more efficient and us passing down the improvements in the form of API price reductions.
(c) We don't want to put an incentive on ourselves to artificially inflate the API list prices to make it look like you are getting a lot (and workaround it through discounts, etc). Over time, we see prices go low enough that it makes sense for most to buy usage as needed without there being a significant gap between what you get in a subscription and what you get in the API for a dollar spent.
(d) Tomorrow, we are adding more things to the subscription that won't draw on the usage, I won't reveal what that is yet.

I wanted to be transparent before all the big announcements tomorrow. Lots of new exciting things are coming to the subscriptions that will make it super compelling, but I wanted to make sure to share this change ahead of time so you can all understand it before we shower you with good news.

Codexingly,

text:
再谈加密钱包技术闲聊（分享给刚入门的朋友 ）：
Passphrase，
也就是大家常说的第 25 个助记词，属于高级钱包管理功能。它并不是什么新技术，早在 2013 年 9 月，就随 BIP39 提案一同诞生。

过去很长一段时间，大家认为 24 位助记词本身安全性足够，Passphrase 也就显得比较鸡肋，大多只有追求极致安全的加密社区极客才会去用。但随着 AI 算力发展，密钥暴力推演的门槛持续降低，这项古老的功能，重新被大家重视起来。

今天下午反复实测了 Ledger 与 OneKey 的 Passphrase 功能，二者底层都遵循 BIP39 标准，逻辑基本一致。 
谈一些我个人觉得需要注意的：
很多人会混淆「绑定第二 PIN」这个功能：这个 PIN 只是硬件钱包本机专属的快捷登录映射，不会改动你的 24 词助记词。
就算忘记这组新PIN、或者钱包硬件损坏了，只要保存好 24 助记词 + Passphrase，就可以在任意支持 BIP39 Passphrase 的钱包（跨品牌硬件Trezor/ledger/Onekey / 部分 App 钱包，例如 TokenPocket）完成资产恢复。

除了抵御助记词被暴力枚举的风险，它还有一个经典的胁迫安全场景：币圈常有线下聚会，如果极端情况遭遇胁迫、被索要助记词，你可以被迫交出主钱包的 24 词。绑匪拿到助记词，只能访问没有大额资产的主钱包；真正存放核心资产的隐藏钱包，必须额外输入 Passphrase 才能打开。

我认为币圈的朋友都可以了解下这套「24+1」的机制：它可以在助记词泄露 / 被枚举破解/胁迫不安全的场景下，增加一道坚固的防护。 
今年夏天比特币社区知名的 Coldcard 事件，硬件随机数发生器出现漏洞，大量用户助记词被暴力算出，造成上亿美金资产损失。试想，如果当时这些用户配置了高强度 Passphrase，结局会完全不同。

Passphrase 支持自定义，长度可以拉得很长，大小写字母、数字、符号都能组合。 曾经我也觉得这项功能比较鸡肋，单纯认为 24 词助记词就足够安全。但看完这次 RNG 漏洞事件，不由得思考：今天有硬件随机数缺陷，未来伴随 AI 算力爆发，私钥推演的门槛只会越来越低。

BIP39 Passphrase，真的是一项伟大的设计。
Hail 自托管！#BTC #Onekey #Ledger #tokenPocket

text:
Seeing a lot of confused posts from people who read that
> NEAR offers confidential balances
> NEAR Intents stopped the Bitget hacker's money

How can BOTH be true??

Easily. The door is public. The room is private.

Public: the deposit that puts money in, and the withdrawal that takes it out. Both are ordinary transactions on Ethereum, Tron or Bitcoin, visible to you, me, Arkham and every analytics firm alive.

Private: everything between those two events. Your balance, your trades, your routes, your counterparties.

Near SHIELD works at the door. It read a public deposit address, matched it against stolen-funds intelligence half the industry already shares, and declined. Nothing confidential was opened to do that. Being refused at a door tells you nothing about what is inside the room.

There is also a viewing key mechanism and a compliance council that can open one specific account when law enforcement brings evidence. It exists, it is documented, and it is not what stopped this. The money never got past the door.

Privacy that cannot tell the difference between you and the people who took $387M out of Bitget is not a stronger product. It is a lazier one.
author: zacodil
quoted_text:
Glad NEAR Intents froze part of the Bitget money. Not all of it, but a chunk with a path back to the people who lost it, and a much larger pile of attempted laundering that never got a quote at all.

Then I read the NEAR Intents write-up again and noticed it is not an operation report. It is a product launch, and the product is called SHIELD. Which is not new by the way, it caught the malicious Litecoin fork back in April.

Look at the shape of it. It names the system, lists its integrations, and pitches four audiences in a row. The part aimed at wallets is a compliance sell with a warning stapled on.

They could also have taken 5% of everything they froze, since Bitget put that bounty up publicly. NEAR Intents waived it, which maximises what goes back to users and, let's be honest, maximises the size of the announcement too. Both are true and I mind neither.

Because the product is genuinely interesting. Chainalysis, TRM and Elliptic sell detection. They tell you the money was dirty, usually once it is gone. SHIELD sits inside the venue, so it ships with a handle. It can refuse to quote, or stop a trade that is already running. Different product, different buyer: wallets, bridges, other venues, custodians, incident response firms.

So is this a new revenue line for NEAR? I hope so. I would like the team building it to grow, get funded properly, and keep being the ones called first when something goes wrong.

text:
Claude can help you build a game.

Give it access to Unreal Engine, Blender, and game-development skills, and you can go a lot further.

Here are 7 GitHub repos worth saving if you want to build games with AI.

Use them with a coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex, following each repo’s setup instructions.

1/ Awesome Gamedev Agent Skills

A collection of 73 skills covering Unity, Unreal, Godot, browser games, and more.

It gives your agent guidance for tasks like building an inventory, adding enemy behavior, creating save files, and making movement feel responsive.

The useful part: it picks relevant skills based on your engine and what you ask for.

Start here if your AI keeps producing code that ignores how your game actually works.

https://t.co/WudWTsajr7

2/ Three.js Game Skills

For building 3D games people can open in their browser.

Nine skills cover gameplay, graphics, menus, audio, assets, debugging, and release checks.

It includes a starter project and browser-testing templates. The README also links to playable demos, including a drifting game and a space dogfight.

Install it, then ask your agent to use “threejs-game-director” to build your idea.

https://t.co/OkZpJhvKnV

3/ Unreal MCP

Connects an AI assistant to Unreal Engine.

It exposes tools for placing objects, editing materials, working with Blueprints, adjusting lighting, creating particle effects, and controlling cinematic sequences.

A useful starting task: block out one small level, place the camera, and set up the lighting.

This requires Unreal and the repo’s plugin setup.

https://t.co/1dGWbYeSAW

4/ MCP for Unity

Gives your AI tools to work inside the Unity Editor.

It can create scenes and objects, edit C# scripts, manage assets, run tests, and build the project.

That gives you a workflow where the agent can make changes and check them inside the engine.

Useful for turning individual features into a playable prototype.

https://t.co/go63szyvru

5/ Godot MCP

Connects your AI agent to Godot.

It can create scenes, add objects, load sprites, launch the game, and read error messages.

That last part matters. When something breaks, the agent can inspect the actual error and work on a fix.

A good option for building a small game around one clear mechanic.

https://t.co/qXwHTtguqL

6/ MCP for Blender

For creating and changing the 3D objects that go into your game.

Connect it to Blender, then ask your AI to create objects, adjust materials, and arrange scenes.

It also supports asset sources including Poly Haven and Sketchfab, plus optional AI model-generation services.

Think props, buildings, furniture, and environment pieces. Check asset licenses and any external service costs.

https://t.co/n1xKro20HB

7/ Agentic Gamedev Skills

For the work that comes after “the game runs.”

This collection focuses on mini-games, with workflows for testing mechanics, tuning difficulty, adding sound, improving impact feedback, and catching browser crashes.

Useful when your prototype works but jumping feels weak, the rules are confusing, or one cheap trick wins every time.

https://t.co/wx8b2PRU3f

My suggestion: pick one engine, add the relevant skills, and build one small playable level.

Try this prompt:

“Build a five-minute playable demo of [idea]. Use the installed game-development skills and connected tools. Start with movement, camera, one core mechanic, and a clear win or lose condition. Run it and fix errors before adding more features. Then improve lighting, sound, feedback, and performance. Tell me what still needs human testing.”

AAA-quality work still takes art direction, good assets, optimization, and a lot of testing. No repo guarantees that.

But you can start with one room, one enemy, and one mechanic worth playing again.

What game have you wanted to build for years?

text:
Aave V4 deposits are growing quickly, now sitting at $1.33B across 8 hubs and 24 spokes.

The hub-and-spoke model is the key change in V4. Hubs act as a shared liquidity base, while Spokes are individual markets that can draw liquidity from a hub under their own risk settings. This solves three major problems:
1. Idle liquidity: Liquidity can be utilised across multiple spokes within the same hub, reducing fragmentation.
2. Market bootstrapping: Any spokes launched under a hub gain access to the same liquidity base as other spokes, rather than scaling from zero.
3. Risk Segmentation: Each spoke runs with independent parameters (collateral factors, access control, etc.), and the hub limits how much each spoke can add and draw through caps, helping contain the risk at the spoke level.

Two of the most interesting hubs listed at the moment are:
✦ @ether_fi cash on @Optimism, powering borrows for its users. It has reached $308m in deposits, with $34m in borrowed assets.
✦ @coinbase stocks on @base, which enables borrowing against tokenised equities. It has reached over $8m in deposits, with borrowing demand still in the early stages.

text:
$ENA 迎来最后一次大型的解锁
解锁的最后会是崩盘还是利空落地？

Ethena 官方在推特上宣布，从月底起，所有和 USDe 相关的 $ENA  激励与通胀归零。
这对持币的大家是好还是坏呢？

首先， $ENA 没有 USDe 所导致的通胀，代表这部分的新增抛压已经没了。
同时基金会也买断了大型投资人的锁仓代币，在 10 月 5 日一次性释放。之前是每个月释放到 2028 年。
除此之外，还迎来了新的回购机制，如果 USDe 供应量回到 75 亿美元以上，就会开始触发 $ENA 回购。

再看另一边，
USDe 供应量从高峰 150 亿美元跌到现在 50 亿美元以下。现在没有了 $ENA 的补贴，供应量会不会继续跌下去，没有人知道。
刚才讲的回购，其实门槛很高，大概是目前的供应量高出一半才会触发。在触发前，任何的计划都只是纸上谈兵。

所以，我觉得 10 月 5 日 会不会崩盘，其实没那么重要，
如果没有补贴后， USDe 的需求继续跌，一切都是伪命题。
author: sanyuanVC
quoted_text:
$ENA 一周拉盘超过 50 %
前几周才公布回购利好，现在又有新消息，大的要来了？

之前我们就聊过， Ethena 把加密货币和稳定币作为底层资产，
同时开合约做空，把价格波动对冲，然后发行 USDe 。
尤其是牛市，当全部人疯狂开多，Ethena 做空对冲，还吃一波资金费。

现在， Ethena 加入币安的 bStocks ，以同样的概念，赚合约的资金费率和基差。把它自身的套利范围从原本的加密货币到现在代币化股票。

 bStocks 在最近 6 个月内，平均年化超过 11 % 。
而最近 3 个月未平仓量平均每个月都增长 30 % 
币安还会降低 Ethena 的 ADL 优先级。
啥意思？
就是，当发生极端行情时候， 不那么容易轮到被自动减仓，减少极端行情下对冲仓位突然消失的风险。

现在的 RWA 已经不满足把美股上链，
直接用代币化股票来作为稳定币的抵押品。

回到 Ethena ，
之前我们也提出了一个疑问，当熊市来了，资金费没那么高了，Ethena 何去何从？

Ethena 对此给出一个很好的答案，
现在的 Ethena 已经不是单靠加密市场资金费率，
代币化美股的加入，让它又多了一个收入来源，
或多或少都可以减低对加密市场资金费的依赖，穿越牛熊周期。

text:
Bridges got commoditized. @zord4n, CEO of @jumperapp, says order books are on the same path:

"Order books are very akin to bridges three, four years ago."

"There are going to be a lot more of them, very specialized, every asset issuer with its own. So why would a user be cemented into one? There are always differences in fees, slippage, funding rates across venues."

"What's missing is the UX layer that combines them, the same model as bridge aggregation. You inherit the liquidity of any order book, but compete on UX: a unified margin account across all of them, with one-click strategies."

"The bet: in the next two years, more specialized order books pop up, and there'll need to be an aggregation layer that unifies them."

一个真正去中心化、已经能自己运转的协议，就算拿赚到的钱回购 Token，也不能因为回购会抬高 Token 价值这件事，直接被 SEC 当成证券。

这事对行业最大的影响，是 DeFi 终于可以更认真地谈价值捕获了。

第一个影响是：

现在对成熟、去中心化的协议来说，手续费 → 协议收入 → 回购/销毁 → 减少供应这条路的监管不确定性下降了一截。

以后市场看 DeFi，TVL 和 APY 可能越来越不够用了，协议赚多少钱、能拿多少真钱持续买回自己的 Token，会变得更重要。

第二个影响是：去中心化开始直接影响 Token 能不能吃到协议现金流。

团队如果还控制多签、财库、升级权限和经济模型，依然很难套这条逻辑。

美国证券交易委员会以后项目放掉控制权，可能不只是为了喊一句我们很去中心化，它会直接关系到回购、销毁、费用回流这些 Tokenomics 能做到什么程度。

所以接下来回购销毁也是一条主线，会有大量的协议将进行销毁。

text:
Moving a token across chains is only half the job. For a bank, the permissions need to arrive with it.

Think of a tokenized fund moving between blockchains.

The issuer still needs to check who can receive it, who approves the transfer, and how much settlement risk is acceptable.

And now @chainlink CCIP 2.0 brings those controls closer to the transfer itself.

Announced live on September 28, Chainlink’s upgrade combines additional verification, programmable compliance, and configurable transfer speeds. Think of a bridge with an issuer-controlled security desk.

Here’s what changes.

Institutions can add their own Cross-Chain Verifiers, or CCVs, alongside Chainlink’s default verification.

Under this additive model, both Chainlink’s committee and the required additional verifiers must sign before execution. An issuer could require extra approval for transfers above $1 million.

Through Chainlink’s Automated Compliance Engine, issuers can apply identity checks, sanctions screening, and transaction limits.

The practical appeal is carrying asset rules across networks without rebuilding every integration.

Speed becomes configurable too. Full source-chain finality remains the default. Faster-than-finality transfers require explicit opt-in across the relevant components. That means executing sooner while accepting the risk that the source blockchain’s recent history changes.

One interesting detail: CCIP 2.0 will support the Ethereum Fast Confirmation Rule (FCR), when FCR launches.

How does this compare with other cross-chain solutions?

@LayerZero_Core already lets applications choose verification networks and configure required signatures and optional thresholds. Customizable verification is therefore not unique to CCIP.

@wormhole’s core messaging uses attestations signed by 13 of 19 Guardians. Some chains use delegated observation, so the underlying trust assumptions also depend on the chain.

CCIP’s strongest pitch is the combination of default Chainlink verification, additional issuer controls, and integrated compliance tooling. Institutions get a more coordinated package.

The tradeoffs however, remain real.

Extra required verifiers can introduce delays or block transfers when unavailable. Poorly configured policies can reject legitimate users. Faster execution can leave tokens unbacked if a source-chain reorganization invalidates the original transfer.

CCIP 2.0 is a meaningful upgrade for regulated assets. Its success should be measured by sustained usage, reliable execution, and integration costs.

NFA. DYOR.

text:
大家最近没注意到的一个 SEC 的细节更新，可能会影响这波版本强势的“代币回购”叙事。

SEC 官方一直设有一份关于“加密资产是否属于证券”的指导问答（FAQ），这也是各大律所和项目方用来规避监管雷区的“红宝书”。

根据海外加密记者 @EleanorTerrett  的爆料，SEC 公司金融部在 9 月 28 日更新了关于代币回购的 FAQ。修订后的核心是：

针对代币回购，加了四个字的豁免前提，即“没有中心方（no central party）”才行。

它的意思是，只有当回购是由链上代码自动执行，且没有任何单一实体可以干预时，这种安排才不构成违规的证券发行。

但如果回购背后还有一个基金会或核心团队在开会拍板，并且大张旗鼓地宣传“给持币人分红”，这就会被监管视为危险的收益承诺。

这道界限如果生效，会直接将当前的几十个回购标的分成两拨：

一类是协议机制派（如 $HYPE、$UNI）。它们的回购资金流向无私钥地址或直接销毁，全程由底层参数驱动，没有团队干预。这种真正“无人操盘”的机制，在本次更新中获得了极大的合规安全垫。

另一类是团队主导派（如 $PUMP、$ENA 以及各类新发代币）。只要回购额度还需要实体开会决定，本质上依然是“科技公司在分配利润”。这精准踩中了 SEC 想打击的管理红线。

所以之后在评价一个代币的回购是否具有稳健基本面时，可能还要考虑回购资金从哪来、谁能修改规则，以及是否包含了收益承诺。

quoted_text:
Wake up, folks. Commodities are telling you something, and yesterday the Treasury confirmed it.

Scarcity in the physical world. Repression in the financial one.

Scarcity pushes prices up. Repression holds yields down. The gap between them is the debasement.

Commodities are the only asset class that wins on both sides.

The structural case for commodities has been turbo charged. Underinvestment, deglobalization and electrification all pushing markets like diesel cracks and copper to new highs.

Meanwhile the chokepoints are increasing, from Hormuz to the Red Sea, the Rhine, the Panama Canal, the Black Sea grain corridor and Russian refining capacity. It is becoming increasingly apparent that not a single one of those is reachable by anything in Washington's toolkit whether it be caused by war or weather.

The illusion of abundance is likely behind us. I said as much on CNBC this Monday, and I got long gold, silver and agriculture last week.

Ten points for you to consider. (1/11)

Long and $AI are the ceiling for Memefi.

Stonk was just a catch-up trade for Solana. Although fundamentally different, the Stonk eco can't thrive unless AI and @longdotxyz move first. 

AI is the de facto Long token, so Long’s growth feeds directly into AI’s narrative. And the next catalyst for both likely comes from Robinhood itself.

With the Hood Summit today, shortly after regulatory developments around tokenized stocks, onchain voting rights, and derivatives, we are all waiting for the main character to make the next move.

The truth is, Vlad and Robinhood started this onchain summer pump with their talks of memes and RWAs. Solana, Base, and others are just beta plays. If Vlad and company are the true leaders, they will make the next move.

Vlad has been on a press tour recently, talking about the growth of stock derivatives in the market as something they did not expect. I suspect this was a white lie. I think they knew what they were doing. They knew that meme LPs would bootstrap the liquidity required to make their chain more attractive.

According to @Kairos_Res, every $1 of stock paid into Long pools was followed by roughly $1.90 of new minting of that same stock within three days, and $2.80 within a week. Kairos estimates Long was behind roughly a fifth of the ~$160M in stock minted on the chain since July. Don’t you think that’s significant to Robinhood’s mission?

Vlad can go into meetings and on air and say, “Hey, look at how much we’ve grown in such a short time.”

While Stonk primarily gives away its fees, Long compounds liquidity and strengthens the RWA chain. Perhaps it’s in Robinhood’s best interest to support and grow the very launchpad that helps them reach their ultimate goals.

Maybe they already have.

We know top projects have NDAs with Robinhood right now, as Al Dunlap of NET confirmed yesterday. It wouldn’t surprise me if @Natan_benish and his team were also under an NDA, knowing what may come next.

Something is brewing behind the scenes; I just can’t prove it yet.

author: LefterisJP
quoted_text:
Hi,

Tomorrow we are re-opening the Pro $200 subscriptions to new subscribers, but together with it we are also changing how we calculate the usage for it. In effect, if you do the math, it will net out at half the dollar in API spend compared to the old Pro $200 plan. 

Now that it's said, let me explain why this is happening and why you will still get more work done than if you were on the Pro $200 subscription one month ago.

(a) We didn't want to compromise in other ways and are committing to not reintroducing the 5h limit, so that you can fully use the weekly usage when you want.
(b) On the subscription, we guarantee that over time you always get more work done and with an increasing level of quality. This means that you will continue to get more value per dollar spent as a result of models getting more efficient and us passing down the improvements in the form of API price reductions.
(c) We don't want to put an incentive on ourselves to artificially inflate the API list prices to make it look like you are getting a lot (and workaround it through discounts, etc). Instead we want to continue to both rapidly reduce prices and increase capabilities of models on the API. This week we introduced GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna at 50% of their previous price. Over time, we see prices go low enough that it makes sense for most to buy usage as needed without there being a significant gap between what you get in a subscription and what you get in the API for a dollar spent.
(d) Tomorrow, we are adding more things to the subscription that won't draw on the usage, I won't reveal what that is yet.

I wanted to be transparent before all the big announcements tomorrow. Lots of new exciting things are coming to the subscriptions that will make it super compelling, but I wanted to make sure to share this change ahead of time so you can all understand it before we shower you with good news.

Codexingly,
Tibo

If you only chase the highest APR on your feed, you’re usually late to the wrong pool.

By the time a 2,000% stock LP is getting quote-tweeted, the liq is already thin, the age is 1–6 days, and most of that APR is just a small pool doing a lot of volume once.

What I look at first now is who actually paid LPs real dollars in the last 24 hours (can check it on @GeckoTerminal)

Sort by fees instead of APR :

HIMS/USDG did ~$17.7K fees on $5.9M vol; CRCL ~$14.7K.

Trading on 'fundamentals' seems easy, but what do you do when revenue starts dropping like this?

1) Hold
2) Sell
3) Buy the dip

Ok but consider that the token trades at 0.61x annualized fees and 1.22x annualized holder revenue.

Buy more? Yet these metrics are based on the last 30 days. Protocol is new.

But what if it belongs to a crypto category which historically is very cyclical, loses attention and gets flooded with new competitors?

Still 'cheap' valuation yet only if the PROTOCOL and revenue survive.

Yeah, trading the revenue meta looks easy when revenue only goes up.

But you still need to bet on:

1) The sector continuing to grow
2) The team continuing to ship
3) Degens continuing to trade
4) Competitors not taking its market share

The revenue is visible onchain in real time but decision to trade is still tough.

text:
메타 뮤즈 이용해서 개인 건강, 식단 관리 하는 팁.
다이어트 하고 싶은 사람들도 이거 활용하면 개꿀임.

이메일 검색하게 시켜서 과거 건강검진 결과표 연도별로 다운받아서 정리시켜놓고 분석하게 했음. 그리고 인바디 앱과 애플 헬스 연동시켜놓음. 그리고 메타 뮤즈와 애플 헬스를 연동 시킴.

그러면 이제 메타 뮤즈는 몇년치 내 건강검진 기록 내용을 알고 있는 상태이고 애플 헬스를 통해서 내 '수면', '걸음 수', '운동 세션', 'HRV,' 'VO2MAX', '심박수', '체중', '체지방율' 등을 '시계열 데이터'로 액세스하게 됨.

그리고 식단 관리 해달라고하면서 아침, 점심, 저녁, 간식 먹을 때 마다 저렇게 표로 정리하고 + 식단 입력할 때 마다 or 저녁 특정 시간에 애플 헬스 데이터도 읽어들여서 분석하고 조언해달라고하면 됨.

참고로 나처럼 애플 워치 같은걸로 수면 측정, 운동 측정을 꾸준히 한 사람들은 활용도가 높음. 난 런닝, 트레드밀, 천국의 계단, 산책, 수면, 심박수를 애플워치로 측정해왔고 약 12년치의 데이터가 있는 상태임. 

메타 뮤즈한테 식단 데이터 관리하고 매주 혹은 매월 단위로 '아티팩트'로 분석해달라고하면 보기좋게 시각화하고, 인터랙티브 차트 등으로 만들어달라고하면 주간/월간으로 매일 칼로리 적자가 어떠했는지 그에 따른 체중, 체지방율 변화도 체크할 수 있음.

아니면 아예 아티팩트 자체를 '입력형'으로 만들어달라고해서 아티팩트 메뉴에서 들어가서 입력하는 방법도 있음. 

그록봇이 성능이나 퍼포먼스는 더 좋지만, 메타 뮤즈처럼 애플 헬스 데이터 연동이 아직은 안되고, 인라인 시각화를 지원안해서 이런 점에서는 메타 뮤즈가 더 강점이 있음.

음식 뭐 먹었는지 대충 사진찍어서 보내도 되고 간략하게 말로 해놓으면되고, 이렇게 해두고 주간/월간으로 체크해보면 좋음

이거 말고도 여러 Wow moment가 있긴했는데, 이렇게 건강검진 내역 정리 + 식단 관리 하는 방법은 여성분들은 체중 관리, 다이어트에 도움이 될거고 운동하는 젊은 남성부터 건강관리해야하는 중년들까지도 모두 도움될거 같아서 공개함. 

애플 헬스 데이터 12년치가 진입장벽이려나?
근데 뭐 몇주, 몇달치 데이터만 있어도 지금부터 시작하면 됨.
건강검진 데이터도 못찾으면 몇년치는 수기로 직접 넣어주고.
관리하려면 이정도 노력은 들여야하지않나 싶음.

메타 뮤즈 한국에서 설치하는 방법?
인용원문 타고 들어가면 있음.

메타 뮤즈 활용법은 반응 좋으면 몇개 더 풀겠음.

Bitget正在承受第一波提币压力测试。在盗币事件发生后，Bitget第一时间关停提币，为全面排查争取时间。当然，这样势必会将挤兑压力推迟到恢复提现的时候。

根据Glassnode数据显示从27-28号期间，Bitget的BTC余额曲线陡然下降，共计减少了5,891枚BTC。

但即便如此，其余额仍然还有29,729枚，相当于回到了2025年10月的水平，情况不算特别严重。

同时，鲸鱼外流指数为0.027，这意味着在该滚动窗口内，从Bitget地址提到巨鲸实体的BTC约占当前余额的2.7%。（这里的巨鲸实体，指持有1000枚BTC以上，且不是交易所，也不是矿工的地址簇）。

该数值相比日常均值未见明显升高，说明在Bitget上的BTC鲸鱼们并未因此次盗币事件而集中恐慌，或对平台失去信任。

据此推测，当前大量提币的，多数应该还是散户群体的避险行为。

通常情况，第一波挤兑是最为凶悍的，后面只要确保安全的前提下逐步开放提币后，压力会逐渐减少。

我们可以实时关注数据的变化。也希望Bitget可以平稳度过自此危机，并保护所有用户的资产安全。

quoted_text:
上一次，Bybit被盗其实对BTC的直接冲击就不大。只是它恰好出现在市场需求开始走弱时，起了放大作用。

导致BTC大幅下跌的主要推手是关税引发的宏观避险情绪和ETF资金大幅流出（单日达创纪录的11.4亿美元）。

这次Bitget被盗金额仅为Bybit的四分之一，且被盗清单里没有BTC，对BTC的直接冲击大概率也会小于Bybit。

（根据Lookonchain公布的被盗明细一共9种资产：XRP，ETH，USDT，USDC，USD₮0，XAUt，BNB，AVAX和TRX）

我们可以把BGB作为此次事件最直接的风险指标。

它只比被盗前的价格低了3-5%，说明市场还是相信Bitget能吸收这次的全部损失。

Bitget官方声称其用户保护基金可以做到全额覆盖，这个基金是由3个地址里的5,500枚BTC构成。

即便是卖出这部分BTC来买回XRP和ETH，恢复1:1兑付，3.5亿美元的体量也就相当于BTC一天成交额的1%。

因此，我个人认为单独凭此意外事件要改变BTC的趋势，可能性不大。

不过有个细节值得关注：

Bybit当时没有关闭提现，10小时内处理了35万多笔提现请求，恐慌在第1天就被消化。

而Bitget选择暂停提现，充值和交易照常。那么挤兑压力测试，就被推迟到恢复提现的时候了。

Hi,

Tomorrow we are re-opening the Pro $200 subscriptions to new subscribers, but together with it we are also changing how we calculate the usage for it. In effect, if you do the math, it will net out at half the dollar in API spend compared to the old Pro $200 plan. 

Now that it's said, let me explain why this is happening and why you will still get more work done than if you were on the Pro $200 subscription one month ago.

(a) We didn't want to compromise in other ways and are committing to not reintroducing the 5h limit, so that you can fully use the weekly usage when you want.
(b) On the subscription, we guarantee that over time you always get more work done and with an increasing level of quality. This means that you will continue to get more value per dollar spent as a result of models getting more efficient and us passing down the improvements in the form of API price reductions.
(c) We don't want to put an incentive on ourselves to artificially inflate the API list prices to make it look like you are getting a lot (and workaround it through discounts, etc). Instead we want to continue to both rapidly reduce prices and increase capabilities of models on the API. This week we introduced GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna at 50% of their previous price. Over time, we see prices go low enough that it makes sense for most to buy usage as needed without there being a significant gap between what you get in a subscription and what you get in the API for a dollar spent.
(d) Tomorrow, we are adding more things to the subscription that won't draw on the usage, I won't reveal what that is yet.

I wanted to be transparent before all the big announcements tomorrow. Lots of new exciting things are coming to the subscriptions that will make it super compelling, but I wanted to make sure to share this change ahead of time so you can all understand it before we shower you with good news.

Codexingly,

近期 ethereum:0x7fc66500c84a76ad7e9c93437bfc5ac33e2ddae9 币价表现强劲，除了短期的行情走势，协议在业务端和经济模型上的重磅动作更值得关注。简单拆解一下 Aave 近期的核心动态与潜在影响：

1️⃣ 突破资产边界，美股抵押借贷率先落地

Aave V4 已在 Base 链上线 Equities Hub，支持符合条件的非美用户将 Coinbase 发行的 7 只代币化美股（$AAPL, $NVDA,$TSLA 等）作为抵押品借入 USDC。用户无需卖出美股仓位即可获取链上流动性。

创始人 Stani 更表示，未来抵押品将向太阳能、GPU、机器人甚至太空基础设施拓展，旨在为“富足经济”转型提供融资。

2️⃣ 风控谨慎与“跨市场跳空”风险

目前该功能处于早期阶段：风控参数极其保守（7 只股票总上限约 2900 万美元），资金利用率仅 5.34%。

需要警惕的是，传统美股交易时间与 DeFi 全天候运行存在“时间错位”，若美股周末休市期间发生重大事件，开盘跳空可能导致链上仓位瞬间清算，机制仍需持续验证。

3️⃣ 竞争加剧，Aavenomics 3.0 酝酿代币销毁

受此前 reETH 事件及内斗带来的信任危机影响，虽然 Aave 当前 TVL 已回升至 190.8 亿美元，但其在借贷与 RWA 市场的份额均有所下滑，每日协议收入也下降了约 39%。

为此，Stani 透露正考虑在 Aavenomics 3.0 中加入代币销毁机制，通过协议收入持续自动化回购并销毁 ethereum:0x7fc66500c84a76ad7e9c93437bfc5ac33e2ddae9 。不过，由于需要优先偿还债务和修复资产负债表，回购重启仍需时间。

💡 总结分析

DeFi 长期受制于优质底层资产供给不足。Aave 的尝试不仅是拓宽抵押品范围，更是验证传统金融资产（RWA）能否真正融入链上信用体系。如果这一模式成功跑通，资产端的极大丰富将为协议带来持续收入，并通过 3.0 的销毁机制直接赋能代币价值。

从借贷加密货币到接入现实万物，Aave 正在尝试重构 DeFi 的资产边界。

text:
Moving a token across chains is only half the job. For a bank, the permissions need to arrive with it.

Think of a tokenized fund moving between blockchains.

The issuer still needs to check who can receive it, who approves the transfer, and how much settlement risk is acceptable.

And now @chainlink CCIP 2.0 brings those controls closer to the transfer itself.

Announced live on September 28, Chainlink’s upgrade combines additional verification, programmable compliance, and configurable transfer speeds. Think of a bridge with an issuer-controlled security desk.

Here’s what changes.

Institutions can add their own Cross-Chain Verifiers, or CCVs, alongside Chainlink’s default verification.

Under this additive model, both Chainlink’s committee and the required additional verifiers must sign before execution. An issuer could require extra approval for transfers above $1 million.

Through Chainlink’s Automated Compliance Engine, issuers can apply identity checks, sanctions screening, and transaction limits.

The practical appeal is carrying asset rules across networks without rebuilding every integration.

Speed becomes configurable too. Full source-chain finality remains the default. Faster-than-finality transfers require explicit opt-in across the relevant components. That means executing sooner while accepting the risk that the source blockchain’s recent history changes.

One interesting detail: CCIP 2.0 will support the Ethereum Fast Confirmation Rule (FCR), when FCR launches.

How does this compare with other cross-chain solutions?

@LayerZero_Core already lets applications choose verification networks and configure required signatures and optional thresholds. Customizable verification is therefore not unique to CCIP.

@wormhole’s core messaging uses attestations signed by 13 of 19 Guardians. Some chains use delegated observation, so the underlying trust assumptions also depend on the chain.

CCIP’s strongest pitch is the combination of default Chainlink verification, additional issuer controls, and integrated compliance tooling. Institutions get a more coordinated package.

The tradeoffs however, remain real.

Extra required verifiers can introduce delays or block transfers when unavailable. Poorly configured policies can reject legitimate users. Faster execution can leave tokens unbacked if a source-chain reorganization invalidates the original transfer.

CCIP 2.0 is a meaningful upgrade for regulated assets. Its success should be measured by sustained usage, reliable execution, and integration costs.

NFA. DYOR.

这种情况下，单个协议拦一次，只能让黑客多花 10 分钟。

author: defidave
quoted_text:
The chief economist at Apollo is warning that mass adoption of AI agents could trigger a bank run as they optimize user investments. Gary Gensler spent his last few years as SEC chair warning that the exact same problem will hit the markets: the pursuit of algorithmic perfection at scale destroys system stability. Personal-finance agents making simultaneous optimal decisions could potentially cause a massive flash crash. 

Agent acausal coordination, with no messages passed between them, will show up in a lot of places. Markets will get the big headlines, but huge numbers of clever advisors making very similar choices will impact all of human society. Capability gains make this worse, not better. The smarter the agents, the narrower the optimal path; and knowing that other agents see that exact same path lets them move together without talking to each other. Agents do not need to collude to act in unison. Thus, they break no human laws by doing so. Human laws were not written for this. They were not written for a lot of what is coming, and it is about to start happening very fast.

Hi,

Tomorrow we are re-opening the Pro $200 subscriptions to new subscribers, but together with it we are also changing how we calculate the usage for it. In effect, if you do the math, it will net out at half the dollar in API spend compared to the old Pro $200 plan. 

Now that it's said, let me explain why this is happening and why you will still get more work done than if you were on the Pro $200 subscription one month ago.

(a) We didn't want to compromise in other ways and are committing to not reintroducing the 5h limit, so that you can fully use the weekly usage when you want.
(b) On the subscription, we guarantee that over time you always get more work done and with an increasing level of quality. This means that you will continue to get more value per dollar spent as a result of models getting more efficient and us passing down the improvements in the form of API price reductions.
(c) We don't want to put an incentive on ourselves to artificially inflate the API list prices to make it look like you are getting a lot (and workaround it through discounts, etc). Instead we want to continue to both rapidly reduce prices and increase capabilities of models on the API. This week we introduced GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna at 50% of their previous price. Over time, we see prices go low enough that it makes sense for most to buy usage as needed without there being a significant gap between what you get in a subscription and what you get in the API for a dollar spent.
(d) Tomorrow, we are adding more things to the subscription that won't draw on the usage, I won't reveal what that is yet.

I wanted to be transparent before all the big announcements tomorrow. Lots of new exciting things are coming to the subscriptions that will make it super compelling, but I wanted to make sure to share this change ahead of time so you can all understand it before we shower you with good news.

Codexingly,

text:
特朗普的中期选举，原油，美股、比特币那点事

特朗普还有五周时间
结束战争
把油价打下来
把美国十年期国债收益率打下来

三件事一件都做不到，他就输掉中期选举，输掉市场，输掉他的政治遗产

这三件事是一条链

战争 2 月底开打，现在是第七个月。开战初期伊朗实际上把霍尔木兹海峡的船堵了，布伦特原油从战前的 72 美元一度冲到接近 120，3 月单月涨 51%。9 月 25 日收在 104.32，比战前高 44%

油价是 CPI 里最直接的一项，油价不下来，通胀预期就下不来

然后是美联储，这一环最狠。市场原本预期 2026 年降息三到四次，结果 9 月 16 日美联储不但没降，还加息 25 个基点到 3.75% 到 4.00%，市场现在定价 10 月再加一次的概率 66%

十年期年初 4.19%，9 月 24 日冲到 5.23%，2007 年以来最高。这一环不全是油价的锅，美债短端通胀预期才 2.4%，十年期里 2.62% 是实际利率。真正的推手是供给，财政部三季度发 7390 亿的债，四季度还要发 6280 亿，AI 公司的资本开支靠发债，赤字占 GDP 6%

十年期是房贷的定价锚，房贷利率从 2 月的 5.98% 走到 9 月 28 日的 7.50%，美国消费者背着 19 万亿的债

最后进选票。特朗普的支持率，路透社和益普索是 32%，历史最低，NBC 平均是 39% 赞成、59% 反对，国会通用选票民主党领先 6 到 7 个点

11 月 3 日投票，今天算起 35 天。参议院共和党 53 比 47，民主党净赢 4 席翻盘。众议院共和党 222 比 213，民主党净赢 5 席翻盘。博彩市场给民主党全胜 50%，民主党拿众议院加共和党守参议院 36%

先说美股

中期选举本身不是主变量。1931 年以来，中期年平均涨 4.7%，其他年份 9.5%，是四年周期里最弱的一年。但中期选举之后的 12 个月是四年里最强的一段，1950 年以来平均涨 15.4%，18 次全部为正。中期年的低点历史上平均落在 8 月中到 9 月底，我们现在正站在这窗口上

真正压在美股身上的是十年期。标普的远期盈利收益率 3.892%，十年期 4.77%，风险溢价负 0.88%。意思是国债给的回报比股票的盈利收益率还高，这是极端高估区的读数，它直接压住估值扩张

所以只有一条线要盯，十年期 5.25%。过了这条线股债相关性反转，两个一起亏，现在 5.23%，刚摸到

中期选举能改变的是财政。众议院翻蓝，新支出过不去，发债压力下来，十年期反而有回落的动力。历史统计也支持，共和党总统加分裂国会，标普平均 13.7%，一党独大只有 6.7%

但黑石那边有个反例，一方丢掉三权独揽，中期选举后六个月反而更弱，10.4% 对 16.1%。而且 2026 年现在的结构和 2018、2022 一模一样，都是美联储在中期选举前加息，那两年标普都是负收益

美股的风险不在 11 月 3 日，在 10 月的议息和十年期。10 月再加一次、十年期站上 5.25% 并站住，标普要先跌一轮，然后才轮到中期选举后的季节性反弹。十年期退回 5% 以下，中期选举后 12 个月那 15% 的历史规律有机会重演

再说比特币

比特币 9 月这一周扛住了三件事，9 月 15 日 CLARITY 法案在参议院 49 比 50 被否，9 月 16 日美联储加息，日本央行加息到 31 年高位。结果从 74,888 涨到 87,402，涨 16.7%

但这波涨的构成要看清楚。一是空头被挤，约 7.5 亿美元的做空仓位被强平。二是 ETF 连续七天净流入，一周 23.9 亿美元，2025 年 10 月以来最强的一周

关键在节奏。单日流入从周一的 9.99 亿一路掉到周五的 1.345 亿，缩了 87%。这是脉冲，不是持续买盘

现在最要紧的数字是 86,000。这是美国现货比特币 ETF 的平均持仓成本，BTC 现价 84,000，整个 ETF 群体水下 2.3%。这个位置他们要么加仓要么离场，冲不上 86,000，ETF 就从买盘变卖盘

利率是硬约束，不生息的资产，机会成本在往上走

今年最扎心的一点：比特币距离 2025 年 10 月的高点还有 33%，同期黄金在历史高位。地缘冲突、赤字占 GDP 6%、通胀没下来，这一整套本该是比特币的主场，结果当对冲工具的是黄金，比特币走成了高贝塔科技股的影子

政策那条线，CLARITY 法案本会期基本死了，下届会期要从头提。但 SEC 和 CFTC 在用规则制定填空，Coinbase 的 CEO 说替代规则可能比法案更宽松。法案失败不等于行业利空落地

比特币被夹在 76,000 到 87,000 这个区间，上方是 ETF 成本线和宏观，下方是 ETF 流入和机构持仓。中期选举对它是次级变量，真正的开关还是 10 月美联储那一次和十年期。10 月再加息、十年期站上 5.25%，比特币回去测 76,000。油价继续跌、十年期退回 5% 以下，回 95,000 以上的路是打开的，而且 11 月到 12 月本来就是中期选举后历史上最强的一段

中美那八点共识把最大的地缘不确定性按住了一部分，这一点市场现在几乎没定价

text:
unpopular opinion: "permissionless" DOES mean "neutral"

it's the whole point of building something "permissionless"

love what @near_intents is building
just want to be clear about what NEAR intents is / isn't ↓

• NEAR Intents 1ClickAPI and MPC Network is NOT permissionless, as it requires permission to participate as a network node

• the message bus also requires SHIELD permission to transact on top of (which is granted by default, but can be arbitrarily removed at any time, as addressed in this article)

i'm not saying it's a bad product, btw

i have been a huge user, supporter, and advocate of NEAR Intents

it has its use/niche and is valuable for the vast majority of people + it addresses known pain points in crypto and makes our lives easier

but permissionless/neutral rails are also extremely valuable for many other reasons, especially because "unlawful user" (as @chronear said in another post) can sometimes be users who are just trying to be free and defend against State-level aggression:

• honest people from globally sanctioned countries
• people fleeing warzone and tyrannies 
• whistleblowers
• honest workers surviving prohibitive, cartelized environments
• victims of political persecution or unfair trials
• etc.

so, i'm glad NEAR Intents is building for its niche (high-efficiency, well-connected rails that addresses crypto fragmentation, KYC/custodial-heavy rails, etc); while other protocols are building for this other niche (permissionless and neutral rails that make no distinction and anyone can become a network peer)

both can (and should) coexist

onwards!

text:
NEWS: Verathos is consolidating under Subnet 96, bringing its hardware-proof and verified-inference work onto one network. @verathos_ai says the change creates a single path for operators, builders and holders.
https://t.co/UG6RL2fRKY
author: taodotcom
quoted_text:
For nearly three years, we have been working on one question from two directions. If you pay someone you do not know to run AI compute, how can you verify both the machine they claim to have and the work they claim to have done?

@nodexo was our answer at the hardware level. It challenged GPUs to prove what they were capable of and brought together a fleet of verified machines. 

Verathos took the question further, using proofs to check that the requested model ran and that the response a customer received was bound to that work.

We built them on separate subnets and kept Verathos unattributed deliberately. If we were asking people to judge a network by its evidence, we wanted Verathos to earn their confidence through its proofs and performance, not through our name.

Running both networks changed our understanding of the product. Nodexo had verified GPU capacity, but renting a whole machine left much of that capacity idle, while the people coming to us increasingly wanted to run models without managing hardware. Verathos serves those requests directly and its mesh; Sleipnir lets GPUs across machines work together on models that one machine could not hold alone.

The two networks had also begun to share more than an idea. Nodexo’s hardware classes and operators matched the supply Verathos needed, while the payment options we built for compute, including prepaid credits, x402 and conviction allowances, had made their way into inference. 

Keeping our work, operators and holders split across two subnets no longer made sense. So we are consolidating under Verathos on subnet 96. 

• For operators, the path is to prove the hardware, serve the model and prove the computation on one network. 
• For builders and agents, it is one OpenAI compatible API with proof metadata on responses and ways to pay with credits or per request. 
• For holders, it is one token connected to this work, with conviction turning locked alpha into a daily allowance of verified inference.

Subnet 106 will be handed to a new team, while our focus moves here; to building Verathos as a network that can put existing GPUs to work and give customers evidence of the inference they paid for.

SN96 $TAO

抛开他持仓 84 万枚 $BTC 的立场，视频中这 4 个基于数学和宏观环境的判断值得参考：

1. 明确的时间边界：从现在到 2035 年是最后的红利期。2035 年，99% 的比特币将被挖出。此后，BTC 的增长曲线将逐渐平缓，大约 20 年后，其年化收益将降至仅比标普 500 高 3-5 个点，超额收益期结束。

2. 下一个价格引擎：比特币货币化分为 ETF、财库储备、数字信贷和银行放贷四步。前三步已经发生，未来 36 个月的核心驱动力将是“银行放贷”——逻辑类似房地产，当银行开始接受 BTC 抵押放贷，资产价格才会被真正撬动。

3. 真实通胀的折算：普通人关注 3% 的 CPI（工业品通胀），而资金关注 15% 的“资本成本”通胀（稀缺资产的涨幅）。

4. 黄金的数学劣势：黄金每年约有 2% 的新增供给，这意味着储存在黄金里的购买力每 36 年会被稀释一半，而比特币的通胀最终趋零。

I wanted to be transparent before all the big announcements tomorrow. Lots of new exciting things are coming to the subscriptions that will make it super compelling, but I wanted to make sure to share this change ahead of time so you can all understand it before we shower you with good news.
