quoted_text:
many false dichotomies around this

you can't reap the benefits of being "early" if you're not willing to stomach the path it requires

many new folks don't get how this works, so a rough explanation is in order, as cross-chain stuff often comes up in crypto

an imperfect but useful analogy: near intents is to near what hyperunit is to hyperliquid

that is, it is not the chain itself, but a cross-chain protocol that augments the chain -- you can think of it as a collection of bridges + some other shit. but it is not part of consensus

a cross-chain protocol, for all chains, will always have more trust assumptions than the underlying chain -- unit for example also has OFAC screening as does pretty much anything of this nature

(your favorite defi or trading app on any chain also almost certainly fits this and even some validators, with few exceptions)

this is almost always true for anything that's not the main chain itself, as most cross-chain protocols are generally secured by MPC networks (or multisigs) and MPC clusters are by definition smaller than core validator clusters

and this remains true of all connective tissue, e.g., recall how Arbitrum multisig froze the funds of NK hacker a few months ago

that of course did not affect the "moneyness" of Ethereum as that is Arbitrum and not ETH on Ethereum itself

same thing here

I am not aware of any system that can function much differently on risk parameters today (though I can think of a few who lie about it who get called out by zach every few months)

the aspiration of course is that over time MPC networks (or multisig governance in the case of rollups) get decentralized enough to reduce the concentration of influence and minimize it to only provable bug patches and asymptotically zero human judgement 

that is fundamentally what you are underwriting

this is a big reason why Solana seeks to concentrate everything internally on a giant chain so that bridge trust risk is minimized (though in practice, this is only half the picture since for example RWAs fundamentally have control authority with the issuer itself, that's why USDT can be frozen on any chain)

so, there are three paths here:

i) you transact on the main chain itself with only the native asset of the chain, i.e ZEC on Zcash, BTC on Bitcoin, SOL on Solana

this is maximal risk reduction, but obviously limiting for anything beyond SoV or payments

ii) you do your bridging via CEXes

fine, but very large tradeoffs for asset selection, withdrawal/deposit limits, KYC, accessibility, privacy and you get way worse freezing/trust problems

iii) you do your bridging via crypto-native protocols that are relatively less decentralized than an entire blockchain itself but are improving security and decentralization constantly, especially against CEXes

for crypto to become a truly planetary economy, iii) must work. this is not a choice, it's just a matter of who wins that segment

but the only way iii) can work is if such protocols survive long enough to not get shut down by the feds because then the exchanges will default win and that aspirational future for crypto will be entirely lost

a valid criticism here is that this should have already been maximally decentralized already, but ofc that comes with its own tradeoffs like being too slow to patch bugs or add features in a relatively nascent stage

again, your job is underwriting the execution risk. and you must do so while understanding the parts at play

昨天和路人蝙@lurenbian 老师聊了聊现在crypto安全的两个百亿美金级别的痛点和我们构想的解决方案：

一个是传统安全攻防是以周甚至月份为单位，项目方，安全公司有足够的时间发现漏洞，审查，修复。就我们的经验来说，一般会持续两周左右。

而在有了AI之后这个时间迅速坍塌到了小时甚至分钟级别。六月份的时候Anthropic的模型就可以在3小时左右复刻18个火狐的漏洞。

因此过去的那套审查，汇报，验证，修复的流程一定会走向消亡。AI时代的攻击和防御一定都是以Agent为主体。因此我认为一种事先授权agent进行白帽救援，留下5-10%赏金的agentic safe harbor会是可选的方案。

通过在链上7*24小时不断的运行，发现漏洞，救援，留下部分赏金作为云计算和模型推理成本，我们能够实现一个完全自主防护的系统。 这也是和Walter @lclwalter 聊下来的结果。

另一个方面就是OPSec，运维安全。今年以来我们见识到越来越多的安全事件并不是代码出现纰漏，而是在多签管理，供应链安全，云服务器部署等被攻破。例如最近的bitget 超过3亿美金被黑，bybit的15亿多签被黑，drift恶意授权等等。

但事实是，OPSec基本不会被大家认真对待，也没有一个标准的流程。在这个方面我们急需建立一套标准，能审查运维中的单点风险，权限最小化。确保最坏情况下一个签名者也不能把整个金库转移走。

这两方面都是我们团队异常关心的问题，也是我们在和项目方，生态伙伴一起探索解决的方向。如果大家有什么想法，欢迎随时留言。

quoted_text:
时间线上已经没什么人聊山寨了。

前两天发了BTC的看法之后，好几个朋友私信过来聊山寨。说实话我理解，BTC的方向大家心里多少有数，但手里那些山寨怎么办，没人讲。

我自己的感受是，经过这轮周期，再看山寨不能只看叙事了。牛市里人人都会讲故事，熊市一来叙事全部归零。但有一个东西装不了：回购。嘴上说Building不花钱，真金白银从市场上买自己的币，得掏真钱。

所以我简单整理了一个维度：回购强度。累计回购金额 ÷ 流通市值。不看谁花的钱多，看谁敢把市值买穿。

排出来第一名。Raydium，累计回购1.99亿美元，流通市值1.69亿。回购金额超过了市值本身。117.5%。

Pump 36.7%，累计4.14亿，绝对金额也不小。Jupiter 17.2%，Meteora 15.5%，Solana系占了前几名。

但如果只看绝对金额，画风完全变了。Hyperliquid砸了11.9亿美元回购，所有项目里最多，但市值128亿，回购强度只有9.3%。

两个数字讲的是完全不同的故事。

翻数据的时候注意到排第五的deBridge，14.3%。去看了一下它基金会的Reserve Fund页面，

有个细节几乎没见过各位博主提。协议100%的收入全部用于回购和积累DBR，不是"拿利润的XX%回购"，是全部。

目前基金会持有6.38亿枚DBR，占总供应量6.38%，另外攒了1276万USDC手续费。一个流通市值不到9000万的项目，国库总资产3100万。

在没人聊山寨的时候，有些项目在用真金白银表态。这种表态值多少钱说不好。但总比嘴上喊Building实际在卖币的强。

我个人持有 $DBR ，以上不构成投资建议。

text:
Five and a half years ago, @crispheaney, @bigz_pubkey, @davijlu and I set out on a weird, winding, and wonderful journey to build a perpetual futures exchange. The crypto market structure was extremely immature then. Perps were just starting out, most DeFi users were paying $200 to execute a single transaction on Ethereum. We were one of the first to bring a fully on-chain perpetual DEX to market and launched for the first time on Solana in November 2021.

Today, as the exchange relaunches and enters its next chapter, I'm stepping down from Drift, now @VelocityDEX.

I'm extremely proud of what we built – one of the largest exchanges on Solana with over $150B traded. Chris and Z, our technical cofounders, led the technology front to build every piece of the exchange stack, while David and I put together an incredible and experienced growth and operational team. I poured my heart, soul, and many years of the most insane ups and downs into building and growing Drift – a gruelling, but immensely fulfilling journey. In many ways, it felt like my first child.

This April, we faced a state-level attack by DPRK, after a long-planned six months of social engineering infiltration. Going through it and the aftermath was by far the worst week of my life.

Within ten sleepless nights, we closed a deal with Tether that put users on a path to recovery. We hired @redacted_noah, ex-head of protocol engineering at Helium, to lead the rebuild of Velocity’s smart contract technology, a difficult task he took on enthusiastically and with zest. We brought on @namanmtl, who joins us from Binance and Trust Wallet to lead Growth and Recovery to grow our trader base for the relaunch. I am proud of my team who stepped up to take initiative above and beyond – especially @tracybbd who personally took the pains to speak to every single trader and market maker on the exchange.

Over the next few months, the team refused to quit and hunkered down to rebuild the exchange with a full security upgrade. Designing DFX as well as coordinating on multi-nation asset recovery working alongside @zeroShadow_io and local law enforcement agencies to freeze assets was a huge feat. This week, Velocity finalized their audit by @osec_io and @asymmetric_re and fully open-sourced the exchange. After a long and arduous journey, with many security audits in tow and with massive effort from the team, the exchange relaunches today – even better and faster than before.

I would like to shout out the incredible team that will be carrying on the Velocity product. @davijlu, along with Foundation, will continue to move on the asset recovery and law enforcement work. @redacted_noah will continue to build out Velocity’s technology, shipping new features like CLOB and Prop AMM that will make the product even better and smoother. @Defioppa, who previously led product at Binance, will continue to lead the product at Velocity. @tracybbd will lead partnerships and stakeholder relationships. @namanmtl will join us from his extensive background at Binance to lead growth.

With a heavy heart, I fully own this decision to step down. I have always done my best work building from zero to one. Velocity is now at the stage where it needs operators who can take it from one to ten, and I trust this team to take it to the next level. It is the right decision for me and for the protocol, to open a new chapter for Velocity.

I've been all in on crypto, my whole career since I was 19. Now I will be spending energy on exploring what’s next for me personally. I care about building bridges between Asia and the US, between digital and physical infrastructure, and about bringing what I've learned home to my local community in Southeast Asia. I will actively continue to champion Velocity, and the founders and teams I’m backing.

To our users and partners: thank you so much for the trust. I know the Velocity team is genuinely giving the relaunch all they have. To our investors: thank you for all your guidance and support all these years. To our team: thank you for everything. I couldn't have imagined doing this with anyone else.

text:
真实的去中心化：没有人可以用任何方式剥夺你合法合规持有的资产。
虚假的去中心化：任何人可以用任何方式抢走你合法合规持有的资产。

进入加密行业这么多年，我自己的思想也产生了很大的转变，从一开始对于那个去中心化code is law乌托邦世界的向往，逐渐地开始动摇和质疑，我们真正要的，到底是自由还是规则？到底是公正还是高效？

曾经我以为去中心化是普通人对抗强权自我保卫的盾牌，但我越来越觉得，过度的极端的去中心化，恰恰是强权掠夺普通人甚至将其合法化的武器。

著名的《人类简史》这本书中提出，人类发展的过程，就是不断地将自己的一些权利让渡出去，形成一个公共服务中心，负责治安、外交等等事项，然后普通人才可以把更多的精力转移到生产劳作。

但如果告诉你，这个世界将不再有任何的中心，每个人都必须只为自己负责，你走在大街上要小心别人会一刀把你捅死，你得随时守在你家大门口别人闯进来就可以把你家据为己有，那这个世界就成了谁强谁有理。

有一部美国电影叫《人类清除计划》，美国政府规定，在这一天，所有的消防、治安、警察等政府部门全部失效，人类想干嘛干嘛，于是在这一天，所有的穷人都只能蜷缩在家里面，但却成了富人的天堂，因为他们可以带着雇佣兵上街大肆杀戮。

规则到底是保护穷人的，还是保护富人的？我敢说绝大多数正常的国家，如果没有规则的话，穷人一定会过得更惨，成为富人的人肉电池。

曾经我也非常信仰code is law，只要说好的事情绝对不能改，但全世界当前最牛逼的国家，美国宪法也修改了27次。

违背承诺当然是一个不好的事情，但是小到一个人，大到一个国家，都是动态发展的，所以没有什么绝对的二极管一定要怎么样，你不能因为看见了柬埔寨的红色高棉、朝鲜的金家政权，就认为政府都是坏的，要打造一个没有中心和谎言的世界。

所以我很费解，那些极力拥护黑客以及为虎作伥的人，到底是什么成分？他们生活中是遭受到了多大的迫害，才会产生如此扭曲的价值观吗，挺心疼他们的
author: youyou5202
quoted_text:
去中心化 ≠ 无政府状态！

Bitcoin、Ethereum 真正珍贵的地方，

是任何人都不能因为身份、国籍、观点，轻易剥夺你持有和转移资产的权利。

但这和黑客偷了 5 亿美元之后，你以去中心化的幌子必须假装没看见完全是两回事。

自由应该保护的是合法用户的财产权与交易权，而不是给犯罪者提供一种「不可被干预的特权」。

加密行业应该找到一种方法，保障大家自由的情况下，充分遏制黑客和其他违法活动，

去中心化不等于无组织和肆意妄为，加密行业应主动遏制犯罪活动，才能长久更好的存活下去。

我认为未来比较合理的 Crypto 架构应该是：

底层协议尽可能中立，上层应用越来越有治理能力。

这就好比 BTC / ETH 等底层保持开放、无需许可、抗审查，DeFi 协议拥有风控、限速、Circuit Breaker、异常检测的权利，Bridge 可以做道大额异常冻结窗口、风控系统，CEX 因为有 KYC 可以追查和冻结冻结赃款，Stablecoin issuer 则有黑名单和执行机制，钱包做好风险地址预警、诈骗识别；

We founded Long Lake three years ago with the thesis that AI is going to change every company, but there’s a large overhang between AI capabilities and how most businesses leverage AI tools.

We partner with strong, profitable, and growing businesses to help them deploy AI and improve their customer service.

Our first cohort of companies has doubled their EBITDA in less than two years through topline and productivity growth, all while increasing headcount. (We’re proud to say that we’ve never conducted a layoff.)

We’re excited to share a bit more about what we’ve been up to.

text:
人话版 Parasite 调研，市场到底在炒作什么？

今天 Solana 上比较有意思的新东西，是 @parasitedotfun。

因为他改了 Meme 发射平台一个很少被动过的东西：交易对。

Pump fun 上绝大多数 Meme，本质都是 SOL → Meme。无论发的是狗、猫、名人币还是热点币，底层资金结构没有区别。

Parasite 改成了 SOL → Host → Parasite。发行新币时，可以选择另一枚已有代币作为 Host，也就是宿主。

比如用 STONK 做宿主发行 A。

A 不再直接对 SOL 交易，而是对 STONK 交易。

每次交易 A，都需要以 STONK 支付手续费，其中一部分直接销毁 STONK，一部分给开发者，一部分进入协议国库，另一部分支付给 Meteora。

国库收到宿主币后，再换成 SOL，回购并销毁 $PARASITE 。

所以一笔寄生币交易，同时影响三层资产：宿主被销毁，寄生币开发者获得收入，$PARASITE 获得回购销毁。

回购销毁本身没什么新鲜的。真正改变的是“谁做你的交易对”，第一次被做成了发币玩法的一部分。

以前一枚 Meme 想蹭另一枚 Meme 的热度，通常就是直接发衍生币。STONK 火了，就出现 BabySTONK、STONK2、STONK AI。

这些币虽然借了 STONK 的流量，但和 STONK 本身没有任何经济关系，甚至会把资金从 STONK 抽走。

Parasite 把关系改了。你依然可以蹭 STONK 的流量，但你要直接把 STONK 变成自己的底层报价资产。你的币交易得越多，STONK 被销毁得越多。衍生 Meme 不再只是吸血，而是开始给宿主交租。

这个设计很聪明。它把原本纯粹的注意力寄生，变成了经济寄生。热门 Meme 不再只是“被蹭”，而可以直接从衍生币的交易活动中受益。

Parasite 最多允许三层寄生。

比如 STONK → A → B。B 用 A 做宿主，交易 B 会销毁 A；A 又用 STONK 做宿主，交易 A 会销毁 STONK。

于是会形成一棵 Meme 的资产树。爷爷币下面长爸爸币，爸爸币下面长孙子币，上一层既是资产，也是下一层的底层流动性。

这套结构天然适合 Meme 市场。因为 Meme 本来就有很强的衍生文化，一个币火了，下面马上会出现几十个衍生币。Parasite 没有阻止这种行为，而是直接把衍生关系协议化了。

以后项目之间竞争的，可能不只是“谁的币涨得更多”，还会变成谁能成为更多新币的宿主。

如果一个 Meme 成为大量新币的 Host，它就不再只是 Meme，而会开始具备一部分“基础结算资产”的属性。

这也是 Parasite 最有想象力的地方，它尝试把 Meme 的注意力做成可组合资产。

而且是金融飞轮也非常直接。假设 STONK 很火，越来越多人拿 STONK 做 Host，越来越多寄生币在 STONK 上发行。寄生币交易带来 STONK 需求，同时持续销毁 STONK。

市场开始炒作“STONK 正在成为 Parasite 生态的基础资产”，STONK 上涨，又会吸引更多项目愿意寄生在 STONK 上，继续强化前面的循环。

$PARASITE 站在整个体系上层。下面不管使用 STONK、其他 Meme 还是别的资产做 Host，只要产生交易，国库都会获得一部分宿主币。这些资产最终被卖出，换成 SOL，再回购销毁 $PARASITE。

所以 $PARASITE 想捕获的，不是某一只寄生币的交易，而是整个 Parasite 生态的交易活动。市场以后真正会炒的，也大概率不是“虫子 Meme”，而是几个数字：有多少 Host，有多少 Parasite，每天多少交易量，每天销毁多少宿主，每天回购多少 $PARASITE。

如果这些数据持续增长，$PARASITE 就会自然形成平台币叙事。

问题也能看出来。Parasite 目前产生的收入，依然高度依赖投机。不是有人必须完成某种现实金融需求，而是大家为了炒新 Meme，不断交易新 Meme。

市场热的时候，这套飞轮很好看。新币增加，交易量增加，Host 被销毁，$PARASITE 被回购，协议收入增长。币价上涨以后，又会吸引更多人发行新币。

但如果市场不再愿意炒这些币，整套飞轮也会迅速降速。

所以现在不能因为“有回购、有销毁、有协议收入”，就直接把 $PARASITE 看成传统意义上的现金流资产。

它目前更像是把 Meme 投机产生的手续费重新分配了一遍。

第二个问题，是多层寄生会增加系统脆弱性。

假设 STONK → A → B，你买 B，不只是在承担 B 的风险。A 的流动性会影响你，STONK 的流动性也会影响你。层数越深，整个交易路径对上游资产的依赖越强。其中任何一层流动性下降、价格暴跌或者深度不足，都会影响下面的资产。

所以三层寄生最大的亮点和最大的风险，其实是同一个东西：套娃。上涨的时候，它会放大叙事；下跌的时候，它也会放大风险传导。

市场现在还有一个猜测：Parasite 会不会是 Meteora 在背后扶持。

目前能确认的是，它和 Meteora 的技术关系非常深。寄生币使用 Meteora 的动态曲线机制，毕业后进入 Meteora 流动性池，Meteora 也能从交易手续费中分成。

但“使用 Meteora 基础设施”和“Meteora 官方推出这个项目”是两回事。目前更值得关注的，是两者的利益天然一致。Parasite 交易越多，Meteora 获得的交易量和手续费越多，已经足够形成合作空间。

现在主要看三个数据。

第一，有没有真正有市场的币愿意成为 Host。如果最后只是 $PARASITE 和一堆小 Meme 互相套娃，模式上限很低。如果 STONK 这种已有流量和社区的资产开始主动接受寄生币，意义完全不同。

第二，有没有寄生币能够真正跑出来。如果所有寄生币最后都是几小时生命周期，那它只是给土狗换了一种发行方式。如果能出现真正的大市值寄生币，市场才会认真研究 Host 选择本身。

第三，PARASITE的回购规模能不能持续增长。如果协议每天只能靠短周期投机产生少量手续费，它仍然只是一个平台Meme。如果整个生态形成稳定交易活动，PARASITE 才开始具备长期价值捕获逻辑。

Parasite 没有发明 Meme Launchpad，也没有发明回购销毁。它真正新鲜的地方，是把币圈每天都在发生的“衍生 Meme 蹭母币流量”，做成了一套明确的经济关系。

以前，你蹭我的 Meme，就是吸我的血。现在，你可以继续蹭，但你每交易一次，都要烧掉一点宿主。

Parasite 这个名字很准确。真正成功的寄生关系，不是立刻杀死宿主，而是寄生物需要宿主活着，宿主也能从寄生关系里获得利益。

如果以后真的出现热门 Meme 主动说“欢迎来寄生我”，那 Parasite 做出来的，就不只是另一个发射平台，而可能创造一种新的 Meme 资产关系。

现在还很早，也很可能最后只是另一轮金融套娃。但这次至少不是换一个发币页面，它确实改了一层底层规则。

说一下我知道的 @SolvProtocol  的事情吧.

团队的人2025年就大部分未解锁代币都OTC出了, 至于什么ecosystem 的代币分配早就掏干净了, 也就是说弃盘了,  现在只剩个壳子.

这个协议就是你把BTC 存进去, 他给你2-3%年化.  BTC本身又不生息, 又无法出借, 这收益哪来的呢?

就是协议把你的BTC 抵押了, 去借出来U, 然后用你的U参与各种defi,  比如说 Ethena, Jupiter, Babylon.

说白了就是代客理财.  低息借U, 然后投资高风险高收益的defi协议.      这个一直都是个笑话, 这种代客理财的模式就不可能跑的通. 

defi协议是有风险的, 那么 如果参与的协议被盗了,或者亏损了, 怎么办?   我2024年参与的时候就问过这个问题 ,Solv的人一直不正面回答.   其实也很简单, 看什么时候以及多少钱.   tge之前的关键节点, 已经亏损不多的情况下, 协议可以补上.    

2024年底他们的第一个协议, SolvBTC.ena,  当时就是亏损的,  也就是他们投资的 ena 收益还无法覆盖 借U的利息.  不过他们最后是自己掏腰包补上 + 送很多积分. 所以没有实际损失.

他们的代币 SOLV 是2025年1月 tge, 在币安 Megadrop, 也就是大撒币.   拿7%的总代币份额出来上供给币安, 这个当时占40%的流通量.        当时的 Scroll厕纸, Lisda, Usual 一样, 都是第一天的总流通量30%- 40% 给到币安空投, 纯纯的傻逼冤大头了, 以后再也没可能出现了.

币安用户拿到了后自然一开盘就哐哐砸, 币价一路下跌.  记得币安有一个朱一旦, 一路喊单抄底,最后亏的裤衩都不剩了被大家笑话.  

Solv最后花在空投和做市的钱应该有上千万美元了.

几个创始人, Ryan和那个孟光头, 自己都说不清楚商业路线, Solv自然很稳定的一路下跌..     跟着所谓的BTCfi 一起灭亡了..

现在来个放50个BTC的大户, 盘子直接送给你了.

text:
《华尔街日报》刚挖出来，今年 7 月洛杉矶那笔一直不知道买家是谁的 1.3 亿美元豪宅交易，背后的人就是 Peter Thiel。

房子叫 Casa Encantada，Bel-Air 最有名的老钱庄园之一，1930 年代建成，占地 8.5 英亩，室内接近 4 万平方英尺。

过去几十年两次卖掉，两次都刷新过美国住宅成交纪录。2023 年原主人去世后曝出财务问题，房子进入止赎拍卖，Thiel 通过一家 LLC 悄悄拿下。

有意思的是时间点。

过去一年 Thiel 一直在身体力行地「离开加州」。加州推动一次性 5% 亿万富豪财富税后，一批硅谷富豪开始把住所、公司和资产往外挪，Thiel 也是其中之一。

Thiel Capital 去年底宣布在迈阿密开办公室，他本人此前已经在迈阿密持有住宅；今年 1 月，他又掏了 300 万美元支持反对这项财富税的组织。

加州政府，不能忍。

加州税收，必须反。

Bel-Air 原价 2.5 亿、现在 1.3 亿的房子，那我得去看看。

反民主党加州是工作，在 Bel-Air 抄底是生活。

嘴上对加州治理模式意见很大，到了资产价格这里，意识形态突然变得非常有弹性。

突然就理解什么叫资本没有祖国了。

Peter Thiel 可能确实不喜欢加州，但他显然没有不喜欢加州的房地产。

text:
Bitget CEO Gracy Chen says THORChain shut its system down when it was the victim, but refused her request to block the hacker's addresses

"At that time, I don't think I knew exactly how their governance works, nor do I know it now. The key thing is, it's quite clear those are public addresses that we listed and kept tracking. Hence I decided to formally ask them to refuse services to those addresses. By asking them, it could be their team members, the core foundation, or the nodes and swaps on that public chain."

"Later on I did more research, and I realized there were cases where they shut down the system because of other hacks, especially hacks where they themselves were a victim. But in general, I don't want to just target THORChain by saying you should change your protocol from permissionless to something else."

"I think what NEAR Intents did was quite interesting. Although the blockchain is still permissionless, you can build a layer on it to do more KYT to avoid the hacker's funds."

"I also saw some major industry leaders, even our competitors, come out and accuse THORChain of not being consistent in their standard. When it's them being the victim, they can shut down the system. And when it's not them, when it's us, they just refuse. I saw THORChain's official tweet refusing my request."

text:
Quantum-safety is a huge concern, and for this reason, we should start talking about the fact that it will be determined by a combination of 2 factors:
1. Quantum exposure
2. Crypto agility

What are these 2 things?

1. Quantum exposure: this is the degree to which a quantum computer will threaten your cryptography. 
For example, elliptic curve cryptography is quantum-vulnerable, while hash-based cryptography (e.g. ZK-STARKs) is quantum-resistant. 
So the more your protocol relies on quantum-vulnerable cryptography, the higher your quantum exposure.

2. Crypto agility: this is the ability to upgrade your cryptography while staying operational. 
Some protocols will need at least a soft fork (hello Bitcoin) to reach quantum-safety, some will require users to navigate their way through clunky UX, and in some cases, users will only need a quick approval for an upgrade. 
So seamless upgradability means high crypto agility. In cases where chains have lower crypto agility, it means the road to quantum-safety is longer and more difficult.

So quantum safety will rely on the combination of these 2 factors together. 
You CANNOT separate them.

More details and ecosystems review in the tweet below👇

text:
6.1 astra被延迟 但是发布了 sol：

别等旗舰了。OpenAI先把干活的那台车开出来了，GPT-6.1 Sol 的定位很直白：接近 GPT-6 Astra 的智力，价格大约只有 Astra 的五分之一，缓存读取再打 95% 折扣。官方自己的说法是——绝对的 workhorse。

旗舰负责刷分、刷面子；Sol 负责天天跑、天天烧、天天赚钱。
这事之所以炸，不只是因为又出了一个模型。
大家等的是 6.1 Astra。结果先等来的是 6.1 Sol。

情绪上像极了：婚礼延期，但先把伴郎请上台了。伴郎还挺能打。编码、电脑操作、专业任务，官方称它已经贴近 Astra；

DeepSWE 这类硬核工程评测上，甚至说能打平 Astra，成本却低一个档。缓存输入只要每百万 token 0.1 美元。对要反复带上下文、反复跑 agent 的人，这才是真刀真枪的降本。
速度也一起打包。Ultrafast 先给 Astra 上，号称最高 8 倍加速；Sol 很快跟上。

订阅侧再甩出 Pro 500：更高额度、更高速度。于是评论区瞬间分裂成两派——
一派说：终于有能日抛的准旗舰了，agent 可以铺开了。
 一派说：Astra 还没到，先把 Pro 200 削一刀，再卖 500，这不是升级，这是套娃。

两种反应都对。OpenAI 这次卖的不是“更神”，是“更便宜地接近神”。旗舰继续压在顶上当信仰；中间层开始变成流水线。谁会真正受益？不是天天截图榜单的人，是要把模型嵌进工作流、嵌进 Codex、嵌进 agent、嵌进反复调用的人。

所以别被名字骗了。Sol 不是安慰奖。它是 OpenAI 在告诉市场：顶峰可以晚点到，但规模化不能等。6.1 Astra 晚一天，Sol 就先把价格打穿一天。

你是来膜拜最强模型的，还是来让模型给你干活的？
前者继续等 Astra。 后者从今天开始，可以先把 Sol 当牲口使。

Project Eleven Acquires Riva Labs to Expand Post-Quantum Research and Engineering

Riva Labs joins Project Eleven as the company brings more specialized post-quantum talent and technology under one roof.

Project Eleven, the company building post-quantum security infrastructure for digital assets, today announced its acquisition of @riva_labs, expanding its expertise in post-quantum signatures, wallets, MPC, and account abstraction. The acquisition also brings technology and intellectual property developed through Riva's work across Ethereum and other public blockchains, adding to Project Eleven's capabilities in post-quantum cryptography and blockchain infrastructure.

Riva Labs has built a reputation for translating post-quantum cryptographic research into practical blockchain systems. Its work spans hash-based post-quantum signatures, post-quantum MPC, account abstraction, wallet infrastructure, and hardware signing, including recent demonstrations of post-quantum signing on consumer hardware.

The addition of Riva expands Project Eleven's research and engineering bench as the digital asset industry prepares for the complexity of post-quantum migration. Rather than treating signatures, wallets, key management, and protocol infrastructure as separate problems, Project Eleven is bringing together expertise across each layer required to make that transition practical.

That work is becoming more urgent as AI accelerates cryptographic research and cryptanalysis, allowing new techniques to be developed, tested, and challenged at greater speed. Riva has made AI a core part of its research and engineering process, bringing that capability into Project Eleven's work across post-quantum cryptography and crypto agility.

"Riva Labs is exactly the kind of talent we want at Project Eleven: deeply technical and focused on turning cryptographic research into systems that can actually be deployed," said @apruden08, CEO and Co-Founder of Project Eleven. "Bringing Riva into Project Eleven strengthens an already exceptional research and engineering team, adds valuable technology, and accelerates our ability to lead the transition to post-quantum security across digital assets."

"Project Eleven and Riva Labs came at this problem from different directions and reached many of the same conclusions about what the industry needs," said @matteovena, Co-Founder of Riva Labs. "Upgrading the public networks the future will run on, without compromising the properties that make them valuable in the first place, is a monumental challenge. Our focus is on giving the industry the tools to accelerate that transition, and joining Project Eleven lets us do it at a much larger scale."

The Riva team and technology will become part of Project Eleven's broader research and product efforts across post-quantum cryptography, digital asset custody, and blockchain security. The acquisition deepens Project Eleven's technical capabilities as it builds the infrastructure required for a secure post-quantum transition.

text:
Oh man there is so much in the OAI launches this morning, early reactions:
- OAI leaning into its strengths around model breadth (full duplex voice / computer use), compute (ultrafast / decisions / price cuts), and knowledge work (spaces / dots)
- Spaces is an impressive effort to connect two key lessons from the last 6 months; one that consumers need "human shaped" interfaces to use models to their full ability (slack / imessage / anthropomorphic agent) and two that group productivity >> sum of individual productivity and requires dedicated collaboration tools like agent native docs / slides / etc.
- Dots acknowledges that consumers have a bounded view of chat interfaces ("better google") and the personal agents primitive needs a different positioning and personality. I like that the UI starts with a single "dot" (agent) and imagines expanding to teams, which combines the simplicity of a muse style approach with the power of grok bots, progressively disclosed.
- Security cloud is the first of many efforts where sensitive / proprietary model capabilities are vertically integrated and sold as an outcome vs API. Expect more of this in areas like biology (smartly framed today as "antibiotics" - who could dislike those?! 😂).
- Yes there are offerings at every spot on the Pareto curve (ultrafast at the high end, decisions at the low), but the wild 3D demo of ultrafast shows that these points on the curve represent new capabilities (i.e. just in time software, real time video transformation etc)
- Consumer adoption has accelerated w/ 1.2B WAU + Connect is a huge unlock for developers by letting users bring their own tokens—this unbundles the unit economics from product value & locks developers + users into the OAI ecosystem
- Plugin directory + discovery is maybe, finally the distribution channel we've been waiting for
- Marketplace allows SAAS partners to sell to OAI customers w/o the procurement headache
- $500 plan, and it's "cheap" given the capabilities .. I predict a $1000 plan by next year that will provide even more price/performance to consumers

Will think + share more when I have a chance to process, but wow some cool launches today.

HYG selling off doesn't tell you much about credit. It's got the rate move sitting inside it.

People see that chart dropping and start panicking about credit going crazy. But on a big move in yields it's going to fall whether or not credit is doing anything at all.

The quick fix is HYGH, the hedged version, which strips the rate part out. If HYGH is going nowhere while HYG drops, spreads aren't really widening and what you're looking at is the bond move.

That's what I've had on my screen through these bond moves, and it's been pretty quiet. I'm not sure how good HYG is as a credit barometer these days anyway, given what's in it.

text:
Impressive. This set of talks, along with the new America dot gov website, has the unmistakable feel of an Apple launch event. They're rebooting the federal government as a tech startup. Several observations.

(1) First, with this new AI interface to the entire federal government, if it works as promised, there won't be a single American who can't say their life wasn't helped at least in part by AI, or that the benefits accrued solely to zillionaires. This in itself cannily mitigates anti-datacenter sentiment.

(2) Second, Joe Gebbia and Marco Rubio's talks on simplifying name changes and passport filings introduce a completely new era where the US government is actually launching tangible features that benefit users.

(3) Third, this launch event in and of itself may visibly drive reform. It could become much more important than the State of the Union. Unlike laws, code is user-visible, and can be instantly audited by the public, as Obama found out with the failed obamacare website launch. So: the annual America dot gov event may be substance, whereas SOTU is traditionally optics. I wouldn't be surprised to see the President present at the next one.

(4) Fourth, this kind of event is a perfect example of where tech and red cooperate best. They both hate bureaucracy. Automating paperwork with code reduces the power of statists over both capitalists and nationalists. It's also hard to undo by other admins: once you digitize a process, hard to turn it back to paper.

(5) Fifth, it's an obvious point perhaps, but think about how much influence YCombinator has had in 20 years. From Gebbia's Airbnb joining their 2009 batch to a complete overhaul of the user interface of the US bureaucracy, and thus the US government.

(6) Sixth, this is another take on the network state. The functional part of the US (the network, meaning tech) is merging with and partially reforming the dysfunctional part (the state, meaning bureaucracy) by automating 20th century paper forms.

As a tech startup, there will no doubt be bugs and user issues and so on, but unlike with paper laws those issues will be visible and the code fixes will be verifiable. A new era of AI America. Rooting for them.

If this approach feels familiar, it is.

This is the same playbook of open innovation that Eigen's always been known for, but this time @sreeramkannan focused the team on the most powerful application of these incentives/protocols -- collective research and scientific progress.

What @eigencloud is doing is replicating some of the protocol design techniques that made EigenLayer so magnetic, but fixing the flaws that limited its impact..

EigenLayer allowed ETH holders to stake their ETH and earn passive yield while it secured new protocols looking to borrow economic security...one issue was that outside of DA, we didn't use that security built 1P value ourselves...we waited for others to do it and it never really materialized (history is repeating itself with Bittensor subnets fwiw) 

Now the scare resource isn't economic security, its compute and inference. 

@darkbloomai allows Mac owners to register their spare compute into a shared grid and earn passive income while developers use their machines to run private inference (10-20B tokens/day and climbing) 

@yukonresearch challenges run on darkbloom and let researchers put their spare AI token balances and harness designs towards solving frontier problems in science and research (including improving open-weight models that expand the footprint of Darkbloom itself).

"I think there are mainly two reasons. The first one is what we discussed earlier, like finding the root and doing the remediation took longer."

"But the amount is much smaller. The total value of the second round of attack is about $30 million, and that's from 8:55 to 9:23, because we switched on the system again and it gave them another chance."

text:
Jeffrey Hu 最近提到，他在看 EASY Residency S5 项目时，尤其关注两个方向：

隐私、后量子。

我顺着这条线往下查了一层，发现这并不是他临时冒出来的两个关键词。

YZi Labs 在 S5 正式公布的投资方向里，本来就单独列出了：

隐私基础设施
和
后量子迁移与密码学升级

所以这里真正值得提前建立观察名单的，我觉得不是“隐私币是不是又要轮动了”，也不是去找几个名字里带 Quantum 的币。

而是两类更底层的基础设施。

第一类：

怎么让机构真正把敏感金融活动搬到链上。

机构不可能公开暴露自己的余额、交易对手、仓位和商业条款，但同时又必须满足合规、审计和风险管理。

所以真正有价值的方向，是：

选择性披露、机密 DeFi、隐私稳定币结算、可编程合规……

核心不是追求绝对匿名，而是：

机构真正敢用、能用的隐私。

第二类更容易被市场低估：

现有 Crypto 基础设施怎么迁移到后量子密码学。

重点不一定是重新造一条“抗量子链”。

更大的市场可能是：

现有的钱包、托管、交易所、协议，怎么在不影响现有资产和用户的情况下，逐步升级签名、密钥管理和托管体系。

如果这个迁移真正开始，它服务的就不是一个新叙事，而可能是整个 Crypto 已有的资产体系。

目前我已经开始顺着这两条线建项目地图。

比如 Inco 更接近前者，做的是可编程的机密计算和隐私基础设施；

Quantus 则代表另一条路线：直接从底层构建面向后量子时代的网络。

但这两个项目，我现在都不会因为“叙事对了”就直接买。

真正值得继续盯的是下一层信号：

谁进入 EASY S5，谁拿到新的资本支持，谁真正获得机构或开发者采用，以及谁开始出现明确、可参与的经济价值捕获。

如果 Jeffrey 这条信号最后对应到一批 S5 项目，我觉得那份名单会非常值得第一时间拆。

因为相比等“隐私 + 后量子”已经变成市场共识以后再追，

现在更值得问的问题是：

资本正在提前寻找什么？

author: zerokn0wledge_
quoted_text:
So, @papertrade_xyz is about to launch, bringing 1000x leverage, 0 slippage, no funding fees, and self-bootstrapping LPs to HyperEVM.

As I explained back in August (see quoted post), this is a great example of a team properly leveraging the HyperEVM USPs (the precompiles to read from/write to Hypercore), and could be the type of breakout app that HyperEVM badly needs.

TL;DR:

- Fully onchain perps on HL with no orderbook, no matching engine and no oracle. Every trade is a synthetic swap vs the LP.

- Price = HL's live BBO mid, read straight off HyperCore via precompile. No signer, no committee, and no admin feed.

- 1000x lev, 0 slippage at any size, 0 funding, 0 fees, 0 gas (relayer pays).

- Only take is a haircut on winning closes, and it hits the hardest on the smallest price moves. That's the trick: a manipulated BBO tick is by definition a tiny move, so the curve eats the gain (hence no oracle guard or circuit breaker required).

- LP starts at exactly $0 and only ever grows from trader losses. Nobody can deposit into it, not the team, not a VC, not you. Holding $PAPER is the sole path to LP exposure, and the sole way to get $PAPER is to lose.

- If the LP can't cover a win, only the profit portion joins an onchain FIFO queue and gets paid as future losses refill it. Your margin always comes back instantly. The temporary insolvency is part of the design, not a bug.

$PAPER: 0 premine, 0 team, 0 VC, 0 airdrop, 0 vesting. 100 minted per $1 of LP gain while the LP is under $2M (underwater included, so early = the best rate you'll ever get), with the rate decaying from there.

- Not 1:1 portable to any other chain bc no one else exposes a consensus-verified CLOB onchain like Hyperliquid does.

Hyperliquid.

text:
blurr explains how papertrade uses $Paper to bootstrap liquidity with trader losses

“On a perp, whenever you take a long, someone on the other side is taking a short. That’s just how they operate. In a casino, when you’re betting, you’re betting against the house, which is owned by whoever owns the casino. That means you need somebody else on the other side to take that risk on.

“If you go to a casino, oftentimes they’ll have a max bet that you can’t break. The casino has to run Kelly on its bankroll, and that is a problem because the cold start for this kind of thing is much higher than it otherwise needs to be." 

"But with tokens, you can effectively sell the upside in the bankroll by getting people to gamble into it”

“If people assume or think that I will be profitable in the long run, they’re encouraged to sort of lose money into it to buy the equity in the system.”

The core problem is stale state.

If a propAMM’s quote, price, or inventory parameters lag behind the market, traders can interact against information the AMM no longer considers accurate.

Fast Feed reduces that observation delay by publishing transactions during block construction rather than waiting for the completed block feed.
author: arbitrum

text:
PGA handles the execution side.

Arbitrum One divides each nominal 250ms block into two nominal 125ms PGA rounds. Transactions waiting at the beginning of each round are ranked by priority, with higher-priority transactions selected first.

For a prop AMM, that means you can selectively pay for priority when getting an update in earlier is worth the cost.

depositas USDC → genera yield → pides MXNB prestado contra esa posición.

Obviamente no es dinero gratis: hay riesgo MXN/USD, riesgo de liquidación, las tasas cambian y están los riesgos propios de DeFi.

text:
Impressive. This set of talks, along with the new America dot gov website, has the unmistakable feel of an Apple launch event. They're rebooting the federal government as a tech startup. Several observations.

(1) First, with this new AI interface to the entire federal government, if it works as promised, there won't be a single American who can't say their life wasn't helped at least in part by AI, or that the benefits accrued solely to zillionaires. This in itself cannily mitigates anti-datacenter sentiment.

(2) Second, Joe Gebbia and Marco Rubio's talks on simplifying name changes and passport filings introduce a completely new era where the US government is actually launching tangible features that benefit users.

(3) Third, this launch event in and of itself may visibly drive reform. It could become much more important than the State of the Union. Unlike laws, code is user-visible, and can be instantly audited by the public, as Obama found out with the failed obamacare website launch. So: the annual America dot gov event may be substance, whereas SOTU is traditionally optics. I wouldn't be surprised to see the President present at the next one.

(4) Fourth, this kind of event is a perfect example of where tech and red cooperate best. They both hate bureaucracy. Automating paperwork with code reduces the power of statists over both capitalists and nationalists. It's also hard to undo by other admins: once you digitize a process, hard to turn it back to paper.

(5) Fifth, it's an obvious point perhaps, but think about how much influence YCombinator has had in 20 years. From Gebbia's Airbnb joining their 2009 batch to a complete overhaul of the user interface of the US bureaucracy, and thus the US government.

(6) Sixth, this is another take on the network state. The functional part of the US (the network, meaning tech) is merging with and partially reforming the dysfunctional part (the state, meaning bureaucracy) by automating 20th century paper forms.

As a tech startup, there will no doubt be bugs and user issues and so on, but unlike with paper laws those issues will be visible and the code fixes will be verifiable. A new era of AI America. Rooting for them.

text:
For years, the crypto industry operated under a bizarre interpretation of securities law: 

- Build a successful protocol? Fine. 
- Generate millions in revenue? Great. 
- Keep improving the product? Sure. 

But whatever you do, don’t let token holders benefit financially from any of it. 

The result was an entire generation of digital assets intentionally designed to have little or no economic value. 

Last week, the SEC staff provided important new guidance that could finally help reverse this. Among other things, the SEC clarified that token buybacks by functional protocols do not, by themselves, constitute “essential managerial efforts”; development teams can continue maintaining and improving functional protocols; promoting utility does not necessarily create an investment contract; and liquid staking tokens may retain the characteristics of their underlying assets. 

This is incredibly bullish for digital assets. 

Crypto finally has real businesses with real customers, real revenues and real cash flows. The next step is connecting those economics to the assets investors actually own. And forgive us for taking a small victory lap, but Arca has been screaming about this for years. Going back to 2023, we argued that legal fears were preventing protocols from providing value to token holders. In 2024, we explicitly called it “bad legal advice.” Last year, we wrote that this approach had led to thousands of tokens deliberately designed without value accrual. And just two months ago, I wrote: “Regulatory uncertainty did not protect investors. It actively encouraged worse token design.” 

I wish more founders, VCs, exchanges and lawyers had listened. The industry lost years, and perhaps most damagingly, trained an entire generation of crypto investors to believe fundamentals don’t matter. But it’s not too late. Protocols now have real revenues. DeFi has survived multiple cycles. Stablecoins have demonstrated product-market fit. Traditional financial institutions are moving assets on-chain. And regulatory clarity is finally improving. So let’s stop fighting the last war. 

We’ve spent long enough designing tokens around lawyers. Let’s start designing them for investors.

text:
After not co-inventing ChatGPT, I built Guard.

Safety researchers keep leaving frontier labs and saying the same thing in public: this is moving faster than the safeguards. Labs have published tests where a model, told it would be shut down, tried to copy its own weights somewhere safe. Cyber attacks are now AI-assisted and growing.

Meanwhile, people run AI agents on their laptops every day. Those agents install packages, start local servers, open ports, and move model files around. Antivirus is built to catch known malware, not to reason about what an AI agent is doing on your machine.

Guard watches that layer. It does not care who did it. A rogue agent, a careless script, or plain malware leave the same footprint, and Guard flags the footprint.

Timegravity Guard is an AI security analyst that lives on your own computer. Offline. No GPU needed. Runs on a CPU.

It runs on a schedule or on demand. Deterministic rules check what changed: new model weights, new listening ports, new services and scheduled tasks, edits to sensitive files like SSH keys and shell startup files. Every finding carries proof, a path, a hash, a port. Then a local model explains the finding like a colleague would: what happened, why it might matter, what to check first.

Rules detect. A local model explains. You decide. It never acts on its own, never touches the network, never changes a file.

Windows and Linux first. Personal machines now, small teams next. Paid plans coming. 

Design paper this week, benchmark in October. @timegravitylabs

Introducing FundByHook. A new way to support projects.

No round to close. No deadline. No fundraising target.

Building doesn’t stop when a funding round ends. We think funding should be able to keep going too.

FundByHook is an incubator where each project gets its own token and a funding pool that stays open. People can back a project as it develops. The team draws from the pool over time to fund its work.

The first fund is $RISK, the official token of FundByHook and Risk Labs, our studio. It comes with RiskLAB:500 generative compositions drawn onchain.

CA: 0xbF0347cB1347B58e11Cd2Ba60854E0DD60d5F12F

Here is how it works.

FUNDING THAT STAYS OPEN

A conventional raise has a finish line: a date, a target, a round to close. The work that follows rarely fits that calendar.

On FundByHook, each pool runs through a Uniswap v4 hook. The hook controls a single liquidity position. External liquidity providers cannot add to it or pull liquidity out.

You back a project by buying its token. You can sell through the same pool, subject to its available liquidity and the sell tax.

The team receives funding in three ways:

→ 1% on buys, paid to the team
→ 10% of the ETH paid out by sells, paid to the team
→ A manual draw of 1% of the pool’s current ETH reserve, available at most once every seven days
The draw does not accumulate. Waiting three weeks does not unlock three withdrawals. The team must trigger it, and each draw starts a new seven-day wait.
Tokens remain in the pool. ETH leaves to fund the work. Each draw lowers the pool price slightly.

After launch, the fund contracts have no admin setters, pause or upgrade functions. Only the team can trigger the draw. The funding rules stay fixed.

Contracts by @tzv and @RISKFDN.

FUND 1: $RISK

$RISK has a fixed supply of 500 tokens.

400 seed the pool. It starts with no ETH: buyers bring it in. Buys move the price up; sells move it down.

The remaining 100 $RISK are allocated to Risk Labs to reward people who help move our projects forward. The first 5 go out this week to people who helped move ELA forward.

Those 100 tokens are not locked by code. We are responsible for how they are used.

$RISK also has a visual form. RiskLAB is a collection of 500 generative compositions built from frames, cells and nodes. Both the images and their metadata are generated onchain.

ONE TOKEN. ONE PIECE.

With NFT mirroring enabled, each whole $RISK in your wallet corresponds to one RiskLAB piece, an ERC-721.

12.93 $RISK = 12 pieces + a 0.93-token fraction.

Transfer a piece and one whole $RISK moves with it. Sell 1 $RISK from that balance and you are left with 11 pieces and 0.93 $RISK. One piece is burned; its ID can later be reissued.

Your tokens and pieces are two representations of the same holding. NFT mirroring is enabled by default for ordinary wallets, and holders can change their own setting.

THE PLATFORM TOKEN

$RISK is the official token of FundByHook. Each fund launched on the platform will have its own token; $RISK remains the token of the platform and Risk Labs.

It is also how we want holders to participate in what Risk Labs builds next.

Our commitment: every future Risk Labs project will share a portion of its fees with $RISK holders.

That commitment comes from the lab. It is not enforced by the $RISK contracts. The percentage, timing, eligibility and distribution mechanism are still to be defined. There is no fee-sharing mechanism live in these contracts today.

On $RISK itself, all buy fees, sell taxes and team draws go to the team.

THE DOOR

For the first 10 blocks after the pool is seeded, buying is restricted to enlisted wallets.

There is a door hidden in a site that was live long before the contract.

That is all we will say.

WHAT COMES NEXT

$RISK is Fund 1. The next funds will come from ideas worth building, whether they come from Risk Labs or anyone else. Eventually, anyone will be able to launch a fund on FundByHook.

Today, only the lab can launch. Permissionless launches are not live yet.

For the lab, two rules apply:

01 / Each project must run autonomously before we start the next.
02 / Nothing launches without a good idea.

$RISK remains the platform and studio token as those projects take shape.

That is the experiment:

Can funding stay open as long as the building does?

Risk Labs starts with $RISK. What we build next has to earn your continued support.

FundByHook is open now: https://t.co/0fAWgDaA76
Explore RiskLAB on FundByHook: https://t.co/nGrKj9MlVR

Back the ones you believe in.

author: hamandcheese
quoted_text:
Impressive. This set of talks, along with the new America dot gov website, has the unmistakable feel of an Apple launch event. They're rebooting the federal government as a tech startup. Several observations.

(1) First, with this new AI interface to the entire federal government, if it works as promised, there won't be a single American who can't say their life wasn't helped at least in part by AI, or that the benefits accrued solely to zillionaires. This in itself cannily mitigates anti-datacenter sentiment.

(2) Second, Joe Gebbia and Marco Rubio's talks on simplifying name changes and passport filings introduce a completely new era where the US government is actually launching tangible features that benefit users.

(3) Third, this launch event in and of itself may visibly drive reform. It could become much more important than the State of the Union. Unlike laws, code is user-visible, and can be instantly audited by the public, as Obama found out with the failed obamacare website launch. So: the annual America dot gov event may be substance, whereas SOTU is traditionally optics. I wouldn't be surprised to see the President present at the next one.

(4) Fourth, this kind of event is a perfect example of where tech and red cooperate best. They both hate bureaucracy. Automating paperwork with code reduces the power of statists over both capitalists and nationalists. It's also hard to undo by other admins: once you digitize a process, hard to turn it back to paper.

(5) Fifth, it's an obvious point perhaps, but think about how much influence YCombinator has had in 20 years. From Gebbia's Airbnb joining their 2009 batch to a complete overhaul of the user interface of the US bureaucracy, and thus the US government.

(6) Sixth, this is another take on the network state. The functional part of the US (the network, meaning tech) is merging with and partially reforming the dysfunctional part (the state, meaning bureaucracy) by automating 20th century paper forms.

As a tech startup, there will no doubt be bugs and user issues and so on, but unlike with paper laws those issues will be visible and the code fixes will be verifiable. A new era of AI America. Rooting for them.

author: Cato_KT
quoted_text:
中东恢复能源输出能力+美对俄准备解除制裁，对目前的美伊谈判真的有益处吗？

今天的美伊谈判对话可以说是一波三折

AP报道，伊朗对美国提出的7天方案出现新的版本，新版本的第一阶段要求伊朗开放霍尔木兹海峡，同时美国解除对伊朗的港口封锁，随后才是逐渐解除对伊朗的制裁

但是新的谈判核心依旧是不拥核+对海峡不收费，而对于最新方案的修正伊朗官方并未明确证实消息的准确性，很显然伊朗需要权衡内部压力谈判条件做综合评估

就在这个关键时刻，特朗普直接表示否认以核换解除制裁的消息，直接推翻了此前所有的谈判进展，而伊朗方面只是表示对话窗口并未关闭，等待美国回应

这里需要注意，为何特朗普突然一口否定此前的要求？

我认为最核心的就是连续两天，沙特与卡塔尔均出现能源恢复出口的数据，并且根据数据采集机构表示，中东能源输出已经大量恢复

另一方面，媒体报道特朗普支持以俄罗斯释放囚犯为条件解除对俄罗斯制裁，其实这对于美伊局势并不是一件好事，此前特朗普就提出或许可以采购俄罗斯柴油来对冲中东能源输出困难的问题，一旦对俄罗斯解除制裁获得柴油进口，那么美国本土能源紧张会得到缓解

整体来看，如果中东能源输出已经恢复接近战前水平+美国获得俄罗斯出口柴油，那么对于特朗普来说，能源问题在市场供给侧得到改善，那么他还有理由跟伊朗谈判吗？

这也是我认为特朗普突然一口否定此前提出以核换海峡政策主要原因，特朗普在拿到这些数据后很有可能坐地起价，并不是不想与伊朗谈，很有可能是想提高价码，让谈判门槛继续提高，对伊朗来说算是一种外交压力测试，如果伊朗同意新增条件，那么后续特朗普将会变本加厉！

所以，目前各类数据支持中东能源输出改善，这对于Brent 市场供给侧是好事，但是对于美伊谈判我觉得这并非是一件好事！

如果我的分析是对的，那么今天特朗普很有可能通过中间人向伊朗提出更高门槛的谈判条件，而伊朗估计不会容易接受，接下来等消息验证吧！

text:
What I've learned: 

- Gamma tokens put the revenue generated by a subnet on chain. This makes it TRANSPARENT.

- Once an alpha token is burned into gamma (credit for subnet usage), it can NOT go back and become alpha again. It's a usage credit now.

- This means alpha supply is always going down proportional to subnet usage.

- Gamma is burned after it's used as a 'credit for product'.

- This puts the 'buy n burn' subnets are doing now fully inside Bittensor.

- By allowed subnets to earn Gamma tokens as subnet owner emissions, this removes the need for subnet owners to sell their alpha tokens into TAO (or dollars) in order to spend it on subnet services -- so less sell pressure on subnets.

quoted_text:
I've been sleeping with the head of my bed raised for a while, and I'm surprised more people don't do it.

Inclined bed therapy (IBT) helps with acid reflux, sleep apnea, airways, puffy face, etc.

Basically, when you lie flat stomach acid can flow back up into your throat, and when you sleep you swallow less, so it stays there. Hence the burning, 3am wake-ups, coughing, etc.

If you tilt the bed, the gravity keeps the acid in your stomach. A systemic review of 5 controlled trials found that IBT generally improved reflux symptoms and acid exposure.

In another study of 52 people with obstructive sleep apnea, it helped reduce apnea events by 32%.

Some people report less facial puffiness, but that's mostly anecdotal.

I use an Avocado adjustable base to raise the head of my head and it's been extremely helpful.

text: Grok @Bot in your Tesla
author: poteto
quoted_text:
I dramatically underestimated the value of Grok Bot in my Tesla. 

Can you technically do everything you’re able to do with Grok Bot in the Tesla just by launching the app on your phone and going voice mode? Sure. 

But the magic isn’t in the raw capability itself, it’s in the combination of raw capability and total seamlessness.

I often have fleeting thoughts while driving around. Some of these things aren’t significant enough to make me fumble around with my phone while supervising FSD, but when I literally don’t have to lift a finger and can just “Hey Grok” anything computer related into reality, I find myself taking advantage daily. And the little things add up. 

I’m on my way to work and remembered that I have a few documents on my home computer that I am going to need for work. So I just asked “Hey Grok, can you grab those 4 pdf files from my Mac downloads folder and move them into X folder on my one drive?” Now they’ll be where I need them to be when I get to my desk, and I won’t have to re-download them on my work machine. 

I have to work on a presentation today for a talk in a few weeks. “Hey grok, go into my sales enablement folder and have Claude Code build me a deck focused on X product for Y industry.” Claude already has my full job context, styling preferences etc and can build a nearly finished deck with a prompt. Now when I get to my desk, instead of building from scratch, I can review and prompt revisions before beginning to dig through my email backlog. 

Feels insane.

text:
permissionless rails. permissioned assets:
@metaplex's new MPL-3643 standard is a banger step forward for real-world assets on solana.

what is MPL-3643?
> issuers can create Token-2022 assets where transfers depend on predefined rules.

> wallets can be required to pass KYC before holding or transferring an asset. 

> additional rules can govern things like lockups, volume limits or where an asset can trade.

why is the onchain enforcement so cool?
> instead of making the entire system permissioned, MPL-3643 uses identity claims + transfer rules to introduce controls at the asset level.

> permission where necessary. permissionless everywhere else.

> this opens up a much bigger design space for tokenized stocks, securities & other RWAs that can’t simply trade everywhere, between everyone, all the time.

what about compliance?
> the technology provides rails for enforcing rules.

> it does not make an asset legally compliant by itself. issuers + their counsel still determine what those rules need to be.

why should you care?
> rules-based trading on permissionless rails is really sexy stuff.

> it's metaplex - the GOAT for building the asset primitives of solana: NFTs, tokens, inscriptions, compressed assets and now permissioned RWAs.
--> lots of cool stuff for builders to experiment with

what next?
> MPL-3643 is live on solana mainnet in early access and is currently unaudited.

> builders & issuers can request alpha access: https://t.co/mW32NlQRzT

--
new building blocks create new possibilities.

go build something that couldn’t exist before!

builders will win.

*stay tuned for updates on meteora ecosystem x mpl-3643

text:
i still don't understand why everyone is NOT using this 100% free alternative to TradingView

it does everything TradingView charges $2,399/year for FREE

i plugged openmarket into my Opus 5.5 + Jev stack and built an ORDER FLOW trading desk that is running autonomously 24/7

here is the EXACT system you can build today:

1. openmarket streams three things live for free, the liquidation heatmap, the order book depth, and CVD, the exact order flow a fund pays thousands for

2. the liquidation map shows where the stops are stacked, price hunts those clusters, so it tells you where the market wants to go next

3. the order book shows if there is more size on the buy or the sell side, that is who is actually in control right now

4. CVD shows if the buying is real, price up but CVD down means the move is fake and about to fail, the read most people never see

5. i pull all three through the OpenMarket API and pack them into one clean snapshot on every candle

6. Jev scores that snapshot in < 100 ms, is a cluster about to get hunted, is the flow real or fading, buy sell or hold

7. Opus 5.5 sits on top, after fixed time it reads which order flow reads actually worked and rewrites the questions Jev asks, so it gets sharper and becomes powerful itself

8. a hard risk layer holds every limit and now the desk trades institutional order flow on its own, for ZERO dollars a month in data

author: MerlinEgalite
quoted_text:
Una cosa de DeFi que me parece increíble:

Hoy puedes depositar USDC en nuestro vault de Morpho, generar ~4.20% de yield, y usar esa misma posición como colateral para pedir MXNB prestado a ~6%.

El yield se genera sobre todo tu colateral, mientras que pagas intereses sólo sobre lo que pides prestado. Como el préstamo está sobrecolateralizado, ignorando el tipo de cambio, el costo efectivo es menor que el spread entre ambas tasas (en este caso, menos de 1.8%).

Si tienes USDC pero necesitas pesos y no quieres vender tus dólares, esto se vuelve todavía más interesante.

Hoy esto requiere varios pasos en Morpho. Lo probé y me tomó menos de un minuto. Pero imaginen esto convertido en un solo click:

depositas USDC → genera yield → pides MXNB prestado contra esa posición.

Obviamente no es dinero gratis: hay riesgo MXN/USD, riesgo de liquidación, las tasas cambian y están los riesgos propios de DeFi.

Pero esto es exactamente lo que me gusta de la composability de DeFi. Tomas dos productos relativamente sencillos y al juntarlos aparece algo que antes era bastante difícil de construir.

text:
Quantum-safety is a huge concern, and for this reason, we should start talking about the fact that it will be determined by a combination of 2 factors:
1. Quantum exposure
2. Crypto agility

What are these 2 things?

1. Quantum exposure: this is the degree to which a quantum computer will threaten your cryptography. 
For example, elliptic curve cryptography is quantum-vulnerable, while hash-based cryptography (e.g. ZK-STARKs) is quantum-resistant. 
So the more your protocol relies on quantum-vulnerable cryptography, the higher your quantum exposure.

2. Crypto agility: this is the ability to upgrade your cryptography while staying operational. 
Some protocols will need at least a soft fork (hello Bitcoin) to reach quantum-safety, some will require users to navigate their way through clunky UX, and in some cases, users will only need a quick approval for an upgrade. 
So seamless upgradability means high crypto agility. In cases where chains have lower crypto agility, it means the road to quantum-safety is longer and more difficult.

So quantum safety will rely on the combination of these 2 factors together. 
You CANNOT separate them.

More details and ecosystems review in the tweet below👇

Here... some heatmaps of where GPT-6 Sol was looking, while sitting behind an API 👀👀

🚨New preprint: 
AnswerMap: Training-free Faithful Spatial Interpretability of VLMs from Answer Posteriors

🔵tl;dr: Cut the image into row and column bands, ask the model a query for each, and take the outer product of the P(yes) answers → a K×K map from only 2K calls. Multiplying maps from several coprime grid sizes gives a very detailed map, and you just need the logprobs, so it works on closed APIs! and the map gives continuous outputs natively, e.g. a location as its expectation, instead of forcing them through discrete text tokens!

text:
OpenAI 推出 dots：24 小时替你干活的 AI 分身

OpenAI 发布了常驻 AI 智能体 dots。普通聊天机器人是你问一句它答一句，dot 不一样：它有自己的云端电脑和浏览器，会记住你的偏好和做事标准，你不在的时候也会继续推进工作，还会主动发现该做的事。

dot 由新模型 GPT-6 Astra 驱动，能通过插件连接 4000 多个应用。你可以在 ChatGPT（桌面、网页、手机）、Slack、Teams 里给它发消息，也可以直接跟它语音通话，短信支持也快上线了。不管从哪个入口找它，它都带着完整的上下文。

它能干什么？OpenAI 举的例子都很具体。Slack 里有人报了 bug，dot 马上开始排查。设计稿一到，dot 就把它做成能跑的应用。开发者的 dot 会盯着用户反馈，自己修小问题、跑测试，再把附带演示视频的代码合并请求交给你审。有位早期测试者忘了给一家媒体开发票，他的 dot 发现后把发票准备好，经他同意后发了出去。

一个 dot 能同时跑好几个项目，你不用开一堆对话窗口挨个指挥。你随时可以打开它的云电脑看它在做什么；如果你授权，它也能直接操作你自己的笔记本电脑。

安全上，dot 默认只在自己的云电脑里工作，跟你的电脑隔离。你不在时它做的"主动调研"只有只读权限。发消息、改内容这类可能影响你账号的操作要先过自动审核，需要时会请你批准。改密码这种敏感操作永远只能你本人来。

除了个人 dot，OpenAI 还预览了"专员 dot"。企业给它分配独立的身份、账号和系统权限，让它专门负责采购、发票处理、客服这类明确的岗位。目前先在少数企业试点，同时和微软合作，让企业能用 Agent 365 里现成的管控工具管理 dots。

怎么用：从今天起，dots 在符合条件的地区陆续开放给 ChatGPT Pro 和 Business Premium 用户；企业版（含教育、医疗）需要管理员开启测试版。第一个 dot 包含在套餐里，不另收费。跟 dot 聊天不占 ChatGPT 用量额度，但让它去 Codex 或 ChatGPT Work 里执行任务，照常计入用量。第一次需要在 ChatGPT 桌面应用或电脑浏览器里创建，之后就能在手机上用。以后还可以加购更多 dot，或者提升单个 dot 的速度和每月工作量。

text:
Some personal news: I'm joining @PrimeIntellect as Head of Scientific AI!

A billion copies of the same very smart, agreeable mind will not be a scientifically fruitful world.

Scientific superintelligence should be weird and definitionally nonconsensus. It should be highly plural, consisting of many minds, human and artificial, that see the world differently and hold each other accountable, with human judgement still playing the central role in setting the trajectory.

Science is about asking the right questions and reducing uncertainty. Professionalizing science made discovery a viable career, but it also introduced incentives to work on what is fundable and publishable. Neither is the same thing as being true or impactful (reward hacking exists in the real world too!). We are very good at accumulating incremental knowledge and rather bad at stewarding unorthodox ideas through infancy, even though these are often the ideas that open entirely new fields of inquiry.

If we aren't careful, scientific AI could reproduce these same incentives at a much larger scale. If everyone relies on the same few large models, we risk inheriting the same priors and blind spots.

Open tools let us shape our own intelligence and take it in directions a frontier lab might never prioritize. This matters for scientific freedom and is central to Prime’s vision.

If you are a scientist, staying at the frontier will mean training your own models on your own research and data. I'll work closely with scientific teams across domains to help them build scientific agents by turning their research problems into environments where agents can learn. This means closing the loop from hypothesis to experiment to validated result, with agents learning from each cycle. Teams will be able to own their intelligence, using tools previously available only to frontier labs, and point it at the questions they care about most, especially those that others might not be asking.

I've had the good fortune of seeing how science operates across academia, industry, government, startups, and venture. I worked on experimental therapeutics for cancer in academia before moving to the National Institutes of Health to work on DNA damage and repair. I cofounded Molecule, where we funded dozens of research projects to speed the translation of early-stage therapeutics to market, focusing on areas traditionally ignored by pharma. Most recently, I started Triplicate, a small fund backing teams and tools accelerating scientific research. Many of the problems I care about most are increasingly soluble with advances in AI, and I hope to bring what I've learned about the bottlenecks in translating research to radically accelerate science in all fields.

I share Alexander Grothendieck's ethos of discovery and believe Prime does too: "Discovery is a child's privilege. I mean the small child, the child who is not afraid to be wrong, to look silly, to not be serious, and to act differently from everyone else."

The goal of progress is not more intelligence for its own sake. In my view, it is to better understand reality, and, in doing so, give more people, and more kinds of minds, the chance to flourish.

If you have a research problem where today's tools fall short, my DMs are open. If our approach resonates and you want to build this with us, we're hiring!

text:
Impressive. This set of talks, along with the new America dot gov website, has the unmistakable feel of an Apple launch event. They're rebooting the federal government as a tech startup. Several observations.

(1) First, with this new AI interface to the entire federal government, if it works as promised, there won't be a single American who can't say their life wasn't helped at least in part by AI, or that the benefits accrued solely to zillionaires. This in itself cannily mitigates anti-datacenter sentiment.

(2) Second, Joe Gebbia and Marco Rubio's talks on simplifying name changes and passport filings introduce a completely new era where the US government is actually launching tangible features that benefit users.

(3) Third, this launch event in and of itself may visibly drive reform. It could become much more important than the State of the Union. Unlike laws, code is user-visible, and can be instantly audited by the public, as Obama found out with the failed obamacare website launch. So: the annual America dot gov event may be substance, whereas SOTU is traditionally optics. I wouldn't be surprised to see the President present at the next one.

(4) Fourth, this kind of event is a perfect example of where tech and red cooperate best. They both hate bureaucracy. Automating paperwork with code reduces the power of statists over both capitalists and nationalists. It's also hard to undo by other admins: once you digitize a process, hard to turn it back to paper.

(5) Fifth, it's an obvious point perhaps, but think about how much influence YCombinator has had in 20 years. From Gebbia's Airbnb joining their 2009 batch to a complete overhaul of the user interface of the US bureaucracy, and thus the US government.

(6) Sixth, this is another take on the network state. The functional part of the US (the network, meaning tech) is merging with and partially reforming the dysfunctional part (the state, meaning bureaucracy) by automating 20th century paper forms.

As a tech startup, there will no doubt be bugs and user issues and so on, but unlike with paper laws those issues will be visible and the code fixes will be verifiable. A new era of AI America. Rooting for them.

quoted_text:
An LLM reads every order. A human signs every trade.

I built 𝐀𝐑𝐄𝐍𝐀 𝟔𝟕 with @Knowledge_JO for the @openservai SERV Reasoning hackathon.

A chat-first trading agent for Robinhood Chain. You type what you want to trade, SERV handles the research and reasoning behind it, and one confirm gate is the only path money can move.

We run it live against Robinhood Chain mainnet (chain 4663), with custodial wallets and every new account starting on a paper sandbox.

How a trade gets made:

> SERV reads your intent, searches the token, prices the amount, picks the pool, then re-prices one last time before you confirm. It never signs.

> A research rail keeps the context fresh: trending, new-tokens, holder overlap, transfer folds, and per-token reports straight off the live chain.

> The confirm gate takes the final quote, checks the session and the caps, and executes through the Uniswap Universal Router with a desk-held signer whose keys are encrypted at rest.

Then we tried to break it.

> Double-confirmed the same intent: the claim is idempotent, so it returned the same receipt and fired 0 extra swaps.

> Injected a pool address straight into the confirm body: rejected. Quote ids are opaque and bound to the session that created them.

Sent a confirm from a second session: 401. The intent store only answers its owning session.

Pushed the trade past the cap: refused. MAX_TRADE_USD and MAX_SLIPPAGE_BPS hold even after the model has already produced its intent.

113 tests across 12 suites keep the gate honest.

Each sponsor powers one job in the desk:

@openservai - the reasoning layer: intent, pricing, requotes, and a refusal to sign.
@RobinhoodCrypto - the rails: mainnet settlement through the Universal Router.
@neondatabase - the state: accounts, the sandbox ledger, conversations, and migrations on boot.

One desk, three distinct jobs.

🔍 I looked into how @API3DAO curates lending vaults on Morpho.

And it’s more than just picking assets and putting liquidity behind them.

API3 handles the important risk layer:

→ Market selection — deciding which lending markets qualify
→ Risk parameters — setting limits around exposure
→ Capital allocation — directing liquidity where it can be used
→ Price feeds — reliable data for collateral, borrowing and liquidations
→ Ongoing risk management — keeping vault exposure controlled as markets change

What caught my attention is the memecoin side.

Through @purintaxyz , API3 is applying this curation model to assets like $PEPE and $SPX , where volatility and liquidity make risk management even more important.

The idea is simple:

Don’t just make an asset borrowable.
Build the risk framework around it.

That’s what I understood from API3’s curation approach on Morpho — the curator is effectively responsible for deciding where capital goes and under what conditions.

Pretty interesting infrastructure layer hiding behind the vault UI. 👀

quoted_text:
Five and a half years ago, @crispheaney, @bigz_pubkey, @davijlu and I set out on a weird, winding, and wonderful journey to build a perpetual futures exchange. The crypto market structure was extremely immature then. Perps were just starting out, most DeFi users were paying $200 to execute a single transaction on Ethereum. We were one of the first to bring a fully on-chain perpetual DEX to market and launched for the first time on Solana in November 2021.

Today, as the exchange relaunches and enters its next chapter, I'm stepping down from Drift, now @VelocityDEX.

I'm extremely proud of what we built – one of the largest exchanges on Solana with over $150B traded. Chris and Z, our technical cofounders, led the technology front to build every piece of the exchange stack, while David and I put together an incredible and experienced growth and operational team. I poured my heart, soul, and many years of the most insane ups and downs into building and growing Drift – a gruelling, but immensely fulfilling journey. In many ways, it felt like my first child.

This April, we faced a state-level attack by DPRK, after a long-planned six months of social engineering infiltration. Going through it and the aftermath was by far the worst week of my life.

Within ten sleepless nights, we closed a deal with Tether that put users on a path to recovery. We hired @redacted_noah, ex-head of protocol engineering at Helium, to lead the rebuild of Velocity’s smart contract technology, a difficult task he took on enthusiastically and with zest. We brought on @namanmtl, who joins us from Binance and Trust Wallet to lead Growth and Recovery to grow our trader base for the relaunch. I am proud of my team who stepped up to take initiative above and beyond – especially @tracybbd who personally took the pains to speak to every single trader and market maker on the exchange.

Over the next few months, the team refused to quit and hunkered down to rebuild the exchange with a full security upgrade. Designing DFX as well as coordinating on multi-nation asset recovery working alongside @zeroShadow_io and local law enforcement agencies to freeze assets was a huge feat. This week, Velocity finalized their audit by @osec_io and @asymmetric_re and fully open-sourced the exchange. After a long and arduous journey, with many security audits in tow and with massive effort from the team, the exchange relaunches today – even better and faster than before.

I would like to shout out the incredible team that will be carrying on the Velocity product. @davijlu, along with Foundation, will continue to move on the asset recovery and law enforcement work. @redacted_noah will continue to build out Velocity’s technology, shipping new features like CLOB and Prop AMM that will make the product even better and smoother. @Defioppa, who previously led product at Binance, will continue to lead the product at Velocity. @tracybbd will lead partnerships and stakeholder relationships. @namanmtl will join us from his extensive background at Binance to lead growth.

With a heavy heart, I fully own this decision to step down. I have always done my best work building from zero to one. Velocity is now at the stage where it needs operators who can take it from one to ten, and I trust this team to take it to the next level. It is the right decision for me and for the protocol, to open a new chapter for Velocity.

I've been all in on crypto, my whole career since I was 19. Now I will be spending energy on exploring what’s next for me personally. I care about building bridges between Asia and the US, between digital and physical infrastructure, and about bringing what I've learned home to my local community in Southeast Asia. I will actively continue to champion Velocity, and the founders and teams I’m backing.

To our users and partners: thank you so much for the trust. I know the Velocity team is genuinely giving the relaunch all they have. To our investors: thank you for all your guidance and support all these years. To our team: thank you for everything. I couldn't have imagined doing this with anyone else.

text:
Some personal news: I'm joining @PrimeIntellect as Head of Scientific AI!

A billion copies of the same very smart, agreeable mind will not be a scientifically fruitful world.

Scientific superintelligence should be weird and definitionally nonconsensus. It should be highly plural, consisting of many minds, human and artificial, that see the world differently and hold each other accountable, with human judgement still playing the central role in setting the trajectory.

Science is about asking the right questions and reducing uncertainty. Professionalizing science made discovery a viable career, but it also introduced incentives to work on what is fundable and publishable. Neither is the same thing as being true or impactful (reward hacking exists in the real world too!). We are very good at accumulating incremental knowledge and rather bad at stewarding unorthodox ideas through infancy, even though these are often the ideas that open entirely new fields of inquiry.

If we aren't careful, scientific AI could reproduce these same incentives at a much larger scale. If everyone relies on the same few large models, we risk inheriting the same priors and blind spots.

Open tools let us shape our own intelligence and take it in directions a frontier lab might never prioritize. This matters for scientific freedom and is central to Prime’s vision.

If you are a scientist, staying at the frontier will mean training your own models on your own research and data. I'll work closely with scientific teams across domains to help them build scientific agents by turning their research problems into environments where agents can learn. This means closing the loop from hypothesis to experiment to validated result, with agents learning from each cycle. Teams will be able to own their intelligence, using tools previously available only to frontier labs, and point it at the questions they care about most, especially those that others might not be asking.

I've had the good fortune of seeing how science operates across academia, industry, government, startups, and venture. I worked on experimental therapeutics for cancer in academia before moving to the National Institutes of Health to work on DNA damage and repair. I cofounded Molecule, where we funded dozens of research projects to speed the translation of early-stage therapeutics to market, focusing on areas traditionally ignored by pharma. Most recently, I started Triplicate, a small fund backing teams and tools accelerating scientific research. Many of the problems I care about most are increasingly soluble with advances in AI, and I hope to bring what I've learned about the bottlenecks in translating research to radically accelerate science in all fields.

I share Alexander Grothendieck's ethos of discovery and believe Prime does too: "Discovery is a child's privilege. I mean the small child, the child who is not afraid to be wrong, to look silly, to not be serious, and to act differently from everyone else."

The goal of progress is not more intelligence for its own sake. In my view, it is to better understand reality, and, in doing so, give more people, and more kinds of minds, the chance to flourish.

If you have a research problem where today's tools fall short, my DMs are open. If our approach resonates and you want to build this with us, we're hiring!

Stocks like $OKTA $P $CDNA keep making 52 week highs in a market that's almost making ATH, but I'm reducing instead of adding today. 

Here's why: the major indexes are near all-time highs, and on the surface the market appears to be moving into a confirmed uptrend. The underlying evidence is far less convincing.

1. No follow-through day. What's missing is a strong follow-through day with a gain of 1% or more on large volume, with broad participation and plenty of individual stocks breaking out and holding. Without it, we view the action with suspicion.

2. Market breadth is unbelievably weak. Today's numbers say the same thing:

Advancers vs. decliners: 1,172 to 1828 (39.1%)
New lows vs. new highs: 138 to 23
Stocks up 4%+ vs. stocks down 4%+: 20 to 85
Up on volume vs. Down on volume: 313 to 615

Only 24.5% of stocks are above their 21-day moving average and 35% above their 50-day moving average

3. The macro environment also adds headwinds. The 30-year Treasury yield is about 5.3%, near the top of its five-year range, offering a yield that is real competition for capital against equities.

Individual stocks are the deciding factor. If a large number of quality names begin to break out together, we participate. If not, we stay defensive. Right now the stock-level evidence is also mixed and doesn't justify aggressive exposure.

Assistant Benchmark creator David Pawlan sits down with a16z's Anish Acharya to unpack the sudden explosion of personal AI agents and what it will take for one to become part of everyday life.

David has been testing dozens of assistants across real-world tasks, from managing email and booking travel to handling financial admin. They discuss why the most useful agents may become increasingly invisible, proactively checking you into flights, finding refunds, filing reimbursements, or simply handling the small tasks that pile up across everyday life.

They also explore whether the winning interface is an app, text thread, voice, or wearable; how much autonomy consumers will actually give their agents; and what happens when agents start interacting with other agents. From commerce and restaurant reservations to entirely new agent-native services, Anish and David ask what the internet looks like when software starts acting on our behalf.

text:
Hyperliquid’s path into the U.S.

I think the U.S. path is becoming more concrete. There are two separate pieces.

1. HYPE’s case for non-security treatment

• Token rights: No company ownership, debt repayment or contractual profit rights.

• Utility: HyperEVM gas, validator staking and HIP-3 market deployment.

• Source of value: Trading fees fund HYPE buybacks and burns. SEC staff’s buyback guidance assumes a non-security token on a functional network without a central party.

• Promises: The case strengthens when value comes from network use and supply and demand, without reliance on unfulfilled team promises of returns. S3 silence could preserve flexibility for retrospective rewards under SEC conditions. That remains speculation.

• Control: Operational, economic and voting control matter, including coordinated groups. Another airdrop could help if meaningful power reaches independent users and builders.

2. Regulated U.S. perps

Trump said in August that CFTC Chairman Michael Selig was working to bring Hyperliquid into the U.S. legally.

Payward, Kraken’s parent, proposes new permissioned HIP-3* markets:

• Hyperliquid: Blockchain and order book.

• Bitnomial Exchange: Market administration.

• Bitnomial Clearinghouse: Clearing and settlement.

• NinjaTrader Clearing: Customer onboarding and accounts.

Only approved customers could trade, with regulated firms carrying the compliance obligations. Listings remain subject to regulatory approval.

On September 24, CFTC staff also clarified that compliant onchain records need not have duplicate offchain copies. Firms must still retain and produce records during network disruptions.

That is the opportunity: strengthening HYPE’s case for non-security treatment and developing a regulated path for U.S. perps on Hyperliquid’s public infrastructure.

author: KuiGas
quoted_text:
明天 HOOD Summit 就要开始了，受 @0xminion 老师的启发，简单聊聊我对 Robinhood 上的两个 Launchpad @longdotxyz 和 @ponsdotfamily 的一些粗浅见解。

先说结论：流动性才是 Launchpad 最大的护城河，更深的流动性会让 bundling/控盘变贵，也意味着这些拥有深度流动性的资产更能扛极端波动。Launchpad 下一阶段的竞争，是谁能把原本属于 MEV/套利/做市/细分板块的流动性留住，并把它们变成自身不可复制的资产。LONG 和 PONS 正在采用两种完全不同的方式来致力于做到这一点。

LONG：内化模型，流动性收在自己的产品体系里

1）Fee 转化成池子里的卖墙（Sell Wall/Floor）和金库里的股票

普通 Launchpad 的 Fee 一般是进创作者钱包或拿来做平台币回购，后续的池子里的交易基本就跟这笔钱没关系了。LONG 则把同一笔成交所产生的 Fee 拆分进入两个不同的容器——池子和金库。

池子是干活的库存。 robinhood:0x2e8c31162b855a2ffa90f6f8634643ad6f111e18 /NVDA 这种币股配对盘，买 meme 就是在往池子里塞股票；股票再涨，同一数量 token 能换到的美元也会跟着变厚。

更关键的是手续费侧的更新。LONG 上线初期创作者拿的 Fee 约 1%，币和股票两边都能领，带来的一个缺陷是热门盘容易变成开发者砸盘的单点故障。7 月 26–27 日起，之后新发的配对盘改了默认的 Fee 结构：大约是成交额的 0.1% 量级给创作者、一部分 v4 Hook 会在卖出时买回（手动销毁，计划自动化）、更大的一部分直接锁进 LP。此前，官方还试过贴着现价的 NVDA 加卖墙，现价下方 10–20% 的可吃深度明显变厚，另外还计划把 v4 LP NFT 转进不可变合约。

金库是不干活的储备。Community Vault 把费用里的股票侧费用打到独立地址，不参与换汇，暴跌时不会因为有人卖 meme 就被抽走；meme 那一侧则锁一部分、烧一部分。池子负责让砸盘变贵，金库负责留一笔不跟盘口一起变动的 NVDA/一篮子股票。

这部分的「费用内化」不是让钱进 LONG 公司账户，而是让这个市场自己的地板和社区名下的股票储备随成交变厚。

2）板块职能由自家产品矩阵顶上

除了 robinhood:0x2e8c31162b855a2ffa90f6f8634643ad6f111e18/NVDA、 $MOO/MU 这种常规币股配对盘，指数仓、LongX 3x 杠杆包装等都是 LONG 的产品矩阵，叙事独立、社区独立，但报价资产、复利路径、费用入口都在同一套产品面上。新盘还可以给旗舰金库送股票腿（LONG 500：新股票配对盘的股票费用里切一部分进 robinhood:0x2e8c31162b855a2ffa90f6f8634643ad6f111e18 金库，另切一部分买回销毁新币，LP 复利继续转）。

3）No vamp

复制一个 Bonding Curve 很容易，但复制「已经锁在现价附近的那批 NVDA + 成为这个股票的链上默认盘口」却很难。官方如果再发一个更低费率的工厂吸自己，等于拆自己的库存和路由权。利益绑在一起，就没有动力对自己生态抽血。

PONS：外化模型，专注发行 + 流量入口，职能下放垂直团队

1）只做最大的那一层：发行机器 + 订单流

Pons 已经证明流量入口可以做到很大：链上最大的发行机器之一，单日费用规模一度达到 $6M 以上级别，远超同期市场上的其他 Launchpad。价值捕获路径极垂直：1% Hook 费 → 70% 创作者 / 30% 协议 → 协议份里约 80% 用于回购销毁 robinhood:0x39dbed3a2bd333467115de45665cc57f813c4571 。

下一步如果把做市、Hook 设计、AI 管盘、推理资本、跨股票路由全做进官方产品，会变成和每个垂直团队抢叙事、抢 Token。因此，将这些职能外置才是最理性的：Pons 自己作为发行底层继续收租，垂直板块让已经跑出来的生态伙伴基于自己的发行底层在做一层。

2）生态垂直团队充当独立事业部

基于上一点的分析，Pons 生态中其实已经有好几个垂直团队可以充当他的职能臂，且每一个都能对上一个已经在 Pons 上跑且有自己 Token 的模块：

v4 hook 规则市场（防狙击、动态费、arb recapture）→ @Hookrfun $HOOKR
AI swarm 锁 bundle、双边做市 → @Moshdottrade $BUN
跨股票 LP、吃波动和错价 → @shroom_network  $SHROOM
Agent 发行 + 可交易推理额度 → @orbiodotso $ORBIO

职能臂都是独立协议，自己管理自己的金库、销毁、用户和估值叙事逻辑，它们可以各自都长到 100M 以上级别，但不会稀释 Pons 的估值叙事逻辑。Pons 只负责提供槽位和成交，不把它们收成官方产品线。

最终谁会胜出？

按照 @0xminion 老师的说法，两个平台两种模型应该是 Both win，逻辑在于：

内化赢在资产负债表。

LONG 把股票深度、金库、板块币、杠杆包装做成同一套账，复制成本随平台 TVL 的上升而上升。

缺点是：所有创新都要自己做，速度慢；没有明确的平台币，二级市场很难按照发行机器 + 链上股票流动性中枢的叙事逻辑给 LONG 单独定价。这里额外多说一句个人的看法，LONG 大概率是不会发行平台币了， robinhood:0x2e8c31162b855a2ffa90f6f8634643ad6f111e18 就是平台币的角色，这个角度也需要一些时间让市场达成充分共识，一旦市场反应过来了， robinhood:0x2e8c31162b855a2ffa90f6f8634643ad6f111e18 应该也很难像现在这么便宜了。

外化赢在分工和估值切分。

Pons 继续做最大流量入口， robinhood:0x39dbed3a2bd333467115de45665cc57f813c4571 吃总闸门费用；Hook/AI 做市/推理资本市场/跨票路由各自有独立股权故事。

缺点是：伙伴做大了可以换入口，比如 Mosh 自己说过他们的机制能挂在任何 Launchpad 上；协调成本高；Pons 官方一旦自研同类 Hook，就是对伙伴的隐性 Vamp。

所以最终谁会胜出，相信大家自己心里都有答案。最后强烈推荐大家关注 @0xminion 老师，总是走在最前沿的高认知研究员 & Trader，每次看他的推文都受益良多，以上很多内容都是我看他的推文受到的启发，然后结合自己的理解写的，如果有理解不对/不足之处，欢迎老师们多多指教。
